children.text: Chapter 1
dharmaikatānāḥ puruṣā yadāsan satyavādinaḥ
children.translated_text: When men were wholly devoted to <s>dharma</s> (normative order) and spoke truth,

children.text: tadā na vyavahāro 'bhūn na dveṣo nāpi matsaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: then no <s>vyavahāra</s> (legal procedure) existed, nor hatred, nor envy.

children.text: naṣṭe dharme manuṣyeṣu vyavahāraḥ pravartate
children.translated_text: When dharma has been lost among human beings, legal procedure comes into operation,

children.text: draṣṭā ca vyavahārāṇāṃ rājā daṇḍadharaḥ kṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and the king, bearer of punishment, was appointed as observer of legal proceedings.

children.text: likhitaṃ sākṣiṇaś cātra dvau vidhī saṃprakīrtitau
children.translated_text: Here written documents and witnesses are proclaimed as the two procedures

children.text: saṃdigdhārthaviśuddhyarthaṃ dvayor vivadamānayoḥ ||
children.translated_text: for clearing up a doubtful matter between two litigants.

children.text: sottaro 'nuttaraś caiva sa vijñeyo dvilakṣaṇaḥ
children.translated_text: It should be known as having two forms: with an answer and without an answer;

children.text: sottaro 'bhyadhiko yatra vilekhāpūrvakaḥ paṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: where the stake, preceded by a written statement, is increased, that is with an answer.

children.text: vivāde sottarapaṇe dvayor yas tatra hīyate
children.translated_text: In a dispute with a counter-stake, whichever of the two is defeated there,

children.text: sa paṇaṃ svakṛtaṃ dāpyo vinayaṃ ca parājaye ||
children.translated_text: he should be made to pay the stake he himself set, and also a fine on defeat.

children.text: sāras tu vyavahārāṇāṃ pratijñā samudāhṛtā
children.translated_text: The essence of legal proceedings is declared to be the claim,

children.text: taddhānau hīyate vādī taraṃs tām uttaro bhavet ||
children.translated_text: when it fails, the plaintiff is defeated; when it overcomes that, the reply becomes stronger.

children.text: kulāni śreṇayaś caiva gaṇāś cādhikṛto nṛpaḥ
children.translated_text: Families, guilds, corporate groups, and the authorized king

children.text: pratiṣṭhā vyavahārāṇāṃ gurvebhyas tūttarottaram ||
children.translated_text: are the foundations of legal proceedings, each later one weightier than the earlier.

children.text: sa catuṣpāc catuḥsthānaś catuḥsādhana eva ca
children.translated_text: This is said to have four feet, four seats, and four means,

children.text: caturhitaś caturvyāpī catuṣkārī ca kīrtyate ||
children.translated_text: to benefit four, pervade four, and produce four results.

children.text: aṣṭāṅgo 'ṣṭādaśapadaḥ śataśākhas tathaiva ca
children.translated_text: It has eight limbs and eighteen titles, and likewise a hundred branches;

children.text: triyonir dvyabhiyogaś ca dvidvāro dvigatis tathā ||
children.translated_text: it has three sources, two accusations, two gates, and two courses.

children.text: dharmaś ca vyavahāraś ca caritraṃ rājaśāsanam
children.translated_text: Dharma, legal procedure, custom, and royal command

children.text: catuṣpād vyavahāro 'yam uttaraḥ pūrvabādhakaḥ ||
children.translated_text: are the four feet of this legal process; the later overrides the earlier.

children.text: tatra satye sthito dharmo vyavahāras tu sākṣiṣu
children.translated_text: In that, dharma rests on truth, while legal procedure rests on witnesses;

children.text: caritraṃ pustakaraṇe rājājñāyāṃ tu śāsanam ||
children.translated_text: custom rests on documentary record, and rule rests on the king's command.

children.text: sāmādyupāyasādhyatvāc catuḥsādhana ucyate
children.translated_text: Because it can be effected by the means beginning with conciliation, it is called four-means,

children.text: caturṇām āśramāṇāṃ ca rakṣaṇāt sa caturhitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and because it protects the four āśramas (life-stages), it is beneficial to four.

children.text: kartṝn atho sākṣiṇaś ca sabhyān rājānam eva ca
children.translated_text: Because it extends, foot by foot, to the parties, the witnesses, the assessors,

children.text: vyāpnoti pādaśo yasmāc caturvyāpī tataḥ smṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and the king himself, therefore it is remembered as pervading four.

children.text: dharmasyārthasya yaśaso lokapaktes tathaiva ca
children.translated_text: Because it brings about dharma, wealth, fame,

children.text: caturṇāṃ karaṇād eṣāṃ catuṣkārī prakīrtitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and approval in the world, these four, it is proclaimed as producing four.

children.text: rājā sapuruṣaḥ sabhyāḥ śāstraṃ gaṇakalekhakau
children.translated_text: The king with his officers, the assessors, the śāstra, the accountant and the scribe,

children.text: hiraṇyam agnir udakam aṣṭāṅgaḥ sa udāhṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: gold, fire, and water: this is declared to be eight-limbed.

children.text: ṛṇādānaṃ hy upanidhiḥ sambhūyotthānam eva ca
children.translated_text: Non-payment of debt, deposit, and undertaking in partnership,

children.text: dattasya punar ādānam aśuśrūṣābhyupetya ca ||
children.translated_text: resumption of what has been given, and failure to perform service after agreeing to it,

children.text: vetanasyānapākarma tathaivāsvāmivikrayaḥ
children.translated_text: non-payment of wages, and likewise sale by one who is not the owner,

children.text: vikrīyāsaṃpradānaṃ ca krītvānuśaya eva ca ||
children.translated_text: non-delivery after sale, and regret after purchase,

children.text: samayasyānapākarma vivādaḥ kṣetrajas tathā
children.translated_text: breach of agreement, and likewise a dispute arising from a field,

children.text: strīpuṃsayoś ca saṃbandho dāyabhāgo 'tha sāhasam ||
children.translated_text: the relation between woman and man, division of inheritance, and violence,

children.text: vākpāruṣyaṃ tathaivoktaṃ daṇḍapāruṣyam eva ca
children.translated_text: verbal abuse, and likewise physical assault,

children.text: dyūtaṃ prakīrṇakaṃ caivety aṣṭādaśapadaḥ smṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: gambling and miscellaneous matters: these are remembered as the eighteen titles.

children.text: eṣām eva prabhedo 'nyaḥ śatam aṣṭottaraṃ smṛtam
children.translated_text: A further subdivision of these same matters is remembered as one hundred and eight;

children.text: kriyābhedān manuṣyāṇāṃ śataśākho nigadyate ||
children.translated_text: because of the varieties of human actions, it is called hundred-branched.

children.text: kāmāt krodhāc ca lobhāc ca tribhyo yasmāt pravartate
children.translated_text: Because it arises from the three: desire, anger, and greed,

children.text: triyoniḥ kīrtyate tena trayam etad vivādakṛt ||
children.translated_text: therefore it is called three-sourced; this triad produces disputes.

children.text: dvyabhiyogas tu vijñeyaḥ śaṅkātattvābhiyogataḥ
children.translated_text: An accusation should be understood as twofold: accusation from suspicion and accusation from fact.

children.text: śaṅkāsatāṃ tu saṃsargāt tattvaṃ hoḍhādidarśanāt ||
children.translated_text: Suspicion arises from association with bad people; fact arises from seeing stolen goods and the like.

children.text: pakṣadvayābhisaṃbandhād dvidvāraḥ samudāhṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: Because it is connected with the two sides, it is declared to have two gates.

children.text: pūrvavādas tayoḥ pakṣaḥ pratipakṣas taduttaram ||
children.translated_text: Of those two, the initial plea is the claim, and its answer is the counterclaim.

children.text: bhūtacchalānusāritvād dvigatiḥ sa udāhṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: Because it follows truth and trickery, it is declared to have two courses.

children.text: bhūtaṃ tattvārthasaṃyuktaṃ pramādābhihitaṃ chalam ||
children.translated_text: Truth is joined with the real meaning; trickery is what is stated through error.

children.text: tatra śiṣṭaṃ chalaṃ rājā marṣayed dharmasādhanaḥ
children.translated_text: There the king, seeking to establish dharma, should tolerate an inadvertent technical misstatement,

children.text: bhūtam eva prapadyeta dharmamūlā yataḥ śriyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: but should resort to the truth alone, since prosperities are rooted in dharma.

children.text: dharmeṇoddharato rājño vyavahārān kṛtātmanaḥ
children.translated_text: For a self-controlled king who settles legal proceedings by dharma,

children.text: sambhavanti guṇāḥ sapta sapta vahner ivārciṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: seven virtues arise, like the seven flames of fire.

children.text: dharmaś cārthaś ca kīrtiś ca lokapaktir upagrahaḥ
children.translated_text: Dharma, wealth, fame, approval in the world, support,

children.text: prajābhyo bahumānaś ca svarge sthānaṃ ca śāśvatam ||
children.translated_text: honor from the subjects, and an eternal place in heaven are those seven.

children.text: tasmād dharmāsanaṃ prāpya rājā vigatamatsaraḥ
children.translated_text: Therefore, having reached the seat of dharma, a king free from envy

children.text: samaḥ syāt sarvabhūteṣu bibhrad vaivasvataṃ vratam ||
children.translated_text: should be impartial toward all beings, bearing the vow of <s>Vaivasvata</s>.

children.text: dharmaśāstraṃ puraskṛtya prāḍvivākamate sthitaḥ
children.translated_text: Placing the dharmaśāstra before him and relying on the opinion of the chief judge,

children.text: samāhitamatiḥ paśyed vyavahārān anukramāt ||
children.translated_text: with concentrated mind he should examine legal proceedings in order.

children.text: āgamaḥ prathamaṃ kāryo vyavahārapadaṃ tataḥ
children.translated_text: First the presentation is to be made, then the title of litigation,

children.text: vivitsā nirṇayaś caiva darśanaṃ syāc caturvidham ||
children.translated_text: then inquiry and decision: examination is fourfold.

children.text: dharmaśāstrārthaśāstrābhyām avirodhena mārgataḥ
children.translated_text: Without conflict with dharmaśāstra and arthaśāstra, along the proper path,

children.text: samīkṣamāṇo nipuṇaṃ vyavahāragatiṃ nayet ||
children.translated_text: examining carefully, he should guide the course of legal procedure.

children.text: yathā mṛgasya viddhasya vyādho mṛgapadaṃ nayet
children.translated_text: Just as a hunter tracks the trail of a wounded deer

children.text: kakṣe śoṇitaleśena tathā dharmapadaṃ nayet ||
children.translated_text: by a speck of blood in the thicket, so should he trace the path of dharma.

children.text: yatra vipratipattiḥ syād dharmaśāstrārthaśāstrayoḥ
children.translated_text: Where there is disagreement between dharmaśāstra and arthaśāstra,

children.text: arthaśāstroktam utsṛjya dharmaśāstroktam ācaret ||
children.translated_text: one should abandon what is stated in arthaśāstra and follow what is stated in dharmaśāstra.

children.text: dharmaśāstravirodhe tu yuktiyukto 'pi dharmataḥ
children.translated_text: But when there is conflict with dharmaśāstra, even what is supported by reasoning on grounds of dharma

children.text: vyavahāro hi balavān dharmas tenāvahīyate ||
children.translated_text: is overborne, for legal procedure is powerful; by it dharma is set aside.

children.text: sūkṣmo hi bhagavān dharmaḥ parokṣo durvicāraṇaḥ
children.translated_text: For revered dharma is subtle, unseen, and hard to discern;

children.text: ataḥ pratyakṣamārgeṇa vyavahāragatiṃ nayet ||
children.translated_text: therefore one should guide the course of legal procedure by a directly perceptible path.

children.text: yāty acauro 'pi cauratvaṃ cauraś cāyāty acauratām
children.translated_text: Even a non-thief may come to thiefhood, and a thief may come to non-thiefhood;

children.text: acauraś cauratāṃ prāpto māṇḍavyo vyavahārataḥ ||
children.translated_text: through legal procedure <s>Māṇḍavya</s>, though not a thief, came to be treated as a thief.

children.text: strīṣu rātrau bahir grāmād antarveśmany arātiṣu
children.translated_text: In matters involving women, at night, outside the village, inside the house, or among enemies,

children.text: vyavahāraḥ kṛto 'py eṣu punaḥ kartavyatām iyāt ||
children.translated_text: a legal proceeding, even if performed in these cases, may have to be performed again,

children.text: gahanatvād vivādānām asāmarthyāt smṛter api
children.translated_text: because disputes are difficult and even memory may be insufficient.

children.text: ṛṇādiṣu haret kālaṃ kāmaṃ tattvabubhutsayā ||
children.translated_text: In matters such as debts, he may take time as he wishes, from a desire to know the truth.

children.text: gobhūhiraṇyastrīsteyapāruṣyātyayikeṣu ca
children.translated_text: But in cases concerning cattle, land, gold, women, theft, abuse or assault, and urgent danger,

children.text: sāhaseṣv abhiśāpe ca sadya eva vivādayet ||
children.translated_text: and in acts of violence and formal denunciation, he should make the parties litigate at once.

children.text: anāvedya tu yo rājñe saṃdigdhe 'rthe pravartate
children.translated_text: But one who proceeds in a doubtful matter without notifying the king

children.text: prasahya sa vineyaḥ syāt sa cāsyārtho na sidhyati ||
children.translated_text: should be punished for acting forcibly, and that claim of his does not succeed.

children.text: vaktavye 'rthe na tiṣṭhantam utkrāmantaṃ ca tadvacaḥ
children.translated_text: When a man does not stand by the matter to be stated and departs from his own statement,

children.text: āsedhayed vivādārthī yāvad āhvānadarśanam ||
children.translated_text: the litigating claimant should put him under <s>āsedha</s> (restraint) until he appears in response to the summons.

children.text: sthānāsedhaḥ kālakṛtaḥ pravāsāt karmaṇas tathā
children.translated_text: <s>Āsedha</s> is fourfold: restraint by place, restraint made by time, restraint from travel,

children.text: caturvidhaḥ syād āsedho nāsiddhas taṃ vilaṅghayet ||
children.translated_text: and restraint from work; the person under restraint must not overstep it.

children.text: nadīsaṃtārakāntāradurdeśopaplavādiṣu
children.translated_text: In cases of river crossings, wilderness, difficult country, disturbances, and the like,

children.text: āsiddhas taṃ parāsedham utkrāman nāparādhnuyāt ||
children.translated_text: a restrained person does no wrong if he oversteps that outside restraint.

children.text: āsedhakāla āsiddha āsedham yo vyatikramet
children.translated_text: If a restrained person transgresses the restraint during the time of restraint,

children.text: sa vineyo 'nyathā kurvann āseddhā daṇḍabhāg bhavet ||
children.translated_text: he should be fined; but if the restrainer acts otherwise, he becomes liable to punishment.

children.text: nirveṣṭukāmo rogārto yiyakṣur vyasane sthitaḥ
children.translated_text: One wishing to discharge an obligation, one afflicted by illness, one about to sacrifice, one caught in calamity,

children.text: abhiyuktas tathānyena rājakāryodyatas tathā ||
children.translated_text: one who has also been accused by another, and one engaged in the king's business,

children.text: gavāṃ pracāre gopālāḥ sasyabandhe kṛṣīvalāḥ
children.translated_text: cowherds while the cattle are grazing, farmers while the crops are being secured,

children.text: śilpinaḥ cāpi tatkālam āyudhīyāś ca vigrahe ||
children.translated_text: artisans at that time, and armed men during battle,

children.text: aprāptavyavahāraś ca dūto dānonmukho vratī
children.translated_text: one not competent for litigation, a messenger, one intent on making a gift, a man under a vow,

children.text: viṣamasthaś ca nāsedhyo na cainān āhvayen nṛpaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and one in a dangerous position are not to be restrained, nor should the king summon them.

children.text: nābhiyukto 'bhiyuñjīta tam atīrtvārtham anyataḥ
children.translated_text: A defendant should not bring a charge against another before he has got through that matter,

children.text: na cābhiyuktam anyena na viddhaṃ veddhum arhati ||
children.translated_text: nor against one already accused by another; one already struck by a charge should not be struck again.

children.text: yam artham abhiyuñjīta na taṃ viprakṛtiṃ nayet
children.translated_text: He should not alter the matter for which he brings a charge,

children.text: nānyat pakṣāntaraṃ gacched gacchan pūrvāt sa hīyate ||
children.translated_text: nor should he go over to another side of the case; if he does so, he loses from the former position.

children.text: na ca mithyābhiyuñjīta doṣo mithyābhiyoginaḥ
children.translated_text: He should not bring a false charge; there is a fault in the false accuser.

children.text: yas tatra vinayaḥ proktaḥ so 'bhiyoktāram āvrajet ||
children.translated_text: Whatever penalty is prescribed in that matter should fall upon the accuser.

children.text: sāpadeśaṃ haran kālam abruvaṃś cāpi saṃsadi
children.translated_text: Taking time with pretexts and not speaking in the assembly,

children.text: uktvā vaco vibruvaṃś ca hīyamānasya lakṣaṇam ||
children.translated_text: and, after making a statement, speaking against it: these are the signs of a man who is losing.

children.text: palāyate ya āhūtaḥ prāptaś ca vivaden na yaḥ
children.translated_text: One who flees after being summoned, or who, though present, does not litigate,

children.text: vineyaḥ sa bhaved rājñā hīna eva sa vādataḥ ||
children.translated_text: should be fined by the king, and he is defeated in the suit.

children.text: nirṇiktavyavahāreṣu pramāṇam aphalaṃ bhavet
children.translated_text: In suits already settled, proof becomes fruitless,

children.text: likhitaṃ sākṣiṇo vāpi pūrvam āveditaṃ na cet ||
children.translated_text: whether written document or witnesses, if it was not announced beforehand.

children.text: yathā pakveṣu dhānyeṣu niṣphalāḥ prāvṛṣo guṇāḥ
children.translated_text: As the virtues of the rains are fruitless when the grain is already ripe,

children.text: nirṇiktavyavahārāṇāṃ pramāṇam aphalaṃ tathā ||
children.translated_text: so proof is fruitless in suits that have already been settled.

children.text: abhūtam apy abhihitaṃ prāptakālaṃ parīkṣyate
children.translated_text: Even something unreal, if stated at the proper time, is examined,

children.text: yat tu pramādān nocyeta tad bhūtam api hīyate ||
children.translated_text: but what is not stated through negligence is lost, even if it is real.

children.text: tīritaṃ cānuśiṣṭaṃ ca yo manyeta vidharmataḥ
children.translated_text: If someone thinks that a matter decided and instructed has been contrary to <s>dharma</s> (lawful order),

children.text: dviguṇaṃ daṇḍam āsthāya tat kāryaṃ punar uddharet ||
children.translated_text: he may reopen that case by undertaking a double fine.

children.text: durdṛṣṭe vyavahāre tu sabhyās taṃ daṇḍam āpnuyuḥ
children.translated_text: But in a badly adjudicated suit the assessors incur that fine,

children.text: na hi jātu vinā daṇḍaṃ kaścin mārge 'vatiṣṭhate ||
children.translated_text: for no one at all stays on the right path without punishment.

children.text: rāgād ajñānato vāpi lobhād vā yo 'nyathā vadet
children.translated_text: If an assessor, from passion, ignorance, or greed, speaks otherwise than the truth,

children.text: sabhyo 'sabhyaḥ sa vijñeyas taṃ rājā vinayed bhṛśam ||
children.translated_text: he should be known as unworthy of the assembly, and the king should punish him severely.

children.text: kiṃtu rājñā viśeṣeṇa svadharmam anurakṣatā
children.translated_text: But the king, especially while protecting his own <s>dharma</s> (duty),

children.text: manuṣyacittavaicitryāt parīkṣyā sādhvasādhutā ||
children.translated_text: must examine what is sound and unsound, because human minds are varied.

children.text: puruṣāḥ santi ye lobhāt prabrūyuḥ sākṣyam anyathā
children.translated_text: There are men who, out of greed, would give testimony falsely,

children.text: santi cānye durātmānaḥ kūṭalekhyakṛto janāḥ ||
children.translated_text: and there are other wicked people who make forged documents.

children.text: ataḥ parīkṣyam ubhayam etad rājñā viśeṣataḥ
children.translated_text: Therefore the king must examine both of these especially:

children.text: lekhyācāreṇa likhitaṃ sākṣyācāreṇa sākṣiṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: a written document according to the procedure for documents, and witnesses according to the procedure for testimony.

children.text: asatyāḥ satyasaṃkāśāḥ satyāś cāsatyadarśanāḥ
children.translated_text: False things look like true ones, and true things appear as false ones;

children.text: dṛśyante vividhā bhāvās tasmād yuktaṃ parīkṣaṇam ||
children.translated_text: many kinds of states are seen, and therefore examination is proper.

children.text: talavad dṛśyate vyoma khadyoto havyavāḍ iva
children.translated_text: The sky appears like a surface, and a firefly like the oblation-bearing fire;

children.text: na talaṃ vidyate vyomni na khadyote hutāśanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: yet there is no surface in the sky, and no fire in a firefly.

children.text: tasmāt pratyakṣadṛṣṭo 'pi yuktam arthaḥ parīkṣitum
children.translated_text: Therefore even a matter seen by direct perception is fit to be examined,

children.text: parīkṣya jñāpayan arthān na dharmāt parihīyate ||
children.translated_text: and one who, after examination, makes matters known does not fall away from <s>dharma</s> (justice).

children.text: evaṃ paśyan sadā rājā vyavahārān samāhitaḥ
children.translated_text: Seeing lawsuits in this way, always attentive, the king

children.text: vitatyeha yaśo dīptaṃ bradhnasyāpnoti viṣṭapam ||
children.translated_text: spreads bright fame here and obtains the world of the sun.

children.text: Chapter 2
suniścitabalādhānas tv arthī svārthapracoditaḥ
children.translated_text: But the claimant, whose grounds of strength are well determined and who is impelled by his own interest,

children.text: lekhayet pūrvapakṣaṃ tu kṛtakāryaviniścayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: having resolved on the action to be done, should have the <s>pūrvapakṣa</s> (opening claim) written down.

children.text: pūrvapakṣaśrutārthas tu pratyarthī tadanantaram
children.translated_text: Then the defendant, after hearing the substance of the opening claim,

children.text: pūrvapakṣārthasaṃbandhaṃ pratipakṣaṃ niveśayet ||
children.translated_text: should enter a <s>pratipakṣa</s> (counter-plea) connected with the matter of the opening claim.

children.text: śvo lekhanaṃ vā sa labhet tryahaṃ saptāham eva vā
children.translated_text: He may obtain time for writing until tomorrow, or for three days, or for seven days.

children.text: arthī tṛtīyapāde tu yuktaṃ sadyo dhruvaṃ jayī ||
children.translated_text: But at the third stage, if the claimant is in the right, he is surely victorious at once.

children.text: mithyā saṃpratipattir vā pratyavaskandam eva vā
children.translated_text: Denial, admission, or a counter-plea,

children.text: prāṅnyāyavidhisādhyaṃ vā uttaraṃ syāc caturvidham ||
children.translated_text: or one to be established by the rule of prior adjudication: an <s>uttara</s> (answer) is fourfold.

children.text: mithyaitan nābhijānāmi tadā tatra na saṃnidhiḥ
children.translated_text: 'This is false'; 'I do not know it'; 'I was not present there then';

children.text: ajātaś cāsmi tatkāla evaṃ mithyā caturvidhā ||
children.translated_text: 'and I was not born at that time': thus denial is fourfold.

children.text: mithyā ca viparītaṃ ca punaḥ śabdasamāgamam
children.translated_text: Denial, contradiction, and again agreement in wording,

children.text: pūrvapakṣārthasaṃbandham uttaraṃ syāc caturvidham ||
children.translated_text: and connection with the matter of the opening claim: the answer should be fourfold.

children.text: bhāṣāyā uttaraṃ yāvat pratyarthī na niveśayet
children.translated_text: Until the defendant enters an answer to the plaint,

children.text: arthī tu lekhayet tāvad yāvad vastu vivakṣitam ||
children.translated_text: the claimant may have written down as much as the matter he wishes to state.

children.text: anyārtham arthahīnaṃ ca pramāṇāgamavarjitam
children.translated_text: A written plaint aimed at another object, meaningless, devoid of proof and authoritative basis,

children.text: lekhyaṃ hīnādhikaṃ bhraṣṭaṃ bhāṣādoṣās tūdāhṛtāḥ ||
children.translated_text: deficient, excessive, or corrupt: these are declared to be defects of the plaint.

children.text: labdhavyaṃ yena yad yasmāt sa tat tasmād avāpnuyāt
children.translated_text: Whatever is to be obtained by someone from someone, he should obtain that from that person,

children.text: na tv anyo 'nyad athānyasmād ity anyārtham idaṃ tridhā ||
children.translated_text: not another thing by another person from another; this 'other object' is of three kinds.

children.text: manasāham api dhyātas tvanmitreṇeha śatruvat
children.translated_text: I too was thought of in the mind by your friend here as if I were an enemy...

children.text: ato 'nyathā mahākṣāntyā tvam ihāvedito mayā ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, if it is otherwise, you have here been informed by me with great patience.

children.text: dravyapramāṇahīnaṃ yat phalopāśrayavarjitam
children.translated_text: Whatever is deficient in the specification of the property and its measure, and is without support for the result,

children.text: pramāṇavarjitaṃ nāma lekhyadoṣaṃ tad utsṛjet ||
children.translated_text: that should be rejected as a defect in a document called 'devoid of proof'.

children.text: āgamavarjitaṃ doṣaṃ pūrvapāde vivarjayet
children.translated_text: In the first pleading one should avoid a defect that lacks authoritative basis,

children.text: ekasya bahubhiḥ sārdhaṃ purarāṣṭravirodhakam ||
children.translated_text: and also what opposes the town or the realm in a case of one person together with many.

children.text: bindumātrāpadavarṇeṣv ekāvidhiṣṭayā
children.translated_text: If, through a single irregular placing, in dots, measures, words, or letters,

children.text: hīnādhikā bhaved vyarthā tāṃ yatnena vivarjayet ||
children.translated_text: a writing becomes deficient, excessive, or meaningless, one should carefully avoid it.

children.text: bhraṣṭaṃ tu duḥsthitaṃ yat syāj jalatailādibhir hatam
children.translated_text: But whatever is corrupted, badly set down, or damaged by water, oil, and the like,

children.text: bhāṣāyāṃ tad api spaṣṭaṃ vispaṣṭārthaṃ vivarjayet ||
children.translated_text: even if clear in its wording, should be rejected if its meaning is indistinct.

children.text: satyā bhāṣā na bhavati yady api syāt pratiṣṭhitā
children.translated_text: A statement is not true, even if it has been established,

children.text: bahiś ced bhraśyate dharmān niyatād vyavahārikāt ||
children.translated_text: if it falls outside the fixed juridical <s>dharma</s> (legal norm) of <s>vyavahāra</s> (litigation).

children.text: gandhamādanasaṃsthasya mayāsyāsīt tad arpitam
children.translated_text: 'That was delivered by me to him while he was staying on <s>Gandhamādana</s>':

children.text: vyavahārikadharmasya bāhyam etan na sidhyati ||
children.translated_text: this lies outside juridical <s>dharma</s> and is not established.

children.text: anyākṣaraniveśena anyārthagamanena ca
children.translated_text: By the insertion of another letter, and by movement toward another meaning,

children.text: ākulaṃ ca kriyādānaṃ kriyā caivākulā bhavet ||
children.translated_text: the presentation of <s>kriyā</s> (proof) becomes confused, and the proof itself becomes confused.

children.text: rāgādīnāṃ yad ekena kopitaḥ karaṇe vadet
children.translated_text: Whatever a litigant, provoked by one among passion and the other faults, may say in the proceeding,

children.text: tad ādau tu likhet sarvaṃ vādinaḥ phalakādiṣu ||
children.translated_text: all that should first be written down on the litigant's tablets and the like.

children.text: nirākulāvabodhāya dharmasthaiḥ suvicāritam
children.translated_text: For an unconfused understanding, what has been well considered by those established in <s>dharma</s>

children.text: tasmād anyad vyapohyaṃ syād vādinaḥ phalakādiṣu ||
children.translated_text: should remain; anything else should be removed from the litigant's tablets and the like.

children.text: vādibhyām abhyanujñātaṃ śeṣaṃ ca phalake sthitam
children.translated_text: What has been approved by both litigants, and the remainder standing on the tablet,

children.text: sasākṣikaṃ likheyus te pratipattiṃ ca vādinoḥ ||
children.translated_text: they should write down together with witnesses, along with the agreement of the two litigants.

children.text: vādibhyāṃ likhitāc cheṣaṃ yat punar vādinā smṛtam
children.translated_text: Whatever remainder from what was written by the two litigants is again recalled by a litigant,

children.text: tat pratyākalitaṃ nāma svapāde tasya likhyate ||
children.translated_text: that is called <s>pratyākalita</s> (recalled matter), and it is written in his own pleading.

children.text: arthinā saṃniyukto vā pratyarthiprahito 'pi vā
children.translated_text: Whether appointed by the claimant or sent by the defendant,

children.text: yo yasyārthe vivadate tayor jayaparājayau ||
children.translated_text: whoever litigates for another's purpose, victory and defeat belong to those two.

children.text: yo na bhrātā na ca pitā na putro na niyogakṛt
children.translated_text: One who is neither brother, nor father, nor son, nor an appointed agent,

children.text: parārthavādī daṇḍyaḥ syād vyavahāre 'pi vibruvan ||
children.translated_text: if he pleads another's cause, should be fined, even though speaking in a lawsuit.

children.text: pūrvavādaṃ parityajya yo 'nyam ālambate punaḥ
children.translated_text: A man who abandons the prior claim and again takes up another

children.text: vādasaṃkramaṇāj jñeyo hīnavādī sa vai naraḥ ||
children.translated_text: is to be known, because of the shifting of the suit, as one whose case is lost.

children.text: sarveṣv api vivādeṣu vākchale nāpahīyate
children.translated_text: In all disputes, however, one is not defeated merely through verbal quibbling.

children.text: paśustrībhūmyṛṇādāne śāsyo 'py arthān na hīyate ||
children.translated_text: In matters of animals, women, land, debts, and deposits, though punishable, he does not lose the property.

children.text: abhiyukto 'bhiyogasya yadi kuryād apahnavam
children.translated_text: If the defendant makes a denial of the accusation,

children.text: abhiyoktā diśed deśyaṃ pratyavaskandito na cet ||
children.translated_text: the accuser should indicate what is to be proved, unless he has been met by a counterclaim.

children.text: pūrvapāde hi likhitaṃ yathākṣaram aśeṣataḥ
children.translated_text: For in the first pleading it is written down completely, letter for letter;

children.text: arthī tṛtīyapāde tu kriyayā pratipādayet ||
children.translated_text: but in the third pleading the claimant should establish it by <s>kriyā</s> (proof).

children.text: kriyāpi dvividhā proktā mānuṣī daivikī tathā
children.translated_text: <s>Kriyā</s> (proof) too is said to be twofold: human and divine.

children.text: mānuṣī lekhyasākṣibhyāṃ dhaṭādir daivikī smṛtā ||
children.translated_text: The human kind is by documents and witnesses; the divine kind is remembered as the balance ordeal and the like.

children.text: divā kṛte kāryavidhau grāmeṣu nagareṣu vā
children.translated_text: When the procedure concerns an act done by day, in villages or towns,

children.text: saṃbhave sākṣiṇāṃ caiva divyā na bhavati kriyā ||
children.translated_text: and when witnesses are possible, divine <s>kriyā</s> does not apply.

children.text: araṇye nirjane rātrāv antarveśmani sāhase
children.translated_text: In a forest, in a deserted place, at night, inside a house, in a violent offense,

children.text: nyāsasyāpahnave caiva divyā sambhavati kriyā ||
children.translated_text: and also in the denial of a deposit, divine <s>kriyā</s> is possible.

children.text: kāraṇapratipattyā ca pūrvapakṣe virodhite
children.translated_text: And when the <s>pūrvapakṣa</s> (initial case) has been opposed by acceptance of the cause,

children.text: abhiyuktena vai bhāvyaṃ vijñeyaṃ pūrvapakṣavat ||
children.translated_text: the defendant must prove it; this should be understood as with the initial case.

children.text: palāyate ya āhūto maunī sākṣiparājitaḥ
children.translated_text: One who flees when summoned, one who is silent, one defeated by witnesses,

children.text: svayam abhyupapannaś ca avasannaś caturvidhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and one who has admitted the matter himself: a failed litigant is of four kinds.

children.text: anyavādī kriyādveṣī nopasthātā niruttaraḥ
children.translated_text: One who speaks otherwise, one hostile to proof, one who does not appear, one without an answer,

children.text: āhūtaprapalāyī ca hīnaḥ pañcavidhaḥ smṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and one who flees after being summoned: the defeated litigant is remembered as fivefold.

children.text: maṇayaḥ padmarāgādyā dīnārādi hiraṇmayam
children.translated_text: Gems such as rubies, gold such as dīnāras,

children.text: muktāvidrumaśaṅkhādyāḥ praduṣṭāḥ svāmigāminaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and pearls, coral, shells, and the like, when defective, go back to the owner.

children.text: gandhamālyam adattaṃ tu bhūṣaṇaṃ vāsa eva vā
children.translated_text: Ungiven perfume or garland, or an ornament, garment,

children.text: pāduketi rājoktaṃ tad ākrāman vadham arhati ||
children.translated_text: or sandals, when declared to be the king's: one who lays hold of that deserves death.

children.text: paṇyamūlyaṃ bhṛtir nyāso daṇḍo yac cāvahārakam
children.translated_text: The price of merchandise, wages, a deposit, a fine, and whatever has been misappropriated,

children.text: vṛthādānākṣikapaṇā vardhante nāvivakṣitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: as well as gratuitous gifts and gambling stakes, do not increase when no such increase was stipulated.

children.text: mithyābhiyogino ye syur dvijānāṃ śūdrayonayaḥ
children.translated_text: Those of śūdra birth who become false accusers of twice-born men:

children.text: teṣāṃ jihvāṃ samutkṛtya rājā śūle vidhāpayet ||
children.translated_text: having cut out their tongues, the king should have them impaled on a stake.

children.text: ājñā lekhaḥ paṭṭakaḥ śāsanaṃ vā ādhiḥ pattraṃ vikrayo vā krayo vā
children.translated_text: An order, a deed, a charter, a royal grant, a pledge, a document, a sale, or a purchase:

children.text: rājñe kuryāt pūrvam āvedanaṃ yas tasya jñeyaḥ pūrvapakṣaḥ vidhijñaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: whoever first makes a declaration to the king, his initial claim should be recognized by those versed in law.

children.text: sākṣikadūṣaṇe kāryaṃ pūrvasākṣiviśodhanam
children.translated_text: When there is an impeachment of witnesses, the prior witnesses should first be cleared;

children.text: śuddheṣu sākṣiṣu tataḥ paścāt sākṣyaṃ viśodhayet ||
children.translated_text: once the witnesses have been cleared, then the testimony should afterward be examined.

children.text: sākṣisabhyāvasannānāṃ dūṣaṇe darśanaṃ punaḥ
children.translated_text: When witnesses and court assessors who have failed are challenged, there is renewed appearance;

children.text: svacaryāvasitānāṃ tu nāsti paunarbhavo vidhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: but for those who have failed through their own conduct, there is no rule of recurrence.

children.text: svayam abhyupapanno 'pi svacaryāvasito 'pi san
children.translated_text: Even one who has admitted the matter himself, even one who has failed through his own conduct,

children.text: kriyāvasanno 'py arheta paraṃ sabhyāvadhāraṇam ||
children.translated_text: and even one who has failed in proof may deserve a further determination by the court assessors.

children.text: pakṣān utsārya kāryas tu sabhyaiḥ kāryaviniścayaḥ
children.translated_text: After setting aside the parties' positions, the assessors should make the decision in the case;

children.text: anutsāritanirṇikte virodhaḥ pretya ceha ca ||
children.translated_text: if a decision is made without such removal and clarification, contradiction arises both here and hereafter.

children.text: sabhair eva jitaḥ paścād rājñā śāsyaḥ svaśāstrataḥ
children.translated_text: One who has been defeated by the assessors should afterward be punished by the king according to his own law;

children.text: jayine cāpi deyaṃ syād yathāvaj jayapatrakam ||
children.translated_text: and a document of victory should also be given properly to the winner.

children.text: vyavahāramukhaṃ caitat pūrvam uktaṃ svayaṃbhuvā
children.translated_text: This opening of <s>vyavahāra</s> (litigation) was formerly taught by <s>Svayambhū</s>.

children.text: mukhaśuddhau hi śuddhiḥ syād vyavahārasya nānyathā ||
children.translated_text: For when the opening is pure, the litigation is pure; not otherwise.

children.text: Chapter 3
niyuktena tu vaktavyam apakṣapatitaṃ vacaḥ ||
children.translated_text: But one who has been appointed must speak words that have not fallen to either side.

children.text: yuktarūpaṃ bruvan sabhyo nāpnuyād dveṣakilbiṣe
children.translated_text: An assessor who speaks what is fitting in form incurs neither hatred nor guilt;

children.text: bruvāṇas tv anyathā sabhyas tad evobhayam āpnuyāt ||
children.translated_text: but an assessor who speaks otherwise incurs both of those.

children.text: rājā tu dhārmikān sabhyān niyuñjyāt suparīkṣitān
children.translated_text: The king should appoint righteous assessors who have been well examined,

children.text: vyavahāradhuraṃ voḍhuṃ ye śaktāḥ sadgavā iva ||
children.translated_text: who are able to bear the burden of litigation like good oxen,

children.text: dharmaśāstrārthakuśalāḥ kulīnāḥ satyavādinaḥ
children.translated_text: skilled in the meaning of <s>dharmaśāstra</s> (legal scripture), well-born, and truthful in speech.

children.text: samāḥ śatrau ca mitre ca nṛpateḥ syuḥ sabhāsadaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The king's assessors should be equal toward enemy and friend.

children.text: tatpratiṣṭhaḥ smṛto dharmo dharmamūlaś ca pārthivaḥ
children.translated_text: Dharma is remembered as founded on them, and the king has dharma as his root.

children.text: saha sadbhir ato rājā vyavahārān viśodhayet ||
children.translated_text: Therefore the king should purify legal proceedings together with good men.

children.text: śuddheṣu vyavahāreṣu śuddhiṃ yānti sabhāsadaḥ
children.translated_text: When legal proceedings are purified, the assessors attain purity;

children.text: śuddhiś ca teṣāṃ dharmāddhi dharmam eva vadet tataḥ ||
children.translated_text: and since their purity comes from dharma, therefore he should speak dharma alone.

children.text: yatra dharmo hy adharmeṇa satyaṃ yatrānṛtena ca
children.translated_text: Where dharma is struck down by adharma, and truth by falsehood,

children.text: hanyate prekṣamāṇānāṃ hatās tatra sabhāsadaḥ ||
children.translated_text: while the onlookers watch, there the assessors are struck down.

children.text: viddho dharmo hy adharmeṇa sabhāṃ yatropatiṣṭhate
children.translated_text: Where dharma, pierced by adharma, comes before the assembly,

children.text: na ced viśalyaḥ kriyate viddhās tatra sabhāsadaḥ ||
children.translated_text: if it is not freed from the dart, there the assessors are pierced.

children.text: sabhā vā na praveṣṭavyā vaktavyaṃ vā samañjasam
children.translated_text: One should either not enter an assembly, or should speak what is fitting;

children.text: abruvan vibruvan vāpi naro bhavati kilbiṣī ||
children.translated_text: by not speaking, or by speaking wrongly, a man becomes guilty.

children.text: ye tu sabhyāḥ sabhāṃ gatvā tūṣṇīṃ dhyāyanta āsate
children.translated_text: But those assessors who, having entered the assembly, sit silently meditating,

children.text: yathāprāptaṃ na bruvate sarve te 'nṛtavādinaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and do not say what is appropriate to the case, all of them are speakers of falsehood.

children.text: pādo 'dharmasya kartāraṃ pādaḥ sākṣiṇam ṛcchati
children.translated_text: A quarter of the adharma reaches the doer; a quarter reaches the witness;

children.text: pādaḥ sabhāsadaḥ sarvān pādo rājānam ṛcchati ||
children.translated_text: a quarter reaches all the assessors, and a quarter reaches the king.

children.text: rājā bhavaty anenās tu mucyante ca sabhāsadaḥ
children.translated_text: The king becomes free from guilt, and the assessors too are released,

children.text: eno gacchati kartāraṃ nindārho yatra nindyate ||
children.translated_text: where the blameworthy one is blamed; the guilt goes to the doer.

children.text: andho matsyān ivāśnāti nirapekṣaḥ sakaṇṭakān
children.translated_text: Like a blind man eating fish heedlessly, bones and all,

children.text: parokṣam arthavaikalyād bhāṣate yaḥ sabhāṃ gataḥ ||
children.translated_text: is one who, having entered an assembly, speaks about an unseen matter because the facts are deficient.

children.text: tasmāt sabhyaḥ sabhāṃ prāpya rāgadveṣavivarjitaḥ
children.translated_text: Therefore an assessor, having come to the assembly and being free from passion and hatred,

children.text: vacas tathāvidhaṃ brūyād yathā na narakaṃ patet ||
children.translated_text: should speak such a statement that he does not fall into hell.

children.text: yathā śalyaṃ bhiṣag vidvān uddhared yantrayuktitaḥ
children.translated_text: Just as a learned physician would extract a dart through instruments and skill,

children.text: prāḍvivākas tathā śalyam uddhared vyavahārataḥ ||
children.translated_text: so the chief judge should extract the dart through legal procedure.

children.text: yatra sabhyo janaḥ sarvaḥ sādhv etad iti manyate
children.translated_text: Where all the people of the assembly think, 'This is proper,'

children.text: sa niḥśalyo vivādaḥ syāt saśalyaḥ syād ato 'nyathā ||
children.translated_text: that dispute is without a dart; otherwise it is with a dart.

children.text: na sā sabhā yatra na santi vṛddhā vṛddhā na te ye na vadanti dharmam
children.translated_text: That is not an assembly where there are no elders; those are not elders who do not speak dharma.

children.text: nāsau dharmo yatra na satyam asti na tat satyaṃ yac chalenānuviddham ||
children.translated_text: That is not dharma where there is no truth, and that is not truth which is pierced by deceit.

children.text: Chapter 4
ṛṇaṃ deyam adeyaṃ ca yena yatra yathā ca yat
children.translated_text: A debt to be paid or not to be paid, by whom, where, how, and which one it is:

children.text: dānagrahaṇadharmāc ca ṛṇādānam iti smṛtam ||
children.translated_text: from the rule of giving and receiving, this is remembered as debt recovery.

children.text: pitary uparate putrā ṛṇaṃ dadyur yathāṃśataḥ
children.translated_text: When the father has died, the sons should pay the debt according to their shares,

children.text: vibhaktā hy avibhaktā vā yas tām udvahate dhuram ||
children.translated_text: whether they are divided or undivided, whoever bears that burden.

children.text: pitṛvyeṇāvibhaktena bhrātrā vā yad ṛṇaṃ kṛtam
children.translated_text: A debt incurred by an undivided paternal uncle or by a brother,

children.text: mātrā vā yat kuṭumbārthe dadyus tad rikthino 'khilam ||
children.translated_text: or by the mother for the sake of the family, the heirs should pay in full.

children.text: kramād avyāhataṃ prāptaṃ putrair yan narṇam uddhṛtam
children.translated_text: A debt received in unbroken succession, which the sons have taken up,

children.text: dadyuḥ paitāmahaṃ pautrās tac caturthān nivartate ||
children.translated_text: the grandsons should pay as ancestral; it ceases with the fourth generation.

children.text: icchanti pitaraḥ putrān svārthahetor yatas tataḥ
children.translated_text: Fathers desire sons for their own benefit, because they think,

children.text: uttamarṇādhamarṇebhyo mām ayaṃ mocayiṣyati ||
children.translated_text: 'This one will release me from creditors and debtors.'

children.text: ataḥ putreṇa jātena svārtham utsṛjya yatnataḥ
children.translated_text: Therefore, once a son is born, he should abandon his own interest and diligently

children.text: pitā mokṣitavya ṛṇād yathā na narakaṃ patet ||
children.translated_text: free his father from debt, so that he may not fall into hell.

children.text: tapasvī cāgnihotrī ca ṛṇavān mriyate yadi
children.translated_text: If an ascetic and an agnihotrin dies while owing a debt,

children.text: tapaś caivāgnihotraṃ ca sarvaṃ tad dhanināṃ dhanam ||
children.translated_text: his austerity and agnihotra all become the creditor's wealth.

children.text: na putrarṇaṃ pitā dadyād dadyāt putras tu paitṛkam
children.translated_text: A father should not pay a son's debt, but a son should pay a paternal debt,

children.text: kāmakrodhasurādyūtaprātibhāvyakṛtaṃ vinā ||
children.translated_text: except what was incurred through desire, anger, liquor, gambling, or suretyship.

children.text: pitur eva niyogād yat kuṭumbabharaṇāya ca
children.translated_text: What was incurred at the father's command, or for the support of the family,

children.text: kṛtaṃ vā yad ṛṇaṃ kṛcchre dadyāt putrasya tat pitā ||
children.translated_text: or whatever debt was incurred in hardship, the father should pay that debt of the son.

children.text: śiṣyāntevāsidāsastrīvaiyāvṛttyakaraiś ca yat
children.translated_text: What has been raised by pupils, resident students, slaves, women, and hired servants

children.text: kuṭumbahetor utkṣiptaṃ voḍhavyaṃ tat kuṭumbinā ||
children.translated_text: for the sake of the family must be borne by the householder.

children.text: nārvāg viṃśatimād varṣāt pitari proṣite sutaḥ
children.translated_text: A son should not, before he is twenty years old, when his father is abroad,

children.text: ṛṇaṃ dadyāt pitṛvye vā jyeṣṭhe bhrātary athāpi vā ||
children.translated_text: pay a debt, if there is a paternal uncle or an eldest brother.

children.text: dāpyaḥ pararṇam eko 'pi jīvatsv adhikṛtaiḥ kṛtam
children.translated_text: Even one person may be made to pay another's debt incurred by authorized persons while they are alive;

children.text: preteṣu tu na tatputraḥ pararṇaṃ dātum arhati ||
children.translated_text: but after they are dead, his son is not liable to pay another's debt.

children.text: na strī patikṛtaṃ dadyād ṛṇaṃ putrakṛtaṃ tathā
children.translated_text: A woman should not pay a debt made by her husband, nor likewise one made by her son,

children.text: abhyupetād ṛte yadvā saha patyā kṛtaṃ bhavet ||
children.translated_text: except what she has agreed to, or what was incurred together with her husband.

children.text: dadyād aputrā vidhavā niyuktā yā mumūrṣuṇā
children.translated_text: A childless widow appointed by a dying man should pay,

children.text: yo vā tadriktham ādadyād yato riktham ṛṇaṃ tataḥ ||
children.translated_text: or whoever takes his inheritance; from wherever the inheritance comes, from there comes the debt.

children.text: na ca bhāryākṛtam ṛṇaṃ kathaṃcit patyur ābhavet
children.translated_text: Nor does a debt incurred by the wife in any way fall upon the husband,

children.text: āpatkṛtād ṛte puṃsāṃ kuṭumbārtho hi vistaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: except one incurred in distress, for men's household responsibility is broad.

children.text: anyatra rajakavyādhagopaśauṇḍikayoṣitām
children.translated_text: Except in the case of the wives of washermen, hunters, cowherds, and liquor sellers;

children.text: teṣāṃ tatpratyayā vṛttiḥ kuṭumbaṃ ca tadāśrayam ||
children.translated_text: their livelihood depends on them, and the family rests on them.

children.text: putriṇī tu samutsṛjya putraṃ strī yānyam āśrayet
children.translated_text: But if a woman with a son abandons her son and resorts to another man,

children.text: ṛkthaṃ tasyā haret sarvaṃ niḥsvāyāḥ putra eva tu ||
children.translated_text: her son alone should take all her property; if she has no property, it is the son alone.

children.text: yā tu sapradhanaiva strī sāpatyā cānyam āśrayet
children.translated_text: But if a woman who has property and offspring resorts to another man,

children.text: so 'syā dadyād ṛṇaṃ bhartur utsṛjed vā tathaiva tām ||
children.translated_text: that man should pay her husband's debt, or else let her go in the same way.

children.text: adhanasya hy aputrasya mṛtasyopaiti yaḥ striyam
children.translated_text: He who takes the wife of a dead man who had neither property nor sons

children.text: ṛṇaṃ voḍhuḥ sa bhajate tad evāsya dhanaṃ smṛtam ||
children.translated_text: undertakes to bear his debt; that alone is remembered as his wealth.

children.text: dhanastrīhāriputrāṇām ṛṇabhāg yo dhanaṃ haret
children.translated_text: As between the taker of wealth, the taker of the wife, and the son, the share of debt belongs to the one who takes the wealth;

children.text: putro 'satoḥ strīdhaninoḥ strīhārī dhaniputrayoḥ ||
children.translated_text: if wife and wealth are absent, it falls on the son; if wealth and sons are absent, on the taker of the wife.

children.text: uttamā svairiṇī yā syād uttamā ca punarbhuvām
children.translated_text: A woman who is the foremost kind of svairiṇī, and the foremost among punarbhūs,

children.text: ṛṇaṃ tayoḥ patikṛtaṃ dadyād yas tām upāśnute ||
children.translated_text: the man who takes her should pay the debt incurred by her husband.

children.text: strīkṛtāny apramāṇāni kāryāṇy āhur anāpadi
children.translated_text: Acts done by women are said to be invalid when there is no emergency,

children.text: viśeṣato gṛhakṣetradānādhamanavikrayāḥ ||
children.translated_text: especially gifts, mortgages, and sales of houses and fields.

children.text: etāny api pramāṇāni bhartā yady anumanyate
children.translated_text: Even these are valid if the husband approves them.

children.text: putraḥ patyur abhāve vā rājā vā patiputrayoḥ ||
children.translated_text: or the son in the husband's absence, or the king when both husband and son are absent.

children.text: bhartrā prītena yad dattaṃ striyai tasmin mṛte 'pi tat
children.translated_text: What has been given to a woman by her husband when he was pleased, even after he has died,

children.text: sā yathākāmam aśnīyād dadyād vā sthāvarād ṛte ||
children.translated_text: she may enjoy as she wishes, or give away, except for immovable property.

children.text: tathā dāsakṛtaṃ kāryam akṛtaṃ paricakṣate
children.translated_text: Likewise, an act done by a slave they declare to be not done,

children.text: anyatra svāmisaṃdeśān na dāsaḥ prabhur ātmanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: except on the master's command; a slave is not his own master.

children.text: putreṇa ca kṛtaṃ kāryaṃ yat syāt pitur anicchataḥ
children.translated_text: And whatever act is done by a son against his father's wish,

children.text: tad apy akṛtam evāhur dāsaḥ putraś ca tau samau ||
children.translated_text: that too, they say, is simply not done; a slave and a son are alike in this respect.

children.text: aprāptavyavahāraś cet svatantro 'pi hi narṇabhāk
children.translated_text: If he has not attained legal capacity for transactions, even though independent he is not liable for debt.

children.text: svātantryaṃ tu smṛtaṃ jyeṣṭhe jyaiṣṭhyaṃ guṇavayaḥkṛtam ||
children.translated_text: But independence is remembered for the eldest; seniority is based on merit and age.

children.text: trayaḥ svatantrā loke 'smin rājācāryas tathaiva ca
children.translated_text: Three are independent in this world: the king, the teacher, and likewise,

children.text: prati prati ca varṇānāṃ sarveṣāṃ svagṛhe gṛhī ||
children.translated_text: for each of all the varṇas, the householder in his own house.

children.text: asvatantrāḥ prajāḥ sarvāḥ svatantraḥ pṛthivīpatiḥ
children.translated_text: All subjects are dependent; the lord of the earth is independent.

children.text: asvatantraḥ smṛtaḥ śiṣya ācārye tu svatantratā ||
children.translated_text: A pupil is remembered as dependent, while independence belongs to the teacher.

children.text: asvatantrāḥ striyaḥ putrā dāsāś ca saparigrahāḥ
children.translated_text: Women, sons, and slaves, together with their possessions, are dependent.

children.text: svatantras tatra tu gṛhī yasya yat syāt kramāgatam ||
children.translated_text: There the householder is independent with respect to whatever has come down in succession to him.

children.text: garbhasthaiḥ sadṛśo jñeya ā varṣād aṣṭamācchiśuḥ
children.translated_text: A child up to the eighth year should be understood as like one still in the womb.

children.text: bāla ā ṣoḍaśāj jñeyaḥ pogaṇḍaś cāpi śabdyate ||
children.translated_text: Up to the sixteenth year he is known as a child, and is also called a paugaṇḍa boy.

children.text: parato vyavahārajñaḥ svatantraḥ pitarau vinā
children.translated_text: After that, if he understands legal dealings, he is independent when without parents.

children.text: jīvator asvatantraḥ syāj jarayāpi samanvitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: While they are alive he is dependent, even if he is advanced in old age.

children.text: tayor api pitā śreyān bījaprādhānyadarśanāt
children.translated_text: Of those two also, the father is superior, because the primacy of the seed is observed.

children.text: abhāve bījino mātā tadabhāve tu pūrvajaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In the absence of the seed-giver, the mother is superior; and in her absence, the elder-born.

children.text: svatantrāḥ sarva evaite paratantreṣu sarvadā
children.translated_text: All these are always independent in relation to those who are dependent on others.

children.text: anuśiṣṭau visarge ca vikraye ceśvarā matāḥ ||
children.translated_text: In discipline, release, and sale they are considered the authorities.

children.text: yad bālaḥ kurute kāryam asvatantras tathaiva ca
children.translated_text: Whatever act a child does, and likewise one who is dependent,

children.text: akṛtaṃ tad iti prāhuḥ śāstre śāstravido janāḥ ||
children.translated_text: the knowers of śāstra say in the śāstra that it is not done.

children.text: svatantro 'pi hi yat kāryaṃ kuryād aprakṛtiṃ gataḥ
children.translated_text: Even whatever act an independent person does after he has fallen from his natural state,

children.text: tad apy akṛtam evāhur asvatantraḥ sa hetutaḥ ||
children.translated_text: that too, they say, is simply not done; because of that cause he is dependent.

children.text: kāmakrodhābhiyuktārtabhayavyasanapīḍitāḥ
children.translated_text: Those overcome by desire or anger, afflicted by distress, fear, or calamity,

children.text: rāgadveṣaparītāś ca jñeyās tv aprakṛtiṃ gatāḥ ||
children.translated_text: and those beset by attachment and hatred, should be known as having fallen from their natural state.

children.text: kule jyeṣṭhas tathā śreṣṭhaḥ prakṛtisthaś ca yo bhavet
children.translated_text: In a family, whoever is eldest, superior, and in his natural state,

children.text: tatkṛtaṃ syāt kṛtaṃ kāryaṃ nāsvatantrakṛtaṃ kṛtam ||
children.translated_text: the act done by him is valid; an act done by one who is dependent is not valid.

children.text: dhanamūlāḥ kriyāḥ sarvā yatnas tatsādhane mataḥ
children.translated_text: All undertakings have wealth as their root; effort is regarded as directed toward obtaining it.

children.text: rakṣaṇaṃ vardhanaṃ bhoga iti tasya vidhiḥ kramāt ||
children.translated_text: Protection, increase, and enjoyment: this is its prescribed order.

children.text: tat punas trividhaṃ jñeyaṃ śuklaṃ śabalam eva ca
children.translated_text: That wealth again should be known as threefold: white, mixed,

children.text: kṛṣṇaṃ ca tasya vijñeyaḥ prabhedaḥ saptadhā pṛthak ||
children.translated_text: and black; its subdivisions should be known separately as sevenfold.

children.text: śrutaśauryatapaḥkanyāśiṣyayājyānvayāgatam
children.translated_text: What comes from learning, valor, austerity, a maiden, a pupil, a sacrificer, or lineage,

children.text: dhanaṃ saptavidhaṃ śuklam udayo 'py asya tadvidhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: is sevenfold white wealth; its income also is of that same kind.

children.text: kusīdakṛṣivāṇijyaśulkaśilpānuvṛttibhiḥ
children.translated_text: What is obtained through interest-lending, agriculture, trade, tolls, crafts, and service,

children.text: kṛtopakārād āptaṃ ca śabalaṃ samudāhṛtam ||
children.translated_text: and from one to whom a service has been rendered, is called mixed wealth.

children.text: pārśvikadyūtadautyārtipratirūpakasāhasaiḥ
children.translated_text: What is obtained through side-dealing, gambling, brokerage, exploiting distress, counterfeiting, and violence,

children.text: vyājenopārjitaṃ yac ca tat kṛṣṇaṃ samudāhṛtam ||
children.translated_text: and whatever is acquired by deceit, that is called black wealth.

children.text: tena krayo vikrayaś ca dānaṃ grahaṇam eva ca
children.translated_text: By means of it, purchase and sale, gift and receipt,

children.text: vividhāś ca pravartante kriyāḥ saṃbhoga eva ca ||
children.translated_text: and various other transactions and enjoyments proceed.

children.text: yathāvidhena dravyeṇa yat kiṃcit kurute naraḥ
children.translated_text: Whatever a man does with property of a particular kind,

children.text: tathāvidham avāpnoti sa phalaṃ pretya ceha ca ||
children.translated_text: he obtains a fruit of that same kind, both after death and here.

children.text: tat punar dvādaśavidhaṃ prativarṇāśrayāt smṛtam
children.translated_text: That again is remembered as twelvefold, depending on each varṇa.

children.text: sādhāraṇaṃ syāt trividhaṃ śeṣaṃ navavidhaṃ smṛtam ||
children.translated_text: The common kind is threefold; the remainder is remembered as ninefold.

children.text: kramāgataṃ prītidāyaḥ prāptaṃ ca saha bhāryayā
children.translated_text: Inherited wealth, a gift of affection, and what is obtained together with a wife:

children.text: aviśeṣeṇa varṇānāṃ sarveṣāṃ trividhaṃ dhanam ||
children.translated_text: for all varṇas without distinction, wealth is threefold in this way.

children.text: vaiśeṣikaṃ dhanaṃ jñeyaṃ brāhmaṇasya trilakṣaṇam
children.translated_text: The special wealth of a Brahmin should be known as threefold:

children.text: pratigraheṇa yallabdhaṃ yājyataḥ śiṣyatas tathā ||
children.translated_text: what is received through accepting gifts, from officiating at sacrifices, and from pupils.

children.text: trividhaṃ kṣatriyasyāpi prāhur vaiśeṣikaṃ dhanam
children.translated_text: They also declare the special wealth of a Kṣatriya to be threefold:

children.text: yuddhopalabdhaṃ kāraś ca daṇḍaś ca vyavahārataḥ ||
children.translated_text: what is obtained in battle, taxes, and fines arising from legal procedure.

children.text: vaiśeṣikaṃ dhanaṃ jñeyaṃ vaiśyasyāpi trilakṣaṇam
children.translated_text: The special wealth of a Vaiśya too should be known as threefold:

children.text: kṛṣigorakṣavāṇijyaiḥ śūdrasyaibhyas tv anugrahāt ||
children.translated_text: through agriculture, cattle-keeping, and trade; that of a Śūdra comes by favor from these.

children.text: sarveṣām eva varṇānām eṣa dharmyo dhanāgamaḥ
children.translated_text: For all varṇas, this alone is the lawful acquisition of wealth.

children.text: viparyayād adharmyaḥ syān na ced āpad garīyasī ||
children.translated_text: By the reverse it is unlawful, unless a more serious emergency exists.

children.text: āpatsv anantarā vṛttir brāhmaṇasya vidhīyate
children.translated_text: In emergencies, the next lower livelihood is prescribed for a Brahmin.

children.text: vaiśyavṛttis tataś coktā na jaghanyā kathaṃcana ||
children.translated_text: After that, the Vaiśya livelihood is stated; never the lowest in any circumstances.

children.text: na kathaṃcana kurvīta brāhmaṇaḥ karma vārṣalam
children.translated_text: A Brahmin should never perform Śūdra work.

children.text: vṛṣalaḥ karma na brāhmaṃ patanīye hi te tayoḥ ||
children.translated_text: A Śūdra should not perform Brahmin work, for those two acts cause downfall for the two of them.

children.text: utkṛṣṭaṃ cāpakṛṣṭaṃ ca tayoḥ karma na vidyate
children.translated_text: For those two, the highest and the lowest work are not available,

children.text: madhyame karmaṇī hitvā sarvasādhāraṇe hi te ||
children.translated_text: apart from the two middle occupations, since those are common to all.

children.text: āpadaṃ brāhmaṇas tīrtvā kṣatravṛttyā hṛtair dhanaiḥ
children.translated_text: When a Brahmin has crossed an emergency by wealth taken through a Kṣatriya livelihood,

children.text: utsṛjet kṣatravṛttiṃ tāṃ kṛtvā pāvanam ātmanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: he should abandon that Kṣatriya livelihood after performing purification for himself.

children.text: tasyām eva tu yo vṛttau brāhmaṇo ramate rasāt
children.translated_text: But a Brahmin who delights in that very livelihood out of relish

children.text: kāṇḍapṛṣṭhaś cyuto mārgāt so 'pāṅkteyaḥ prakīrtitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: is a <s>kāṇḍapṛṣṭha</s>, fallen from the path; he is declared unfit to sit in the ritual dining line.

children.text: vaiśyavṛttāv avikreyaṃ brāhmaṇasya payo dadhi
children.translated_text: In a Vaiśya livelihood, milk and curds are not to be sold by a Brahmin,

children.text: ghṛtaṃ madhu madhūcchiṣṭaṃ lākṣākṣārarasāsavāḥ ||
children.translated_text: nor ghee, honey, beeswax, lac, alkali, juices, or fermented liquors,

children.text: māṃsaudanatilakṣaumasomapuṣpaphalapalāḥ
children.translated_text: nor meat, cooked rice, sesame, linen, soma, flowers, fruits, and edible roots,

children.text: manuṣyaviṣaśastrāmbulavaṇāpūpavīrudhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: nor human beings, poison, weapons, water, salt, cakes, or creepers,

children.text: nīlīkauśeyacarmāsthikutapaikaśaphā mṛdaḥ
children.translated_text: nor indigo, silk, hides, bones, blankets, one-hoofed animals, or earth,

children.text: udaśvitkeśapiṇyākaśākādyauṣadhayas tathā ||
children.translated_text: and likewise buttermilk, hair, oil-cake, vegetables, and medicines and the like.

children.text: brāhmaṇasya tu vikreyaṃ śuṣkaṃ dāru tṛṇāni ca
children.translated_text: But dry wood and grasses may be sold by a Brahmin.

children.text: gandhadravyairakāvetratūlamūlatuśād ṛte ||
children.translated_text: except for fragrant substances, lac, cane, cotton, roots, and husks.

children.text: svayaṃ śīrṇaṃ ca vidalaṃ phalānāṃ badareṅgude
children.translated_text: And among fruits, what has fallen by itself, and split fruit such as jujube and iṅguda,

children.text: rajjuḥ kārpāsikaṃ sūtraṃ tac ced avikṛtaṃ bhavet ||
children.translated_text: rope and cotton thread, provided that it has not been altered.

children.text: aśaktau bheṣajasyārthe yajñahetos tathaiva ca
children.translated_text: In incapacity, for the sake of medicine, and likewise for the purpose of sacrifice,

children.text: yady avaśyaṃ tu vikreyās tilā dhānyena tatsāmāḥ ||
children.translated_text: if sesame must necessarily be sold, it should be exchanged for an equal measure of grain.

children.text: avikreyāṇi vikrīṇan brāhmaṇaḥ pracyutaḥ pathaḥ
children.translated_text: A brāhmaṇa who sells things that are not to be sold has fallen from the path;

children.text: mārge punar avasthāpya rājñā daṇḍena bhūyasā ||
children.translated_text: the king should set him back on the path by means of a heavy fine.

children.text: pramāṇāni pramāṇasthaiḥ paripālyāni yatnataḥ
children.translated_text: Standards of measure are to be carefully protected by those who are in charge of standards;

children.text: sīdanti hi pramāṇāni pramāṇair avyavasthitaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: for standards of measure fail when the standards are unsettled.

children.text: likhitaṃ sākṣiṇo bhuktiḥ pramāṇaṃ trividhaṃ smṛtaṃ
children.translated_text: A written document, witnesses, and possession are remembered as the threefold proof

children.text: dhanasvīkaraṇe yena dhanī dhanam upāśnute ||
children.translated_text: in the taking up of property, by which an owner obtains his property.

children.text: likhitaṃ balavan nityaṃ jīvantas tv eva sākṣiṇaḥ
children.translated_text: A written document is always strong, but witnesses are strong only while living;

children.text: kālātiharaṇād bhuktir iti śāstreṣu niścayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: possession, because of the passage of time, is the settled conclusion in the śāstras.

children.text: trividhasyāsya dṛṣṭasya pramāṇasya yathākramam
children.translated_text: Of this threefold visible proof, in due order,

children.text: pūrvaṃ pūrvaṃ guru jñeyaṃ bhuktir ebhyo garīyasī ||
children.translated_text: the prior proof is to be known as weighty, yet possession is weightier than these.

children.text: vidyamāne 'pi likhite jīvatsv api hi sākṣiṣu
children.translated_text: Even when a written document exists and even when witnesses are alive,

children.text: viśeṣataḥ sthāvarāṇāṃ yan na bhuktaṃ na tat sthiram ||
children.translated_text: especially in the case of immovables, what has not been possessed is not secure.

children.text: bhujyamānān parair arthān yaḥ svān maurkhyād upekṣate
children.translated_text: When a man, through folly, neglects his own property while it is being possessed by others,

children.text: samakṣaṃ jīvato 'py asya tān bhuktiḥ kurute vaśe ||
children.translated_text: possession brings that property under their control, even while he is alive and looking on.

children.text: yatkiṃcid daśa varṣāṇi saṃnidhau prekṣate dhanī
children.translated_text: Whatever property an owner watches for ten years in his presence

children.text: bhujyamānaṃ parais tūṣṇīṃ na sa tal labdhum arhati ||
children.translated_text: while it is being possessed by others, and remains silent, he is not entitled to recover.

children.text: upekṣāṃ kurvatas tasya tūṣṇīṃ bhūtasya tiṣṭhataḥ
children.translated_text: For one who is negligent, silent, and standing by,

children.text: kāle 'tipanne pūrvokte vyavahāro na sidhyati ||
children.translated_text: when the previously stated time has passed, a lawsuit does not succeed.

children.text: ajaḍaś ced apogaṇḍo viṣaye cāsya bhujyate
children.translated_text: If he is not dull-witted, not a minor, and the property is possessed within his domain,

children.text: bhuktaṃ tad vyavahāreṇa bhoktā tad dhanam arhati ||
children.translated_text: then, when it has been possessed, by legal procedure the possessor is entitled to that property.

children.text: ādhiḥ sīmā bāladhanaṃ nikṣepopanidhī striyaḥ
children.translated_text: A pledge, a boundary, a minor's property, deposits and sealed deposits, women,

children.text: rājasvaṃ śrotriyasvaṃ ca nopabhogena jīryate ||
children.translated_text: royal property, and the property of a śrotriya do not lapse through use.

children.text: pratyakṣaparibhogāc ca svāmino dvidaśāḥ samāḥ
children.translated_text: But through direct possession in the owner's sight for twenty years,

children.text: ādhyādīny api jīryante strīnarendradhanād ṛte ||
children.translated_text: even pledges and the like lapse, except for women's and royal property.

children.text: strīdhanaṃ ca narendrāṇāṃ na kadācana jīryate
children.translated_text: Women's property and the property of kings never lapse,

children.text: anāgamaṃ bhujyamānaṃ vatsarāṇāṃ śatair api ||
children.translated_text: even when possessed without title for hundreds of years.

children.text: nirbhogo yatra dṛśyeta na dṛśyetāgamaḥ kvacit
children.translated_text: Where absence of possession is seen, and no title is seen anywhere,

children.text: āgamaḥ kāraṇaṃ tatra na bhogas tatra kāraṇam ||
children.translated_text: there title is the cause; possession is not the cause there.

children.text: anāgamaṃ bhujyate yan na tad bhogo 'tivartate
children.translated_text: What is possessed without title is not carried beyond by that possession;

children.text: prete tu bhoktari dhanaṃ yāti tadvaṃśyabhogyatām ||
children.translated_text: but when the possessor has died, that property passes into the enjoyment of his descendants.

children.text: āhartaivābhiyuktaḥ sann arthānām uddharet padam
children.translated_text: The acquirer himself, when challenged, should produce the basis for the property;

children.text: bhuktir eva viśuddhiḥ syāt prāptānāṃ pitṛtaḥ kramāt ||
children.translated_text: possession itself is the purification of things received in succession from the father.

children.text: anvāhitaṃ hṛtaṃ nyastaṃ balāvaṣṭabdhaṃ yācitam
children.translated_text: What has been entrusted, stolen, deposited, held by force, borrowed,

children.text: apratyakṣaṃ ca yad bhuktaṃ ṣaḍ etāny āgamaṃ vinā ||
children.translated_text: or possessed out of sight: these six require title.

children.text: tathārūḍhavivādasya pretasya vyavahāriṇaḥ
children.translated_text: Likewise, when a litigant has died after his dispute has been formally raised,

children.text: putreṇa so 'rthaḥ saṃśodhyo na taṃ bhogo 'tivartate ||
children.translated_text: that property is to be cleared by his son; possession does not override it.

children.text: yad vināgamam apy ūrdhvaṃ bhuktaṃ pūrvais tribhir bhavet
children.translated_text: But what has been possessed without title by the three preceding generations,

children.text: na tac chakyam apākartuṃ kramāt tripuruṣāgatam ||
children.translated_text: having come down in succession through three generations, cannot be set aside.

children.text: santo 'pi na pramāṇaṃ syur mṛte dhanini sākṣiṇaḥ
children.translated_text: Even if witnesses exist, they are not proof when the property-holder has died,

children.text: anyatra śrāvitaṃ yat syāt svayam āsannamṛtyunā ||
children.translated_text: except where something was made known by the man himself as death approached.

children.text: na hi pratyarthini prete pramāṇaṃ sākṣiṇāṃ vacaḥ
children.translated_text: For when the opponent is dead, the statement of witnesses is not proof;

children.text: sākṣimat karaṇaṃ tatra pramāṇaṃ syād viniścaye ||
children.translated_text: there, in the determination, a document furnished with witnesses should be proof.

children.text: śrāvitas tv ātureṇāpi yas tv artho dharmasaṃhitaḥ
children.translated_text: But a matter connected with dharma, even if made known by a sick man,

children.text: mṛte 'pi tatra sākṣī syāt ṣaṭsu cānvāhitādiṣu ||
children.translated_text: may have a witness even after his death, and so too in the six cases beginning with entrusted property.

children.text: kriyarṇādiṣu sarveṣu balavaty uttarottarā
children.translated_text: In all matters such as transactions and debts, the later proof is stronger;

children.text: pratigrahādhikrīteṣu pūrvā pūrvā garīyasī ||
children.translated_text: in gifts, acceptances, and purchases, the earlier proof is weightier.

children.text: sthānalābhanimittaṃ hi dānagrahaṇam iṣyate
children.translated_text: Giving and receiving are held to be for the sake of obtaining gain in a fixed place;

children.text: tat kusīdam iti proktaṃ tena vṛttiḥ kusīdinām ||
children.translated_text: that is called <s>kusīda</s> (usury), and by it usurers make their living.

children.text: kāyikā kālikā caiva kāritā ca tathā smṛtā
children.translated_text: It is remembered as bodily, temporal, and stipulated,

children.text: cakravṛddhiś ca śāstreṣu tasya vṛddhiś caturvidhā ||
children.translated_text: and also as compound interest; in the śāstras its interest is fourfold.

children.text: kāyāvirodhinī śaśvat paṇapādyā tu kāyikā
children.translated_text: The bodily kind is that which always remains compatible with the principal and begins with a paṇa;

children.text: pratimāsaṃ sravati yā vṛddhiḥ sā kālikā smṛtā ||
children.translated_text: the interest that flows each month is remembered as temporal.

children.text: vṛddhiḥ sā kāritā nāma yarṇikena svayaṃkṛtā
children.translated_text: That interest which is made by the debtor himself is called stipulated;

children.text: vṛddher api punar vṛddhiś cakravṛddhir udāhṛtā ||
children.translated_text: and further interest upon interest is called compound interest.

children.text: ṛṇānāṃ sārvabhaumo 'yaṃ vidhir vṛddhikaraḥ smṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: This is remembered as the universal rule concerning debts, producing interest;

children.text: deśācāravidhis tv anyo yatrarṇam avatiṣṭhati ||
children.translated_text: another rule is that of local custom, wherever the debt is established.

children.text: dviguṇaṃ triguṇaṃ caiva tathānyasmiṃś caturguṇam
children.translated_text: In one place it stands at double, at triple, and in another at fourfold;

children.text: tathāṣṭaguṇam anyasmin deśe deśe 'vatiṣṭhate ||
children.translated_text: in yet another it stands at eightfold, according to each region.

children.text: hiraṇyadhānyavastrāṇāṃ vṛddhir dvitricaturguṇā
children.translated_text: The interest on gold, grain, and cloth is twofold, threefold, and fourfold;

children.text: ghṛtasyāṣṭaguṇā vṛddhiḥ strīpaśūnāṃ ca saṃtatiḥ ||
children.translated_text: the interest on ghee is eightfold, and for women and livestock it is the offspring.

children.text: sūtrakarpāsakiṇvānāṃ trapuṣaḥ sīsakasya ca
children.translated_text: For thread, cotton, ferment, tin, and lead,

children.text: āyudhānāṃ ca sarveṣāṃ carmaṇas tāmralohayoḥ ||
children.translated_text: and for all weapons, leather, copper, and iron,

children.text: anyeṣāṃ caiva sarveṣām iṣṭakānāṃ tathaiva ca
children.translated_text: and indeed for all other things, and likewise for bricks,

children.text: akṣayyā vṛddhir eteṣāṃ manur āha prajāpatiḥ ||
children.translated_text: the interest is inexhaustible; so said <s>Manu</s>, <s>Prajāpati</s>.

children.text: tailānāṃ caiva sarveṣāṃ madyānāṃ madhusarpiṣām
children.translated_text: For all oils, and for liquors, honey, and ghee,

children.text: vṛddhir aṣṭaguṇā jñeyā guḍasya lavaṇasya ca ||
children.translated_text: and for jaggery and salt, the interest should be known as eightfold.

children.text: na vṛddhiḥ prītidattānāṃ syād anākāritā kvacit
children.translated_text: There should never be interest on things given out of affection when it has not been stipulated;

children.text: anākāritam apy ūrdhvaṃ vatsarārdhād vivardhate ||
children.translated_text: even when not stipulated, after half a year it increases thereafter.

children.text: eṣa vṛddhividhiḥ proktaḥ prativṛddhasya dharmataḥ
children.translated_text: This rule of interest has been stated according to dharma for a debt that has increased.

children.text: vṛddhis tu yoktā dhānyānāṃ vārddhuṣyaṃ tad udāhṛtam ||
children.translated_text: But the increase applicable to grain is called <s>vārddhuṣya</s> (interest-taking).

children.text: āpadaṃ nistared vaiśyaḥ kāmaṃ vārddhuṣakarmaṇā
children.translated_text: A vaiśya may indeed get through distress by the practice of <s>vārddhuṣa</s> (lending at interest),

children.text: āpatsv api hi kaṣṭāsu brāhmaṇasya na vārddhuṣam ||
children.translated_text: but even in severe emergencies <s>vārddhuṣa</s> is not for a brāhmaṇa.

children.text: brāhmaṇasya tu yad deyaṃ sānvayasya na cāsti saḥ
children.translated_text: But what is to be given to a brāhmaṇa, if he is no longer there though he has lineage,

children.text: svakulyasyāsya nivapet tadabhāve 'sya bandhuṣu ||
children.translated_text: one should deposit with a member of his own family; failing that, among his kinsmen.

children.text: yadā tu na svakulyāḥ syur na ca saṃbandhibāndhavāḥ
children.translated_text: But when there are no members of his own family, nor relatives and kinsmen,

children.text: tadā dadyāt svajātibhyas teṣv asatsv apsu nikṣipet ||
children.translated_text: then one should give it to people of his own caste; if they are absent, one should cast it into the waters.

children.text: gṛhītvopagataṃ dadyād ṛṇikāyodayaṃ dhanī
children.translated_text: The creditor, having received what has been brought, should give the debtor an acknowledgment,

children.text: adadad yācyamānas tu śeṣahānim avāpnuyāt ||
children.translated_text: but if he does not give it when requested, he incurs the loss of the balance.

children.text: lekhyaṃ dadyād ṛṇe śuddhe tadabhāve pratiśravam
children.translated_text: When the debt is cleared, he should give a written document; in its absence, an oral acknowledgment.

children.text: dhanikarṇikayor evaṃ viśuddhiḥ syāt parasparam ||
children.translated_text: In this way there is mutual clearance between creditor and debtor.

children.text: viśrambhahetū dvāv atra pratibhūr ādhir eva ca
children.translated_text: There are two grounds of trust in this matter: a <s>pratibhū</s> (guarantor) and an <s>ādhi</s> (pledge).

children.text: likhitaṃ sākṣiṇaś ca dve pramāṇe vyaktikārake ||
children.translated_text: A written document and witnesses are the two proofs that make the matter clear.

children.text: upasthānāya dānāya pratyayāya tathaiva ca
children.translated_text: For producing a person, for payment, and likewise for assurance,

children.text: trividhaḥ pratibhūr dṛṣṭas triṣv evārtheṣu sūribhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: the guarantor is seen by the wise as threefold, in just these three matters.

children.text: ṛṇiṣv apratikurvatsu pratyaye vā vivādite
children.translated_text: When debtors do not make repayment, or when the assurance is disputed,

children.text: pratibhūs tad ṛṇaṃ dadyād anupasthāpayaṃs tathā ||
children.translated_text: the guarantor should pay that debt, and likewise when he does not produce the debtor.

children.text: bahavaś cet pratibhuvo dadyus te 'rthaṃ yathākṛtam
children.translated_text: If there are many guarantors, they should pay the sum according to what was agreed.

children.text: arthe 'viśeṣite hy eṣu dhaninaś chandataḥ kriyā ||
children.translated_text: For when the amount has not been specified among them, action is at the creditor's choice.

children.text: yaṃ cārthaṃ pratibhūr dadyād dhanikenopapīḍitaḥ
children.translated_text: And whatever sum a guarantor pays, being pressed by the creditor,

children.text: ṛṇikas taṃ pratibhuve dviguṇaṃ pratipādayet ||
children.translated_text: the debtor must hand that over to the guarantor in double amount.

children.text: adhikriyata ity ādhiḥ sa vijñeyo dvilakṣaṇaḥ
children.translated_text: Because it is placed under authority, it is called an <s>ādhi</s> (pledge); it should be known as twofold in character:

children.text: kṛtakālopaneyaś ca yāvaddeyodyatas tathā ||
children.translated_text: one to be recovered at an appointed time, and one standing until what is owed is paid.

children.text: sa punar dvividhaḥ prokto gopyo bhogyas tathaiva ca
children.translated_text: That again is said to be of two kinds: one to be kept safe, and one to be used.

children.text: pratidānaṃ tathaivāsya lābhahānir viparyaye ||
children.translated_text: Its return is likewise; in the contrary case there is gain or loss.

children.text: pramādād dhaninas tadvad ādhau vikṛtim āgate
children.translated_text: Likewise, when a pledge has undergone damage through the creditor's negligence,

children.text: vinaṣṭe mūlanāśaḥ syād daivarājakṛtād ṛte ||
children.translated_text: if it is destroyed, the principal is lost, except when the loss is caused by fate or the king.

children.text: rakṣyamāṇo 'pi yatrādhiḥ kāleneyād asāratām
children.translated_text: Where a pledge, even though being protected, becomes worthless over time,

children.text: ādhir anyo 'dhikartavyo deyaṃ vā dhanine dhanam ||
children.translated_text: another pledge should be assigned, or the money should be paid to the creditor.

children.text: atha śaktivihīnaḥ syād ṛṇī kālaviparyayāt
children.translated_text: But if the debtor has become without means because circumstances have changed,

children.text: śakyaprekṣam ṛṇaṃ dāpyaḥ kāle kāle yathodayam ||
children.translated_text: he should be made to pay the debt according to his ability, from time to time, as interest accrues.

children.text: śakto vā yadi daurātmyān na dadyād dhanine dhanam
children.translated_text: Or if he is able, but out of wickedness does not give the money to the creditor,

children.text: rājñā dāpayitavyaḥ syād gṛhītvāṃśaṃ tu viṃśakam ||
children.translated_text: he should be made to pay by the king, after the king has taken a twentieth share.

children.text: naśyed ṛṇaparīmāṇaṃ kāleneharṇikasya cet
