children.translated_text: If the amount of a debt has been lost with time in the debtor's case,

children.text: jātisaṃjñādhivāsānām āgamo lekhyataḥ smṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: information about caste, name, and residence is remembered as coming from the written document.

children.text: lekhyaṃ tu dvividhaṃ jñeyaṃ svahastānyakṛtaṃ tathā
children.translated_text: A written document should be known as twofold: made in one's own hand and made by another.

children.text: asākṣimat sākṣimac ca siddhir deśasthites tayoḥ ||
children.translated_text: It may be without witnesses or with witnesses; the validity of those two depends on local usage.

children.text: deśācārāviruddhaṃ yad vyaktādhikṛtalakṣaṇam
children.translated_text: That which is not contrary to local custom and has the marks of a clear authorized transaction,

children.text: tat pramāṇaṃ smṛtaṃ lekhyam aviluptakramākṣaram ||
children.translated_text: that written document, with its sequence and letters unimpaired, is remembered as proof.

children.text: mattābhiyuktastrībālabalātkārakṛtaṃ ca yat
children.translated_text: What is made by an intoxicated person, an accused person, a woman, a child, or by force,

children.text: tad apramāṇakaraṇaṃ bhītopadhikṛtaṃ tathā ||
children.translated_text: that is not a valid instrument of proof; so too what is made through fear or deceit.

children.text: mṛtāḥ syuḥ sākṣiṇo yatra dhanikarṇikalekhakāḥ
children.translated_text: Where the witnesses, the creditor, the debtor, and the scribe are dead,

children.text: tad apy apārthaṃ likhitam ṛte tv ādheḥ sthirāśrayāt ||
children.translated_text: that written document too is without purpose, except in the case of a pledge with a stable basis.

children.text: ādhir yo dvividhaḥ prokto jaṅgamaḥ sthāvaras tathā
children.translated_text: The pledge that has been said to be twofold is movable and immovable.

children.text: siddhir atrobhayasyāsya bhogo yady asti nānyathā ||
children.translated_text: Here the validity of both of these exists if there is possession and use, not otherwise.

children.text: darśitaṃ pratikālaṃ yac chrāvitaṃ śrāvitaṃ ca yat
children.translated_text: A document that has been shown at each proper time and has been read out repeatedly

children.text: lekhyaṃ sidhyati sarvatra mṛteṣv api hi sākṣiṣu ||
children.translated_text: is valid everywhere, even when the witnesses have died.

children.text: aśrutārtham adṛṣṭārthaṃ vyavahārārtham eva ca
children.translated_text: A document whose matter was not heard, whose matter was not seen, or that was made only for litigation

children.text: na lekhyaṃ siddhim āpnoti jīvatsv api hi sākṣiṣu ||
children.translated_text: does not attain validity, even while the witnesses are alive.

children.text: lekhye deśāntaranyaste dagdhe durlikhite hṛte
children.translated_text: When a document is deposited in another country, burnt, badly written, or stolen,

children.text: satas tatkālakaraṇam asato dṛṣṭadarśanam ||
children.translated_text: if it exists, a new one should be made at that time; if it does not exist, there should be proof by those who saw it.

children.text: yasmin syāt saṃśayo lekhye bhūtābhūtakṛte kvacit
children.translated_text: When there is doubt about some document, whether it was actually made or not,

children.text: tatsvahastakriyācihnaprāptiyuktibhir uddharet ||
children.translated_text: one should establish it by handwriting, execution, marks, possession, and reasoning.

children.text: lekhyaṃ yac cānyanāmāṅkaṃ hetvantarakṛtaṃ bhavet
children.translated_text: And a document marked with another name, or made for another reason,

children.text: vipratyaye parīkṣyaṃ tat saṃbandhāgamahetubhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: should, when disputed, be examined by grounds of connection, provenance, and purpose.

children.text: likhitaṃ likhitenaiva sākṣimat sākṣibhir haret
children.translated_text: One should rebut a written document only by a written document, and a witnessed one by witnesses.

children.text: sākṣibhyo likhitaṃ śreyo likhitena tu sākṣiṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Written evidence is better than witnesses; but witnesses prevail by means of writing.

children.text: chinnabhinnahṛtonmṛṣṭanaṣṭadurlikhiteṣu ca
children.translated_text: In cases where it is cut, torn, stolen, erased, lost, or badly written,

children.text: kartavyam anyal lekhyaṃ syād eṣa lekhyavidhiḥ smṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: another document should be made; this is remembered as the rule concerning documents.

children.text: saṃdigdheṣu tu kāryeṣu dvayor vivadamānayoḥ
children.translated_text: But in doubtful cases involving two disputing parties,

children.text: dṛṣṭaśrutānubhūtatvāt sākṣibhyo vyaktidarśanam ||
children.translated_text: clarity is obtained from witnesses, because they have seen, heard, or experienced the matter.

children.text: samakṣadarśanāt sākṣī vijñeyaḥ śrotracakṣuṣoḥ
children.translated_text: A witness is to be understood from direct perception by the ear and the eye.

children.text: śrotrasya yat paro brūte cakṣuṣaḥ kāyakarma yat ||
children.translated_text: What another says belongs to the ear; bodily action belongs to the eye.

children.text: ekādaśavidhaḥ sākṣī sa tu dṛṣṭo manīṣibhiḥ
children.translated_text: The witness, however, has been regarded by the wise as elevenfold.

children.text: kṛtaḥ pañcavidhas teṣāṃ ṣaḍvidho 'kṛta ucyate ||
children.translated_text: Of these, the appointed witness is fivefold; the unappointed is said to be sixfold.

children.text: likhitaḥ smāritaś caiva yadṛcchābhijña eva ca
children.translated_text: The written witness, the reminded witness, and the one who happens to know by chance,

children.text: gūḍhaś cottarasākṣī ca sākṣī pañcavidhaḥ smṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the hidden witness and the subsequent witness: the witness is remembered as fivefold.

children.text: akṛtaḥ ṣaḍvidhaś cāpi sūribhiḥ parikīrtitaḥ
children.translated_text: And the unappointed witness also has been declared by learned men to be sixfold:

children.text: grāmaś ca prāḍvivākaś ca rājā ca vyavahāriṇām ||
children.translated_text: the village, the chief judge, and the king in the affairs of litigants;

children.text: kāryeṣv abhyantaro yaḥ syād arthinā prahitaś ca yaḥ
children.translated_text: one who is privy to the matters, and one who has been sent by the claimant;

children.text: kulaṃ kulavivādeṣu bhaveyus te 'pi sākṣiṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and the family in family disputes: these too may be witnesses.

children.text: kulīnā ṛjavaḥ śuddhā janmataḥ karmato 'rthataḥ
children.translated_text: They should be well-born, upright, and pure by birth, conduct, and wealth.

children.text: tryavarāḥ sākṣiṇo 'nindyāḥ śucayaḥ syuḥ subuddhayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Witnesses should be no fewer than three, blameless, clean, and intelligent.

children.text: brāhmaṇāḥ kṣatriyā vaiśyāḥ śūdrā ye cāpy aninditāḥ
children.translated_text: Brāhmaṇas, kṣatriyas, vaiśyas, and śūdras, if they too are blameless, may serve as witnesses.

children.text: prativarṇaṃ bhaveyus te sarve sarveṣu vā punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: They should belong to the corresponding <s>varṇa</s> (social class), or again all may serve in all cases.

children.text: śreṇīṣu śreṇipuruṣāḥ sveṣu vargeṣu vargiṇaḥ
children.translated_text: Among guilds, guild-men should be witnesses; among their own groups, men of those groups should be witnesses.

children.text: bahirvāsiṣu bāhyāś ca striyaḥ strīṣu ca sākṣiṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For those living outside, outsiders should be witnesses, and for women, women should be witnesses.

children.text: śreṇyādiṣu tu vargeṣu kaścic ced dveṣyatām iyāt
children.translated_text: But if, in groups such as guilds, someone should incur hostility,

children.text: tebhya eva na sākṣī syād dveṣṭāraḥ sarva eva te ||
children.translated_text: no witness should come from those very people, for they are all haters of him.

children.text: asākṣy api hi śāstreṣu dṛṣṭaḥ pañcavidho budhaiḥ
children.translated_text: In the <s>śāstras</s>, too, non-witnesshood has been seen by the wise as fivefold:

children.text: vacanād doṣato bhedāt svayamukter mṛtāntaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: by textual declaration, by fault, by discrepancy, by self-declaration, and by the death of the other party.

children.text: śrotriyādyā vacanataḥ stenādyā doṣadarśanāt
children.translated_text: <s>Śrotriyas</s> and the like are excluded by declaration; thieves and the like by the perception of fault.

children.text: bhedād vipratipattiḥ syād vivāde yatra sākṣiṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: There is exclusion by discrepancy where, in a dispute, the witnesses contradict one another.

children.text: svayamukter anirdiṣṭaḥ svayam evaitya yo vadet
children.translated_text: By self-declaration, an unappointed man is meant, one who comes by himself and speaks.

children.text: mṛtāntaro 'rthini prete mumūrṣuśrāvitād ṛte ||
children.translated_text: The case after death is when the claimant has died, except for what was heard from one about to die.

children.text: śrotriyās tāpasā vṛddhā ye ca pravrajitā narāḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Śrotriyas</s>, ascetics, old men, and men who have renounced the world

children.text: asākṣiṇas te vacanān nātra hetur udāhṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: are non-witnesses by declaration; no reason is stated here for this.

children.text: stenāḥ sāhasikāś caṇḍāḥ kitavā vadhakās tathā
children.translated_text: Thieves, violent offenders, fierce men, gamblers, and killers likewise

children.text: asākṣiṇas te duṣṭatvāt teṣu satyaṃ na vidyate ||
children.translated_text: are non-witnesses because they are corrupt; truth is not found in them.

children.text: rājñā parigṛhīteṣu sākṣiṣv ekārthaniścaye
children.translated_text: When witnesses have been accepted by the king for the determination of a single matter,

children.text: vacanaṃ yatra bhidyate te syur bhedād asākṣiṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: if their statement differs, they become non-witnesses because of discrepancy.

children.text: anirdiṣṭas tu sākṣitve svayam evaitya yo vadet
children.translated_text: But one who, though not appointed as a witness, comes by himself and speaks

children.text: sūcīty uktaḥ sa śāstreṣu na sa sākṣitvam arhati ||
children.translated_text: is called a <s>sūcī</s> (informer) in the <s>śāstras</s>; he is not fit for witnesshood.

children.text: yo 'rthaḥ śrāvayitavyaḥ syāt tasminn asati cārthini
children.translated_text: When the matter was one that should have been made known, but the claimant is no longer present,

children.text: kva tad vadatu sākṣitvam ity asākṣī mṛtāntaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: where can that testimony be stated? Thus the after-death witness is a non-witness.

children.text: dvayor vivadator arthe dvayoḥ satsu ca sākṣiṣu
children.translated_text: When two men are disputing over a matter, and witnesses are present for both,

children.text: pūrvapakṣo bhaved yasya bhaveyus tasya sākṣiṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the witnesses should belong to the one whose <s>pūrvapakṣa</s> (initial claim) stands.

children.text: ādharyaṃ pūrvapakṣasya yasminn arthe vaśād bhavet
children.translated_text: But in a matter where the support of the initial claim depends on possession,

children.text: praṣṭavyāḥ sākṣiṇas tatra vivāde prativādinaḥ ||
children.translated_text: there, in the dispute, the witnesses of the defendant are to be questioned.

children.text: na pareṇa samuddiṣṭam upeyāt sākṣiṇaṃ rahaḥ
children.translated_text: One must not approach in private a witness named by the other party,

children.text: bhedayet taṃ na cānyena hīyetaivaṃ samācaran ||
children.translated_text: nor should he make that witness change through another; acting in this way, he would lose his case.

children.text: sākṣy uddiṣṭo yadi preyād gacched vāpi digantaram
children.translated_text: If an appointed witness should die or go away to a distant region,

children.text: tacchrotāraḥ pramāṇaṃ syuḥ pramāṇaṃ hy uttarakriyā ||
children.translated_text: those who heard him may be evidence, for the subsequent procedure is valid evidence.

children.text: sudīrgheṇāpi kālena likhitaṃ siddhim āpnuyāt
children.translated_text: Even after a very long time, a written document may attain validity.

children.text: jānatā cātmanā lekhyaṃ ajānānastu lekhayet ||
children.translated_text: One who knows how should write the document himself; one who does not know should have it written.

children.text: siddhir uktāṣṭamād varṣāt smāritasyeha sākṣiṇaḥ
children.translated_text: For a witness who has been reminded, validity is said here to extend up to the eighth year.

children.text: ā pañcamāt tathā siddhir yadṛcchopagatasya tu ||
children.translated_text: Likewise, for one who has arrived by chance, validity extends up to the fifth year.

children.text: ā tṛtīyāt tathā varṣāt siddhir gūḍhasya sākṣiṇaḥ
children.translated_text: Likewise, for a hidden witness, validity extends up to the third year.

children.text: ā vai saṃvatsarāt siddhiṃ vadanty uttarasākṣiṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For later witnesses, they declare validity to extend up to one year.

children.text: athavā kālaniyamo na dṛṣṭaḥ sākṣiṇaṃ prati
children.translated_text: Or else no fixed rule of time is observed with regard to a witness.

children.text: smṛtyapekṣaṃ hi sākṣitvam āhuḥ śāstravido janāḥ ||
children.translated_text: For those who know the <s>śāstras</s> say that witnesshood depends on memory.

children.text: yasya nopahatā puṃsaḥ smṛtiḥ śrotraṃ ca nityaśaḥ
children.translated_text: A man whose memory and hearing are not continually impaired

children.text: sudīrgheṇāpi kālena sa sākṣī sākṣyam arhati ||
children.translated_text: is fit to give testimony as a witness even after a very long time.

children.text: asākṣipratyayās tv anye ṣaḍvivādāḥ prakīrtitāḥ
children.translated_text: Other disputes, six in number, are declared to be established without witnesses.

children.text: lakṣaṇāny eva sākṣitvaṃ eṣām āhur manīṣiṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The wise say that their marks themselves constitute witnesshood for them.

children.text: ulkāhasto 'gnido jñeyaḥ śastrapāṇis tu ghātakaḥ
children.translated_text: A man with a firebrand in his hand should be known as an arsonist; one with a weapon in hand as a killer.

children.text: keśākeśigṛhītaś ca yugapat pāradārikaḥ ||
children.translated_text: One seized hair-to-hair at the same time should be known as an adulterer.

children.text: kuddālapāṇir vijñeyaḥ setubhettā samīpagaḥ
children.translated_text: One with a spade in his hand, standing nearby, should be known as a breaker of an embankment.

children.text: tathā kuṭhārapāṇiś ca vanachettā prakīrtitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Likewise, one with an axe in his hand is declared to be a cutter of the forest.

children.text: abhyagracihno vijñeyo daṇḍapāruṣyakṛn naraḥ
children.translated_text: A man bearing fresh marks should be known as one who has committed assault with a staff.

children.text: asākṣipratyayā hy ete pāruṣye tu parīkṣaṇam ||
children.translated_text: These indeed are matters established without witnesses; but in assault there must be examination.

children.text: kaścit kṛtvātmanaś cihnaṃ dveṣāt param upadravet
children.translated_text: For someone might make marks on himself and, out of hatred, harass another man.

children.text: hetvarthagatisāmarthyais tatra yuktaṃ parīkṣaṇam ||
children.translated_text: There examination is proper, by motives, facts, course of events, and capability.

children.text: nārthasaṃbandhino nāptā na sahāyā na vairiṇaḥ
children.translated_text: Those connected with the matter, close associates, helpers, and enemies

children.text: na dṛṣṭadoṣāḥ praṣṭavyā na vyādhyārtā na dūṣitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: should not be questioned, nor those seen to have faults, nor the disease-afflicted, nor the tainted.

children.text: dāsanaikṛtikāśraddhavṛddhastrībālacākrikāḥ
children.translated_text: Slaves, cheats, unbelievers, old men, women, children, and cartmen,

children.text: mattonmattapramattārtakitavagrāmayājakāḥ ||
children.translated_text: drunkards, madmen, the careless, the distressed, gamblers, and village priests,

children.text: mahāpathikasāmudravaṇikpravrajitāturāḥ
children.translated_text: long-road travelers, seafaring men, merchants, renouncers, and the sick,

children.text: lubdhakaśrotriyācārahīnaklībakuśīlavāḥ ||
children.translated_text: hunters, <s>śrotriyas</s>, those without proper conduct, impotent men, and men of bad conduct,

children.text: nāstikavrātyadārāgnityāgino 'yājyayājakāḥ
children.translated_text: atheists, <s>vrātyas</s> (uninitiated outsiders), men who have abandoned wife and sacred fire, and priests for those unfit to sacrifice,

children.text: ekasthālīsahāyāricarajñātisanābhayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: common-table companions, allies, agents of enemies, relatives, and agnates,

children.text: prāgdṛṣṭadoṣaśailūṣaviṣajīvyahituṇḍikāḥ
children.translated_text: those whose fault was previously seen, actors, poison-dealers, and snake-charmers,

children.text: garadāgnidakīnāśaśūdrāputropapātikāḥ ||
children.translated_text: poisoners, arsonists, ploughmen, <s>śūdras</s>, sonless men, and those guilty of minor transgressions,

children.text: klāntasāhasikaśrāntanirdhanāntyāvasāyinaḥ
children.translated_text: the exhausted, violent offenders, the weary, the poor, and those following the lowest occupations,

children.text: bhinnavṛttāsamāvṛttajaḍatailikamūlikāḥ ||
children.translated_text: those of broken conduct, those who have not completed their studentship, dullards, oilmen, and root-sellers,

children.text: bhūtāviṣṭanṛpadviṣṭavarṣanakṣatrasūcakāḥ
children.translated_text: the possessed, those hated by the king, and predictors of rain and lunar mansions,

children.text: aghaśaṃsyātmavikretṛhīnāṅgabhagavṛttayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: evil speakers, self-sellers, men with defective limbs, and those who live by sexual commerce,

children.text: kunakhī śyāvadan śvitrimitradhruk śaṭhaśauṇḍikāḥ
children.translated_text: men with bad nails, men with discolored teeth, lepers, betrayers of friends, rogues, and liquor sellers,

children.text: aindrajālikalubdhograśreṇīgaṇavirodhinaḥ ||
children.translated_text: magicians, greedy men, fierce men, and opponents of guilds and corporations,

children.text: vadhakṛc citrakṛn maṅkhaḥ patitaḥ kūṭakārakaḥ
children.translated_text: a killer, a painter, a wandering bard, a fallen man, and a forger,

children.text: kuhakaḥ pratyavasitas taskaro rājapūruṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: a deceiver, a relapsed offender, a thief, and a royal officer,

children.text: manuṣyaviṣaśastrāmbulavaṇāpūpavīrudhām
children.translated_text: a seller of humans, poison, weapons, water, salt, cakes, or plants,

children.text: vikretā brāhmaṇaś caiva dvijo vārdhuṣikaś ca yaḥ ||
children.translated_text: if he is a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, and also any twice-born man who is an usurer,

children.text: cyutaḥ svadharmāt kulikaḥ stāvako hīnasevakaḥ
children.translated_text: one fallen from his own <s>dharma</s>, an artisan, a panegyrist, and a servant of low people,

children.text: pitrā vivadamānaś ca bhedakṛc cety asākṣiṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: one who is disputing with his father, and a maker of division: these are non-witnesses.

children.text: asākṣiṇo ye nirdiṣṭā dāsanaikṛtikādayaḥ
children.translated_text: Those who have been specified as non-witnesses, beginning with slaves and cheats,

children.text: kāryagauravam āsādya bhaveyus te 'pi sākṣiṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: may themselves become witnesses when the gravity of the case requires it.

children.text: sāhaseṣu ca sarveṣu steyasaṃgrahaṇeṣu ca
children.translated_text: In all cases of violent crime, and in thefts and seizures,

children.text: pāruṣyayoś cāpy ubhayor na parīkṣeta sākṣiṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and also in both kinds of abuse, one should not scrutinize the witnesses.

children.text: teṣām api na bālaḥ syān naiko na strī na kūṭakṛt
children.translated_text: Even among them, however, there should be no child, no single witness, no woman, and no forger.

children.text: na bāndhavo na cārātir brūyus te sākṣyam anyathā ||
children.translated_text: Neither a relative nor an enemy should give testimony otherwise.

children.text: bālo 'jñānād asatyāt strī pāpābhyāsāc ca kūṭakṛt
children.translated_text: A child, through ignorance; a woman, through untruth; and a false witness, through practice in sin,

children.text: vibrūyād bāndhavaḥ snehād vairaniryātanād ariḥ ||
children.translated_text: may make a distorted statement; a relative does so from affection, an enemy from retaliation for enmity.

children.text: athavānumato yaḥ syād dvayor vivadamānayoḥ
children.translated_text: Or a person who has been approved by the two disputing parties

children.text: asākṣy eko 'pi sākṣitve praṣṭavyaḥ syāt sa saṃsadi ||
children.translated_text: should be questioned as a witness in the assembly, even if he is alone and otherwise not a witness.

children.text: yas tv ātmadoṣabhinnatvād asvastha iva lakṣyate
children.translated_text: But one who, because he is shaken by his own fault, appears as if unsettled,

children.text: sthānāt sthānāntaraṃ gacched ekaikaṃ copadhāvati ||
children.translated_text: moves from one place to another and approaches each person one by one,

children.text: kāsate 'nibhṛto 'kasmād abhīkṣṇaṃ niśvasaty api
children.translated_text: coughs restlessly for no reason and also sighs again and again,

children.text: bhūmiṃ likhati pādābhyāṃ bāhuvāso dhunoti ca ||
children.translated_text: scratches the ground with his feet and shakes his arms and garment,

children.text: bhidyate mukhavarṇo 'sya lalāṭaṃ svidyate tathā
children.translated_text: whose facial color changes and whose forehead likewise sweats,

children.text: śoṣam āgacchataś coṣṭhāv ūrdhvaṃ tiryak ca vīkṣate ||
children.translated_text: whose lips become dry, and who looks upward and sideways,

children.text: tvaramāṇa ivābaddham apṛṣṭo bahu bhāṣate
children.translated_text: who, as if in haste, speaks much incoherently without being asked,

children.text: kūṭasākṣī sa vijñeyas taṃ pāpaṃ vinayen nṛpaḥ ||
children.translated_text: should be known as a false witness; the king should punish that sinful man.

children.text: śrāvayitvā ca yo 'nyebhyaḥ sākṣitvaṃ tad vinihnute
children.translated_text: And one who, after making others hear that he is a witness, then denies that status

children.text: sa vineyo bhṛśataraṃ kūṭasākṣyadhiko hi saḥ ||
children.translated_text: should be punished much more severely, for he is worse than a false witness.

children.text: āhūya sākṣiṇaḥ pṛcchen niyamya śapathair bhṛśam
children.translated_text: Having summoned the witnesses, he should question them, firmly binding them by oaths,

children.text: samastān viditācārān vijñātārthān pṛthak pṛthak ||
children.translated_text: all together, their conduct known and the matter understood, and then separately one by one.

children.text: satyena śāpayed vipraṃ kṣatriyaṃ vāhanāyudhaiḥ
children.translated_text: He should put a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> under oath by truth, a <s>Kṣatriya</s> by vehicles and weapons,

children.text: gobījakāñcanair vaiśyaṃ śūdraṃ sarvais tu pātakaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: a <s>Vaiśya</s> by cattle, seed, and gold, but a <s>Śūdra</s> by all sins.

children.text: purāṇair dharmavacanaiḥ satyamāhātmyakīrtanaiḥ
children.translated_text: With ancient tales, sayings on <s>dharma</s>, and proclamations of the greatness of truth,

children.text: anṛtasyāpavādaiś ca bhṛśam uttrāsya sākṣiṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and with censures of falsehood, he should thoroughly frighten the witnesses.

children.text: nagno muṇḍaḥ kapālena bhikṣārthī kṣutpipāsitaḥ
children.translated_text: Naked, shaven-headed, with a skull-bowl, begging, hungry and thirsty,

children.text: dīnaḥ śatrugṛhaṃ gacched yaḥ sākṣyam anṛtaṃ vadet ||
children.translated_text: wretched, may the man who gives false testimony go to an enemy's house.

children.text: nagare pratiruddhaḥ san bahirdvāre bubhukṣitaḥ
children.translated_text: Shut out within a city, hungry at the outer gate,

children.text: amitrān bhūyaśaḥ paśyed yaḥ sākṣyam anṛtaṃ vadet ||
children.translated_text: may the man who gives false testimony see enemies again and again.

children.text: yāṃ rātrim adhivinnā strī yāṃ caivākṣaparājitaḥ
children.translated_text: The night that a superseded wife endures, and that which a man defeated at dice endures,

children.text: yāṃ ca bhārābhitaptāṅgo durvivaktā sa tāṃ vaset ||
children.translated_text: and that which a man whose limbs are oppressed by a burden endures, that night the wrongful speaker must pass.

children.text: sākṣī sākṣyasamuddeśe gokarṇaśithilaṃ caran
children.translated_text: A witness, when testimony is at issue, moving slackly like a cow's ear,

children.text: sahasraṃ vāruṇān pāśān ātmani pratimuñcati ||
children.translated_text: fastens upon himself a thousand nooses of <s>Varuṇa</s>.

children.text: tasya varṣaśate pūrṇe pāśam ekaṃ pramucyate
children.translated_text: When a hundred years have been completed for him, one noose is released;

children.text: evaṃ sa bandhanāt tasmān mucyate niyutāḥ samāḥ ||
children.translated_text: thus he is freed from that bondage only after ten thousand years.

children.text: yāvato bāndhavān yasmin hanti sākṣye 'nṛtaṃ vadan
children.translated_text: How many relatives a man destroys in a given testimony by speaking falsehood,

children.text: tāvataḥ saṃkhyayā tasmin śṛṇu saumyānupūrvaśaḥ ||
children.translated_text: hear their number in that case, good sir, in due order.

children.text: pañca paśvanṛte hanti daśa hanti gavānṛte
children.translated_text: By a lie about livestock he kills five; by a lie about cows he kills ten;

children.text: śatam aśvānṛte hanti sahasraṃ puruṣānṛte ||
children.translated_text: by a lie about horses he kills a hundred; by a lie about human beings, a thousand.

children.text: hanti jātān ajātāṃś ca hiraṇyārthe 'nṛtaṃ vadan
children.translated_text: Speaking falsehood for the sake of gold, he kills both those already born and those unborn;

children.text: sarvaṃ bhūmyanṛte hanti mā sma bhūmyanṛtaṃ vadīḥ ||
children.translated_text: by a lie about land he kills everything. Never speak falsely about land.

children.text: ekam evādvitīyaṃ tat prāhuḥ pāvanam ātmanaḥ
children.translated_text: That one thing alone, without a second, they call the purifier of the self:

children.text: satyaṃ svargasya sopānaṃ pārāvārasya naur iva ||
children.translated_text: truth is the stairway to heaven, like a boat across the ocean.

children.text: aśvamedhasahasraṃ ca satyaṃ ca tulayā dhṛtam
children.translated_text: A thousand <s>aśvamedha</s> sacrifices and truth, when placed in a balance,

children.text: aśvamedhasahasrāddhi satyam eva viśiṣyate ||
children.translated_text: truth alone is superior to a thousand <s>aśvamedha</s> sacrifices.

children.text: varaṃ kūpaśatād vāpi varaṃ vāpīśatāt kratuḥ
children.translated_text: Better than a hundred wells is a reservoir; better than a hundred reservoirs is a sacrifice;

children.text: varaṃ kratuśatāt putraḥ satyaṃ putraśatād varam ||
children.translated_text: better than a hundred sacrifices is a son; truth is better than a hundred sons.

children.text: bhūr dhārayati satyena satyenodeti bhāskaraḥ
children.translated_text: The earth is upheld by truth; by truth the sun rises;

children.text: satyena vāyuḥ pavate satyenāpaḥ sravanti ca ||
children.translated_text: by truth the wind blows, and by truth the waters flow.

children.text: satyam eva paraṃ dānaṃ satyam eva paraṃ tapaḥ
children.translated_text: Truth alone is the highest gift; truth alone is the highest austerity;

children.text: satyam eva paro dharmo lokānām iti naḥ śrutam ||
children.translated_text: truth alone is the highest <s>dharma</s> of the worlds: so we have heard.

children.text: satyaṃ devāḥ samāsena manuṣyās tv anṛtaṃ smṛtam
children.translated_text: In brief, the gods are truth, while human beings are remembered as falsehood.

children.text: ihaiva tasya devatvaṃ yasya satye sthitā matiḥ ||
children.translated_text: He whose mind is fixed on truth has divinity right here.

children.text: satyaṃ brūhy anṛtaṃ tyaktvā satyena svargam eṣyasi
children.translated_text: Speak truth, abandoning falsehood; through truth you will reach heaven.

children.text: uktvānṛtaṃ mahāghoraṃ narakaṃ pratipatsyate ||
children.translated_text: Having spoken falsehood, you will enter a very terrible hell.

children.text: nirayeṣu ca te śaśvaj jihvām utkṛtya dāruṇāḥ
children.translated_text: And in the hells, after cutting out your tongue forever, the dreadful,

children.text: asibhiḥ śātayiṣyanti balino yamakiṃkarāḥ ||
children.translated_text: powerful servants of <s>Yama</s> will slice it with swords.

children.text: śūlair bhetsyanti cākruddhāḥ krośantam aparāyaṇam
children.translated_text: Angry, they will pierce you with spears as you cry out, with no refuge,

children.text: avākśirasam utkṣipya kṣepsyanty agnihradeṣu ca ||
children.translated_text: and, lifting you head downward, they will throw you into lakes of fire.

children.text: anubhūya ca duḥkhās tāś ciraṃ narakavedanāḥ
children.translated_text: And after experiencing those sufferings, the pains of hell, for a long time,

children.text: iha yāsyasy abhavyāsu gṛdhrakākādiyoniṣu ||
children.translated_text: here you will pass into inauspicious births such as vultures and crows.

children.text: jñātvaitān anṛte doṣāñ jñātvā satye ca sadguṇān
children.translated_text: Knowing these faults in falsehood and knowing the good qualities in truth,

children.text: satyaṃ vadoddharātmānaṃ mātmānaṃ pātayiṣyasi ||
children.translated_text: speak truth and raise yourself up; do not cast yourself down.

children.text: na bāndhavā na suhṛdo na dhanāni mahānty api
children.translated_text: Neither relatives, nor friends, nor even great riches

children.text: alaṃ tārayituṃ śaktās tamasy ugre nimajjataḥ ||
children.translated_text: are able to rescue one who is sinking in terrible darkness.

children.text: pitaras tv avalambante tvayi sākṣitvam āgate
children.translated_text: But the ancestors depend upon you when you have come to be a witness,

children.text: tārayiṣyati kiṃvāsmān ātmānaṃ pātayiṣyati ||
children.translated_text: thinking, "Will he rescue us, or will he cast himself down?"

children.text: satyam ātmā manuṣyasya satye sarvaṃ pratiṣṭhitam
children.translated_text: Truth is a human being's self; everything is established in truth.

children.text: sarvathaivātmanātmānaṃ śreyasā yojayiṣyasi ||
children.translated_text: In every way, by yourself, you should join yourself to what is best.

children.text: yāṃ ca rātrim ajaniṣṭhā yāṃ rātriṃ ca mariṣyasi
children.translated_text: The night on which you were born and the night on which you will die:

children.text: vṛthā tadantaraṃ te syāt kuryāś cet satyam anyathā ||
children.translated_text: the time between them would be wasted for you, if you should distort truth.

children.text: nāsti satyāt paro dharmo nānṛtāt pātakaṃ param
children.translated_text: There is no <s>dharma</s> higher than truth, and no sin greater than falsehood;

children.text: sākṣidharme viśeṣeṇa satyam eva vadet tataḥ ||
children.translated_text: therefore, especially in the <s>dharma</s> of witnesses, one should speak truth alone.

children.text: yaḥ parārthe praharati svāṃ vācaṃ puruṣādhamaḥ
children.translated_text: The lowest man who violates his own speech for another's sake:

children.text: ātmārthe kiṃ na kuryāt sa pāpo narakanirbhayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: what would that sinner, unafraid of hell, not do for his own sake?

children.text: arthā vai vāci niyatā vāṅmūlā vāgviniḥsṛtāḥ
children.translated_text: Matters are indeed fixed in speech; rooted in speech, they issue from speech.

children.text: yo hy etāṃ stenayed vācaṃ sa sarvasteyakṛn naraḥ ||
children.translated_text: For the man who steals this speech commits every theft.

children.text: sākṣivipratipattau tu pramāṇaṃ bahavo yataḥ
children.translated_text: But when witnesses contradict one another, the greater number is the authority.

children.text: tatsāmye śucayo grāhyās tatsāmye smṛtimattarāḥ ||
children.translated_text: When there is equality in that respect, pure persons should be accepted; when there is equality in that too, those with stronger recollection.

children.text: smṛtimatsākṣisāmyaṃ tu vivāde yatra dṛśyate
children.translated_text: But where, in a dispute, equality among witnesses with good memory is seen,

children.text: sūkṣmatvāt sākṣidharmasya sākṣyaṃ vyāvartate punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: because the duty of a witness is subtle, the testimony is again set aside.

children.text: nirdiṣṭeṣv arthajāteṣu sākṣī cet sākṣyam āgataḥ
children.translated_text: If a witness has come to testify about specified classes of matters,

children.text: na brūyād akṣarasamaṃ na tan nigaditaṃ bhavet ||
children.translated_text: but does not state them exactly syllable for syllable, that is not considered to have been stated.

children.text: deśakālavayodravyapramāṇākṛtijātiṣu
children.translated_text: Where there is disagreement about place, time, age, object, measure, shape, or class,

children.text: yatra vipratipattiḥ syāt sākṣyaṃ tad asad ucyate ||
children.translated_text: that testimony is said to be invalid.

children.text: ūnam abhyadhikaṃ cārthaṃ prabrūyur yatra sākṣiṇaḥ
children.translated_text: Where witnesses state the matter as less or greater than it is,

children.text: tad apy anuktaṃ vijñeyam eṣa sākṣyavidhiḥ smṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: that too should be understood as unstated; this is remembered as the rule of testimony.

children.text: pramādād dhanino yatra na syāl lekhyaṃ na sākṣiṇaḥ
children.translated_text: Where, through the creditor's negligence, there is neither document nor witnesses,

children.text: arthaṃ cāpahnuyād vādī tatroktas trividho vidhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: and the litigant denies the claim, a threefold procedure is prescribed there.

children.text: codanā pratikālaṃ ca yuktileśas tathaiva ca
children.translated_text: It is questioning at intervals, and likewise a trace of reasoning;

children.text: tṛtīyaḥ śapathaś coktas tair evaṃ sādhayet kramāt ||
children.translated_text: the third is said to be the oath; by these, in order, one should establish the case.

children.text: abhīkṣṇaṃ codyamāno yaḥ pratihanyān na tadvacaḥ
children.translated_text: The man who, when repeatedly questioned, does not refute that statement,

children.text: tricatuḥpañcakṛtvo vā parato 'rthaṃ tam āvahet ||
children.translated_text: after three, four, or five times, should thereafter be made to bear that claim.

children.text: codanāpratighāte tu yuktileśais tam anviyāt
children.translated_text: But if he resists the questioning, one should pursue him with traces of reasoning,

children.text: deśakālārthasaṃbandhaparimāṇakriyādibhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: through place, time, connection with the matter, amount, action, and the like.

children.text: yuktiṣv apy asamarthāsu śapathair enam ardayet
children.translated_text: When even arguments are ineffectual, one should press him with oaths,

children.text: arthakālabalāpekṣam agnyambusukṛtādibhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: using fire, water, meritorious acts, and the like, according to the value involved, the time, and the person's strength.

children.text: dīptāgnir yaṃ na dahati yam antardhārayanty āpaḥ
children.translated_text: He whom blazing fire does not burn and whom the waters hold within

children.text: sa taraty abhiśāpaṃ taṃ kilbiṣī syād viparyaye ||
children.translated_text: passes through that imprecation; in the opposite case he is guilty.

children.text: strīṇāṃ śīlābhiyogeṣu steyasāhasayor api
children.translated_text: In accusations concerning the chastity of women, and also in theft and violent assault,

children.text: eṣa eva vidhir dṛṣṭaḥ sarvārthāpahnaveṣu ca ||
children.translated_text: this very rule is observed, and also in all denials of property.

children.text: śapathā hy api devānām ṛṣīṇām api ca smṛtāḥ
children.translated_text: For oaths are remembered even among gods and also among seers;

children.text: vasiṣṭhaḥ śapathaṃ śepe yātudhāne tu śaṅkitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> swore an oath when he was suspected of being a yātudhāna.

children.text: saptarṣayas tathendrāya puṣkarārthe samāgatāḥ
children.translated_text: Likewise the <s>Saptarṣis</s>, having assembled before <s>Indra</s> in the matter of the lotuses,

children.text: śepuḥ śapatham avyagrāḥ parasparaviśuddhaye ||
children.translated_text: calmly swore an oath for mutual purification.

children.text: ayuktaṃ sāhasaṃ kṛtvā pratyāpattiṃ bhajeta yaḥ
children.translated_text: Whoever, after committing an improper act of violence, resorts to confession,

children.text: brūyāt svayaṃ vā sadasi tasyārdhavinayaḥ smṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: or himself declares it in the court, is remembered as owing half the fine.

children.text: gūhamānas tu daurātmyād yadi pāpaṃ sa jīyate
children.translated_text: But if, from wickedness, he conceals the evil and is defeated,

children.text: sabhyāś cātra na tuṣyanti tīvro daṇḍaś ca pātyate ||
children.translated_text: the assessors are not satisfied in this, and a severe penalty is imposed.

children.text: Chapter 5
svadravyaṃ yatra viśrambhān nikṣipaty aviśaṅkitaḥ
children.translated_text: Where a man, trusting and without suspicion, deposits his own property,

children.text: nikṣepo nāma tat proktaṃ vyavahārapadaṃ budhaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: that is called <s>nikṣepa</s> (deposit), a head of legal procedure, by the wise.

children.text: anyadravyavyavahitaṃ dravyam avyākṛtaṃ ca yat
children.translated_text: Property that is covered by other property and not openly specified,

children.text: nikṣipyate paragṛhe tad aupanidhikaṃ smṛtam ||
children.translated_text: when deposited in another's house, is remembered as <s>aupanidhika</s> (concealed deposit).

children.text: sa punar dvividhaḥ proktaḥ sākṣimān itaras tathā
children.translated_text: That again is said to be of two kinds: with witnesses and without them;

children.text: pratidānaṃ tathaivāsya pratyayaḥ syād viparyaye ||
children.translated_text: its return is likewise, and in the opposite case there should be proof.

children.text: yācyamānas tu yo dātrā nikṣepaṃ na prayacchati
children.translated_text: One who, when requested by the giver, does not return a deposit

children.text: daṇḍyaḥ sa rājñā dāpyaś ca naṣṭe dāpyaś ca tatsamam ||
children.translated_text: is to be fined by the king and made to pay it; if it has been lost, he must pay an equal amount.

children.text: yaś cārthaṃ sādhayet tena nikṣeptur ananujñayā
children.translated_text: And whoever makes profit from that property without the depositor's permission

children.text: tatrāpi daṇḍyaḥ sa bhavet tac ca sodayam āvahet ||
children.translated_text: is punishable in that case too, and must hand it over with its increase.

children.text: grahītuḥ saha yo 'rthena naṣṭo naṣṭaḥ sa dāyinaḥ
children.translated_text: What is lost together with the receiver's property is a loss for the giver;

children.text: daivarājakṛte tadvan na cet taj jihmakāritam ||
children.translated_text: the same applies when it is caused by fate or the king, provided it was not his crooked doing.

children.text: eṣa eva vidhir dṛṣṭo yācitānvāhitādiṣu
children.translated_text: This same rule is observed for borrowed and entrusted goods and the like,

children.text: śilpiṣūpanidhau nyāse pratinyāse tathaiva ca ||
children.translated_text: and likewise with artisans, concealed deposits, deposits, and redeposits.

children.text: pratigṛhṇāti pogaṇḍaṃ yaś ca sapradhanaṃ naraḥ
children.translated_text: The man who receives a <s>pogaṇḍa</s> (minor ward) together with his principal property

children.text: tasyāpy eṣa bhaved dharmaḥ ṣaḍ ete vidhayaḥ samāḥ ||
children.translated_text: has this same rule too; these six procedures are equal.

children.text: Chapter 6
vaṇikprabhṛtayo yatra karma sambhūya kurvate
children.translated_text: Where merchants and others undertake work jointly,

children.text: tat saṃbhūyasamutthānaṃ vyavahārapadaṃ smṛtam ||
children.translated_text: that is remembered as <s>saṃbhūyasamutthāna</s> (joint enterprise), a head of legal procedure.

children.text: phalahetor upāyena karma sambhūya kurvatām
children.translated_text: For those who jointly undertake work by a method for the sake of profit,

children.text: ādhārabhūtaḥ prakṣepas tenottiṣṭheyur aṃśataḥ ||
children.translated_text: the invested contribution is the basis; by it they should proceed according to shares.

children.text: samo 'tirikto hīno vā yatrāṃśo yasya yādṛśaḥ
children.translated_text: Whether a person's share in a venture is equal, greater, or lesser,

children.text: kṣayavyayau tathā vṛddhis tasya tatra tathāvidhāḥ ||
children.translated_text: his loss, expense, and increase there are of that same kind.

children.text: bhāṇḍapiṇḍavyayoddhārabhārasārānvavekṣaṇam
children.translated_text: They should examine merchandise, capital, expenses, recoveries, loads, and value

children.text: kuryus te 'vyabhicāreṇa samaye sve vyavasthitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: without deviation, remaining fixed in their own agreement.

children.text: pramādān nāśitaṃ dāpyaḥ pratiṣiddhakṛtaṃ ca yat
children.translated_text: A partner must be made to pay for what he has destroyed through negligence, and for what he has done when forbidden,

children.text: asaṃdiṣṭaś ca yat kuryāt sarvaiḥ saṃbhūyakāribhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: and for whatever he does without instruction from all the joint actors.

children.text: daivataskararājotthe vyasane samupasthite
children.translated_text: When a misfortune arising from fate, thieves, or the king has occurred,

children.text: yas tat svaśaktyā saṃrakṣet tasyāṃśo daśamaḥ smṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the one who protects the property by his own ability is remembered as entitled to a tenth share.

children.text: ekasya cet syād vyasanaṃ dāyādo 'sya tad āpnuyāt
children.translated_text: If misfortune should befall one partner, his heir should receive that share;

children.text: anyo vāsati dāyāde śaktāś cet sarva eva vā ||
children.translated_text: or another may do so if there is no heir, or all of them if they are capable.

children.text: ṛtvijāṃ vyasane 'py evam anyas tat karma nistaret
children.translated_text: In the case of misfortune among officiating priests also, another should carry that rite through;

children.text: labheta dakṣiṇābhāgaṃ sa tasmāt saṃprakalpitam ||
children.translated_text: from it he should receive the fee-share that has been assigned.

children.text: ṛtvig yājyam aduṣṭaṃ yas tyajed anapakāriṇam
children.translated_text: The officiating priest who abandons a faultless patron who has done him no wrong,

children.text: aduṣṭaṃ vartvijaṃ yājyo vineyau tāv ubhāv api ||
children.translated_text: and the patron who abandons a faultless officiating priest, both are to be fined.

children.text: ṛtvik tu trividho dṛṣṭaḥ pūrvajuṣṭaḥ svayaṃkṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: An officiating priest is seen as threefold: one previously served, one personally chosen,

children.text: yadṛcchayā ca yaḥ kuryād ārtvijyaṃ prītipūrvakam ||
children.translated_text: and one who, by chance, performs priestly service out of affection.

children.text: kramāgateṣv eṣa dharmo vṛteṣv ṛtvikṣu ca svayam
children.translated_text: This rule applies to priests who come in due succession and to those personally appointed;

children.text: yādṛcchike tu saṃyājye tattyāge nāsti kilbiṣam ||
children.translated_text: but with a chance officiant at a sacrifice, there is no guilt in abandoning him.

children.text: śulkasthānaṃ vaṇik prāptaḥ śulkaṃ dadyād yathopagam
children.translated_text: A merchant who has reached a customs station should pay the customs duty according to agreement;

children.text: na tad vyatihared rājñāṃ balir eṣa prakalpitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: he should not evade it, for this levy is prescribed for kings.

children.text: śulkasthānaṃ pariharan na kāle krayavikrayī
children.translated_text: A buyer or seller who avoids the customs station, trades at an improper time,

children.text: mithyoktvā ca parīmāṇaṃ dāpyo 'ṣṭaguṇam atyayam ||
children.translated_text: and falsely states the measure, must be made to pay an eightfold penalty.

children.text: kaścic cet saṃcaran deśāt preyād abhyāgato vaṇik
children.translated_text: If some merchant, travelling from one region to another and having arrived, should die

children.text: rājāsya bhāṇḍaṃ tad rakṣet yāvad dāyādadarśanam ||
children.translated_text: The king should guard that property until an heir appears.

children.text: dāyāde 'sati bandhubhyo jñātibhyo vā tad arpayet
children.translated_text: If there is no heir, he should hand it over to relatives or kinsmen.

children.text: tadabhāve suguptaṃ tad dhārayed daśatīḥ samāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Failing those, he should keep it well guarded for ten years.

children.text: asvāmikam adāyādaṃ daśavarṣasthitaṃ tataḥ
children.translated_text: Then, after ten years, property that has no owner and no heir

children.text: rājā tad ātmasāt kuryād evaṃ dharmo na hīyate ||
children.translated_text: the king may make his own; in this way <s>dharma</s> is not impaired.

children.text: Chapter 7
dattvā dravyam asamyag yaḥ punar ādātum icchati
children.translated_text: When a man, after improperly giving away property, wishes to take it back again,

children.text: dattāpradānikaṃ nāma tad vivādapadaṃ smṛtam ||
children.translated_text: that is remembered as the head of dispute called <s>dattāpradānika</s> (recovery of a gift).

children.text: adeyam atha deyaṃ ca dattaṃ cādattam eva ca
children.translated_text: What is not to be given, what is to be given, what has been given, and what is not truly given:

children.text: vyavahāreṣu vijñeyo dānamārgaś caturvidhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: in legal proceedings the path of gift is to be understood as fourfold.

children.text: tatra hyaṣṭāv adeyāni deyam ekavidhaṃ smṛtam
children.translated_text: Among these, eight things are remembered as not to be given, and only one kind as fit to be given.

children.text: dattaṃ saptavidhaṃ vidyād adattaṃ ṣoḍaśātmakam ||
children.translated_text: One should know what has been given as sevenfold, and what is not truly given as sixteenfold.

children.text: anvāhitaṃ yācitakam ādhiḥ sādhāraṇaṃ ca yat
children.translated_text: What has been entrusted for use, what has been borrowed, a pledge, and what is held in common,

children.text: nikṣepaḥ putradāraṃ ca sarvasvaṃ cānvaye sati ||
children.translated_text: a deposit, one's son and wife, and all one's property when descendants exist,

children.text: āpatsv api hi kaṣṭāsu vartamānena dehinā
children.translated_text: even by a living person who is in the midst of severe calamities,

children.text: adeyāny āhur ācāryā yac cānyasmai pratiśrutam ||
children.translated_text: the teachers declare to be things not to be given, as also whatever has been promised to another.

children.text: kuṭumbabharaṇād dravyaṃ yatkiṃcid atiricyate
children.translated_text: Whatever wealth remains over after the support of the family

children.text: tad deyam upahṛtyānyad dadad doṣam avāpnuyāt ||
children.translated_text: is what should be given; one who gives anything else, after taking it away, incurs fault.

children.text: paṇyamūlyaṃ bhṛtis tuṣṭyā snehāt pratyupakārataḥ
children.translated_text: The price of goods, wages, a gift from satisfaction, from affection, and in return for a benefit,

children.text: strīśulkānugrahārthaṃ ca dattaṃ dānavido viduḥ ||
children.translated_text: and what is given as a bride-price or as a favor: those who know gift-law recognize these as given.

children.text: adattaṃ tu bhayakrodhaśokavegarujānvitaiḥ
children.translated_text: But what is given by persons affected by fear, anger, grief, impulse, or illness is not truly given,

children.text: tathotkocaparīhāsavyatyāsacchalayogataḥ ||
children.translated_text: and likewise what is given through bribery, joking, substitution, or deceit.

children.text: bālamūḍhāsvatantrārtamattonmattāpavarjitam
children.translated_text: What is excluded because it comes from a child, a fool, a dependent person, one in distress, a drunkard, or a madman,

children.text: kartā mamāyaṃ karmeti pratilābhecchayā ca yat ||
children.translated_text: and what is given with the hope of receiving something back, thinking, 'This man will do my work,'

children.text: apātre pātram ity ukte kārye cādharmasaṃhite
children.translated_text: what is given to an unworthy recipient when he is called worthy, or for an undertaking connected with <s>adharma</s>,

children.text: yad dattaṃ syād avijñānād adattaṃ tad api smṛtam ||
children.translated_text: whatever has been given through ignorance is also remembered as not truly given.

children.text: gṛhṇāty adattaṃ yo lobhād yaś cādeyaṃ prayacchati
children.translated_text: He who takes what was not truly given out of greed, and he who gives what ought not to be given,

children.text: adattādāyako daṇḍyas tathādeyasya dāyakaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the taker of the ungiven is punishable, and so too the giver of what should not be given.

children.text: Chapter 8
abhyupetya tu śuśrūṣāṃ yas tāṃ na pratipadyate
children.translated_text: But when someone undertakes service and then does not perform it,

children.text: aśuśrūṣābhyupetyaitad vivādapadam ucyate ||
children.translated_text: this is called the head of dispute concerning failure to serve after agreement.

children.text: śuśrūṣakaḥ pañcavidhaḥ śāstre dṛṣṭo manīṣibhiḥ
children.translated_text: A service-person is seen in the śāstra by the wise as fivefold.

children.text: caturvidhaḥ karmakaras teṣāṃ dāsās tripañcakāḥ ||
children.translated_text: The worker is fourfold; among these, the slaves are fifteenfold.

children.text: śiṣyāntevāsibhṛtakāś caturthas tv adhikarmakṛt
children.translated_text: Students, resident pupils, hired servants, and, as the fourth, the household manager:

children.text: ete karmakarāḥ proktā dāsās tu gṛhajādayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: these are called workers, while the slaves begin with those born in the house.

children.text: sāmānyam asvatantratvam eṣām āhur manīṣiṇaḥ
children.translated_text: The wise say that their common feature is lack of independence.

children.text: jātikarmakṛtas tūkto viśeṣo vṛttir eva ca ||
children.translated_text: The special distinction is said to be produced by birth and work, and also by livelihood.

children.text: karmāpi dvividhaṃ jñeyam aśubhaṃ śubham eva ca
children.translated_text: Work too should be known as twofold: impure and pure.

children.text: aśubhaṃ dāsakarmoktaṃ śubhaṃ karmakṛtāṃ smṛtam ||
children.translated_text: Impure work is said to be the work of slaves; pure work is remembered as belonging to workers.

children.text: gṛhadvārāśucisthānarathyāvaskaraśodhanam
children.translated_text: Cleaning houses, doors, impure places, roads, and refuse,

children.text: guhyāṅgasparśanocchiṣṭaviṇmūtragrahaṇojjhanam ||
children.translated_text: touching private parts, and taking away or removing leftovers, feces, and urine,

children.text: iṣṭataḥ svāminaś cāṅgair upasthānam athāntataḥ
children.translated_text: and bodily attendance on the master at his pleasure, finally:

children.text: aśubhaṃ karma vijñeyaṃ śubham anyad ataḥ param ||
children.translated_text: this should be understood as impure work; beyond this, anything else is pure.

children.text: ā vidyāgrahaṇāc chiṣyaḥ śuśrūṣet prayato gurum
children.translated_text: Until he has acquired learning, a student should carefully serve his teacher.

children.text: tadvṛttir gurudāreṣu guruputre tathaiva ca ||
children.translated_text: The same conduct applies toward the teacher's wives and likewise toward the teacher's son.

children.text: brahmacārī cared bhaikṣam adhaḥśāyy analaṃkṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: A brahmacārin should go for alms, sleep low, and remain unadorned.

children.text: jaghanyaśāyī sarveṣāṃ pūrvotthāyī guror gṛhe ||
children.translated_text: In the teacher's house he should sleep lower than everyone and rise before them.

children.text: nāsaṃdiṣṭaḥ pratiṣṭheta tiṣṭhed vāpi guruṃ kvacit
children.translated_text: Unless instructed, he should not take his place or stand near the teacher at any time.

children.text: saṃdiṣṭaḥ karma kurvīta śaktaś ced avicārayan ||
children.translated_text: When instructed, if he is able, he should do the task without questioning it.

children.text: yathākālam adhīyīta yāvan na vimanā guruḥ
children.translated_text: He should study at the proper time, as long as the teacher is not displeased,

children.text: āsīno 'dho guroḥ kūrce phalake vā samāhitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: sitting attentively below the teacher on a seat, stool, or board.

children.text: anuśāsyaś ca guruṇā na ced anuvidhīyate
children.translated_text: If, though instructed by the teacher, he does not comply,

children.text: avadhenāthavā hanyāt rajjvā veṇudalena vā ||
children.translated_text: the teacher may strike him, without wounding him, with a rope or a strip of bamboo.

children.text: bhṛśaṃ na tāḍayed enaṃ nottamāṅge na vakṣasi
children.translated_text: He should not beat him severely, nor on the head, nor on the chest.

children.text: anuśāsyātha viśvāsyaḥ śāsyo rājñānyathā guruḥ ||
children.translated_text: After disciplining him the teacher is to be trusted; otherwise the teacher is punishable by the king.

children.text: samāvṛttaś ca gurave pradāya gurudakṣiṇām
children.translated_text: When he has completed studentship and has given the teacher's fee to the teacher,

children.text: pratīyāt svagṛhān eṣā śiṣyavṛttir udāhṛtā ||
children.translated_text: he should go back to his own house; this is declared to be the conduct of a student.

children.text: svaśilpam icchann āhartuṃ bāndhavānām anujñayā
children.translated_text: One who wishes to acquire his own craft, with the permission of his relatives,

children.text: ācāryasya vased ante kālaṃ kṛtvā suniścitam ||
children.translated_text: should live near the instructor after setting a definite period of time.

children.text: ācāryaḥ śikṣayed enaṃ svagṛhād dattabhojanam
children.translated_text: The instructor should teach him, feeding him from his own household,

children.text: na cānyat kārayet karma putravac cainam ācaret ||
children.translated_text: and should not make him do any other work; he should treat him like a son.

children.text: śikṣayantam aduṣṭaṃ ca yas tv ācāryaṃ parityajet
children.translated_text: But if someone abandons an instructor who is teaching him and has committed no fault,

children.text: balād vāsayitavyaḥ syād vadhabandhau ca so 'rhati ||
children.translated_text: he should be made to stay there by force, and he deserves beating and confinement.

children.text: śikṣito 'pi kṛtaṃ kālam antevāsī samāpnuyāt
children.translated_text: Even after being taught, a resident pupil should complete the agreed period of time.

children.text: tatra karma ca yat kuryād ācāryasyaiva tatphalam ||
children.translated_text: Whatever work he does there has its benefit for the instructor alone.

children.text: gṛhītaśilpaḥ samaye kṛtvācāryaṃ pradakṣiṇam
children.translated_text: When he has acquired the craft, at the agreed time, after circumambulating the instructor,

children.text: śaktitaś cānumānyainam antevāsī nivartayet ||
children.translated_text: and honoring him according to his ability, the resident pupil should depart.

children.text: bhṛtakas trividho jñeya uttamo madhyamo 'dhamaḥ
children.translated_text: A hired servant should be known as threefold: superior, middling, and inferior.

children.text: śaktibhaktyanurūpā syād eṣāṃ karmāśrayā bhṛtiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Their work-based wage should correspond to their ability and devotion.

children.text: uttamas tv āyudhīyo 'tra madhyamas tu kṛṣīvalaḥ
children.translated_text: Here the superior one is the armed man; the middling one is the cultivator.

children.text: adhamo bhāravāhaḥ syād ity evaṃ trividho bhṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The inferior one is the burden-carrier; in this way a hired servant is threefold.

children.text: artheṣv adhikṛto yaḥ syāt kuṭumbasya tathopari
children.translated_text: One who is placed in charge of financial matters and also over the household

children.text: so 'dhikarmakaro jñeyaḥ sa ca kauṭumbikaḥ smṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: should be known as an <s>adhikarmakara</s> (household manager), and he is remembered as a family steward.

children.text: śubhakarmakarās tv ete catvāraḥ samudāhṛtāḥ
children.translated_text: These four have thus been described as workers engaged in pure work.

children.text: jaghanyakarmabhājas tu śeṣā dāsās tripañcakāḥ ||
children.translated_text: But the remaining fifteen slaves are sharers in low work.

children.text: gṛhajātas tathā krīto labdho dāyād upāgataḥ
children.translated_text: One born in the house, one bought, one received, and one obtained by inheritance,

children.text: anākālabhṛtas tadvad ādhattaḥ svāminā ca yaḥ ||
children.translated_text: one maintained in a time of famine, likewise, and one pledged by his master,

children.text: mokṣito mahataś carṇāt prāpto yuddhāt paṇe jitaḥ
children.translated_text: one released from a great debt, one obtained from war, and one won by wager,

children.text: tavāham ity upagataḥ pravrajyāvasitaḥ kṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: one who has come saying, "I am yours," one fallen from ascetic life, and one made by contract.

children.text: bhaktadāsaś ca vijñeyas tathaiva vaḍavābhṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: A <s>bhaktadāsa</s> (food-slave) should also be recognized, and likewise a <s>vaḍavābhṛta</s>.

children.text: vikretā cātmanaḥ śāstre dāsāḥ pañcadaśā smṛtāḥ ||
children.translated_text: And one who sells himself: in the śāstra slaves are remembered as fifteenfold.

children.text: tatra pūrvaś caturvargo dāsatvān na vimucyate
children.translated_text: Among these, the first fourfold class is not released from slavery,

children.text: prasādāt svāmino 'nyatra dāsyam eṣāṃ kramāgatam ||
children.translated_text: except by the master's favor; their servitude has come down in succession.

children.text: yaś caiṣāṃ svāminaṃ kaścin mokṣayet prāṇasaṃśayāt
children.translated_text: And if any one of these saves his master from danger to life,

children.text: dāsatvāt sa vimucyeta putrabhāgaṃ labheta ca ||
children.translated_text: he is released from slavery and also receives a son's share.

children.text: anākālabhṛto dāsyān mucyate goyugaṃ dadat
children.translated_text: One maintained in a time of distress is released from slavery by giving a yoke of cattle.

children.text: saṃbhakṣitaṃ yad durbhikṣe na tac chudhyeta karmaṇā ||
children.translated_text: What has been eaten in famine is not cleared by labor.

children.text: ādhatto 'pi dhanaṃ dattvā svāmī yady enam uddharet
children.translated_text: Even a pledged man, if the master redeems him after paying money,

children.text: athopagamayed enaṃ sa vikrītād anantaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: and then brings him under his authority, is next after one who has been bought.

children.text: dattvā tu sodayam ṛṇaṃ ṛṇī dāsyāt pramucyate
children.translated_text: But a debtor is released from slavery after paying the debt with interest.

children.text: kṛtakālābhyupagamāt kṛtako 'pi vimucyate ||
children.translated_text: A contracted servant too is released when the agreed term has arrived.

children.text: tavāham ity upagato yuddhaprāptaḥ paṇe jitaḥ
children.translated_text: One who has come saying "I am yours," one captured in war, and one won in a wager

children.text: pratiśīrṣapradānena mucyate tulyakarmaṇā ||
children.translated_text: is released by giving a substitute person of equal work.

children.text: rājña eva tu dāsaḥ syāt pravrajyāvasito naraḥ
children.translated_text: But a man fallen from the ascetic order becomes the king's slave alone.

children.text: na tasya pratimokṣo 'sti na viśuddhiḥ kathaṃcana ||
children.translated_text: For him there is no release and no purification in any way.

children.text: bhaktasyopekṣaṇāt sadyo bhaktadāsaḥ pramucyate
children.translated_text: A <s>bhaktadāsa</s> is immediately released when his food is neglected.

children.text: nigrahād vaḍavāyāś ca mucyate vaḍavābhṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And a <s>vaḍavābhṛta</s> is released through the restraint of the <s>vaḍavā</s>.

children.text: vikrīṇīte ya ātmānaṃ svatantraḥ san narādhamaḥ
children.translated_text: The lowest of men who, though free, sells himself

children.text: sa jaghanyataras teṣāṃ naiva dāsyāt pramucyate ||
children.translated_text: is the lowest of all these and is never released from servitude.

children.text: caurāpahṛtavikrītā ye ca dāsīkṛtā balāt
children.translated_text: Those who have been abducted and sold by thieves, and those enslaved by force,

children.text: rājñā mokṣayitavyās te dāsatvaṃ teṣu neṣyate ||
children.translated_text: must be released by the king; slavery is not accepted in their case.

children.text: varṇānāṃ prātilomyena dāsatvaṃ na vidhīyate
children.translated_text: Slavery is not prescribed in the reverse order of the <s>varṇas</s>,

children.text: svadharmatyāgino 'nyatra dāravad dāsatā matā ||
children.translated_text: except for those who abandon their own <s>dharma</s>; servitude is regarded as in the case of wives.

children.text: tavāham iti cātmānaṃ yo 'svatantraḥ prayacchati
children.translated_text: And one who, not being independent, gives himself saying "I am yours"

children.text: na sa taṃ prāpnuyāt kāmaṃ pūrvasvāmī labheta tam ||
children.translated_text: does not obtain that desired object; his former master should get him.

children.text: adhanās traya evoktā bhāryā dāsas tathā sutaḥ
children.translated_text: Three indeed are said to be without property: a wife, a slave, and a son.

children.text: yat te samadhigacchanti yasya te tasya tad dhanam ||
children.translated_text: Whatever they acquire is the wealth of the person to whom they belong.

children.text: svadāsam icched yaḥ kartum adāsaṃ prītamānasaḥ
children.translated_text: If someone, being pleased in mind, wishes to make his own slave a non-slave,

children.text: skandhād ādāya tasyāpi bhindyāt kumbhaṃ sahāmbhasā ||
children.translated_text: he should take a water-pot from his shoulder and break it together with the water.

children.text: akṣatābhiḥ sapuṣpābhir mūrdhany enam avākiret
children.translated_text: He should sprinkle him on the head with unbroken grains together with flowers,

children.text: adāsa iti coktvā triḥ prāṅmukhaṃ tam athotsṛjet ||
children.translated_text: and, after saying three times "You are not a slave," he should then release him facing east.

children.text: tataḥprabhṛti vaktavyaḥ svāmyanugrahapālitaḥ
children.translated_text: From then onward he should be called one protected by the master's favor.

children.text: bhojyānnaḥ pratigṛhyaś ca bhavaty abhimataś ca saḥ ||
children.translated_text: He becomes one whose food may be eaten, one fit to receive gifts, and one who is approved.

children.text: Chapter 9
bhṛtānāṃ vetanasyokto dānādānavidhikramaḥ
children.translated_text: For hired workers, the ordered rule for giving and withholding wages has been stated.

children.text: vetanasyānapākarma tad vivādapadaṃ smṛtam ||
children.translated_text: Non-payment of wages is remembered as that head of dispute.

children.text: bhṛtāya vetanaṃ dadyāt karmasvāmī yathākramam
children.translated_text: The employer should give wages to a hired worker in due order,

children.text: ādau madhye 'vasāne vā karmaṇo yad viniścitam ||
children.translated_text: as was determined at the beginning, middle, or end of the work.

children.text: bhṛtāvaniścitāyāṃ tu daśabhāgaṃ samāpnuyuḥ
children.translated_text: But when the wage has not been fixed, they should obtain a tenth share,

children.text: lābhagobījasasyānāṃ vaṇiggopakṛṣīvalāḥ ||
children.translated_text: merchants, cowherds, and cultivators, of profit, cattle, seed, and crop.

children.text: karmopakaraṇaṃ caiṣāṃ kriyāṃ prati yad āhṛtam
children.translated_text: Whatever equipment for their work has been brought for the task,

children.text: āptabhāvena kurvīta na jihmena samācaret ||
children.translated_text: one should use it with trustworthiness and should not act crookedly.

children.text: karmākurvan pratiśrutya kāryo dattvā bhṛtiṃ balāt
children.translated_text: One who promises the work and does not do it should be made to do it by force after the wage has been given.

children.text: bhṛtiṃ gṛhītvākurvāṇo dviguṇāṃ bhṛtim āvahet ||
children.translated_text: One who takes the wage but does not work should pay a double wage.

children.text: kāle 'pūrṇe tyajet karma bhṛtināśo 'sya cārhati
children.translated_text: If he abandons the work before the time is complete, he deserves loss of his wage.

children.text: svāmidoṣād apākrāman yāvat kṛtam avāpnuyāt ||
children.translated_text: If he withdraws because of the master's fault, he should receive as much as he has done.

children.text: bhṛtiṣaḍbhāgam ābhāṣya pathi yugyakṛtaṃ tyajan
children.translated_text: After agreeing to a sixth part of the wage, if one abandons on the road what was engaged for the yoke or transport,

children.text: adadat kārayitvā tu karmaivaṃ sodayāṃ bhṛtim ||
children.translated_text: or, after causing the work to be done, does not pay, he must pay that wage with interest.

children.text: anayan bhāṭayitvā tu bhāṇḍavān yānavāhane
children.translated_text: If, after hiring transport by vehicle or carrier for goods, one does not bring them,

children.text: dāpyo bhṛticaturbhāgaṃ samam ardhapathe tyajan ||
children.translated_text: but abandons them halfway, he should be made to pay a quarter of the hire equally.

children.text: anayan vāhako 'py evaṃ bhṛtihānim avāpnuyāt
children.translated_text: A carrier who does not bring them likewise incurs loss of hire.

children.text: dviguṇāṃ tu bhṛtiṃ dāpyaḥ prasthāne vighnam ācaran ||
children.translated_text: But one who creates an obstruction at the departure should be made to pay double the hire.

children.text: bhāṇḍaṃ vyasanam āgacched yadi vāhakadoṣataḥ
children.translated_text: If the goods meet with disaster through the carrier's fault,

children.text: dāpyo yat tatra naṣṭaṃ syād daivarājakṛtād ṛte ||
children.translated_text: he should be made to pay whatever has been lost there, except when it is caused by fate or by the king.

children.text: gavāṃ śatād vatsatarī dhenuḥ syād dviśatād bhṛtiḥ
children.translated_text: From a hundred cows a heifer should be the wage; from two hundred, a milch cow.

children.text: prati saṃvatsaraṃ gope sadohaś cāṣṭame 'hani ||
children.translated_text: For a cowherd this is yearly, and there is also a milking on the eighth day.

children.text: upānayet gā gopāya pratyahaṃ rajanīkṣaye
children.translated_text: One should bring the cows to the cowherd every day at the end of night.

children.text: cīrṇāḥ pītāś ca tā gopaḥ sāyāhne pratyupānayet ||
children.translated_text: The cowherd should bring them back in the evening after they have grazed and drunk.

children.text: syāc ced govyasanaṃ gopo vyāyacchet tatra śaktitaḥ
children.translated_text: If a calamity befalls the cows, the cowherd should exert himself there according to his ability.

children.text: aśaktas tūrṇam āgamya svāmine tan nivedayet ||
children.translated_text: If he is unable, he should come quickly and report it to the owner.

children.text: avyāyac channavikrośan svāmine cānivedayan
children.translated_text: If he does not exert himself, does not cry out, and does not report it to the owner,

children.text: voḍhum arhati gopas tāṃ vinayaṃ cāpi rājani ||
children.translated_text: the cowherd deserves to bear that liability, and also a fine before the king.

children.text: naṣṭavinaṣṭaṃ kṛmibhiḥ śvahataṃ viṣame mṛtam
children.translated_text: What is lost, destroyed, eaten by worms, killed by dogs, or dead in rough ground,

children.text: hīnaṃ puruṣakāreṇa gopāyaiva nipātayet ||
children.translated_text: when it is lacking through human effort, should be charged to the cowherd alone.

children.text: ajāvike tathāruddhe vṛkaiḥ pāle tv anāyati
children.translated_text: Likewise, in the case of goats and sheep when they are penned and the keeper does not come as wolves attack,

children.text: yat prasahya vṛko hanyāt pāle tatkilbiṣam bhavet ||
children.translated_text: whatever the wolf kills by force is the keeper's fault.

children.text: tāsāṃ caivāniruddhānāṃ carantīnāṃ mitho vane
children.translated_text: But among those same animals, when they are not penned and are roaming together in the forest,

children.text: yām utpatya vṛko hanyān na pālas tatra kilbiṣī ||
children.translated_text: whichever one a wolf leaps upon and kills, the keeper is not at fault there.

children.text: vighuṣya tu hṛtaṃ caurair na pālo dātum arhati
children.translated_text: But if, after he has raised an alarm, it is stolen by thieves, the keeper is not required to pay,

children.text: yadi deśe ca kāle ca svāminaḥ svasya śaṃsati ||
children.translated_text: provided that he reports it to his own master at the proper place and time.

children.text: etena sarvapālānāṃ vivādaḥ samudāhṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: By this the dispute concerning all keepers has been set forth.

children.text: mṛteṣu ca viśuddhiḥ syāt pālasyāṅkādidarśanāt ||
children.translated_text: And in cases of dead animals, the keeper's exoneration comes from showing marks and the like.

children.text: śulkaṃ gṛhītvā paṇyastrī necchantī dvis tad āvahet
children.translated_text: A courtesan who has taken a fee and then is unwilling should pay that fee twice over.

children.text: aprayacchaṃs tadā śulkam anubhūya pumān striyam ||
children.translated_text: A man who, after enjoying the woman, does not then pay that fee...

children.text: ayonau kramate yas tu bahubhir vāpi vāsayet
children.translated_text: But one who approaches outside the proper sexual organ, or causes cohabitation with many men,

children.text: śulkam aṣṭaguṇaṃ dāpyo vinayas tāvad eva ca ||
children.translated_text: shall be made to pay eight times the bride-price, and a fine of just the same amount.

children.text: parājire gṛhaṃ kṛtvā stomaṃ dattvā vaset tu yaḥ
children.translated_text: But one who builds a house in another's enclosure and dwells there after paying rent

children.text: sa tad gṛhītvā nirgacchet tṛṇakāṣṭheṣṭakādikam ||
children.translated_text: shall depart taking that with him, including grass, wood, bricks, and the like.

children.text: stomavāhīni bhāṇḍāni pūrṇakālāny upānayet
children.translated_text: Goods and vessels bearing rent should be brought back when the full term is complete.

children.text: grahītur ābhaved bhagnaṃ naṣṭaṃ cānyatra saṃplavāt ||
children.translated_text: If they are broken or lost, the loss falls on the taker, except in a flood.

children.text: Chapter 10
nikṣiptaṃ vā paradravyaṃ naṣṭaṃ labdhvāpahṛtya vā
children.translated_text: When another's property, whether deposited, lost and then found, or stolen,

children.text: vikrīyate 'samakṣaṃ yad vijñeyo 'svāmivikrayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: is sold without the owner's presence, it is to be known as <s>asvāmivikraya</s> (sale by a non-owner).

children.text: dravyam asvāmivikrītaṃ prāpya svāmī samāpnuyāt
children.translated_text: When the owner obtains property sold by a non-owner, he should recover it.

children.text: prakāśaṃ krayataḥ śuddhiḥ kretuḥ steyaṃ rahaḥ krayāt ||
children.translated_text: The buyer is cleared by an open purchase; by a secret purchase, there is theft.

children.text: asvāmyanumatād dāsād asataś ca janād rahaḥ
children.translated_text: From a slave not authorized by the owner, or secretly from an untrustworthy person,

children.text: hīnamūlyam avelāyāṃ krīṇaṃs taddoṣabhāg bhavet ||
children.translated_text: one who buys at a low price and at an improper time shares that fault.

children.text: na gūhetāgamaṃ kretā śuddhis tasya tadāgamāt
children.translated_text: The buyer must not conceal the source; his clearance comes from that source.

children.text: viparyaye tulyadoṣaḥ steyadaṇḍaṃ ca so 'rhati ||
children.translated_text: In the opposite case he has equal guilt and deserves the penalty for theft.

children.text: vikretā svāmine 'rthaṃ ca kretur mūlyaṃ ca tatkṛtam
children.translated_text: The seller should give the property to the owner and the agreed price to the buyer,

children.text: dadyād daṇḍaṃ tathā rājñe vidhir asvāmivikraye ||
children.translated_text: and likewise pay a fine to the king; this is the rule in <s>asvāmivikraya</s>.

children.text: pareṇa nihitaṃ labdhvā rājany upaharen nidhim
children.translated_text: On finding a treasure deposited by another, one should hand the treasure over to the king.

children.text: rājagāmī nidhiḥ sarvaḥ sarveṣāṃ brāhmaṇād ṛte ||
children.translated_text: All treasure goes to the king for everyone, except for a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>.

children.text: brāhmaṇo 'pi nidhiṃ labdhvā kṣipraṃ rājñe nivedayet
children.translated_text: Even a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, on finding treasure, should report it quickly to the king.

children.text: tena dattaṃ ca bhuñjīta stenaḥ syād anivedayan ||
children.translated_text: He may enjoy what is given by him; if he does not report it, he becomes a thief.

children.text: svam apy arthaṃ tathā naṣṭaṃ labdhvā rājñe nivedayet
children.translated_text: Likewise, after finding even his own property that was lost, one should report it to the king.

children.text: gṛhṇīyāt tatra taṃ śuddham aśuddhaṃ syāt tato 'nyathā ||
children.translated_text: There he may take it as cleared; otherwise it would be uncleared.

children.text: Chapter 11
vikrīya paṇyaṃ mūlyena kretur yan na pradīyate
children.translated_text: When merchandise has been sold for a price but is not delivered to the buyer,

children.text: vikrīyāsaṃpradānaṃ tad vivādapadam ucyate ||
children.translated_text: that is called <s>vikrīyāsaṃpradāna</s> (non-delivery after sale), a head of dispute.

children.text: loke 'smin dvividhaṃ dravyaṃ jaṅgamaṃ sthāvaraṃ tathā
children.translated_text: In this world property is twofold, movable and also immovable;

children.text: krayavikrayadharmeṣu sarvaṃ tat paṇyam ucyate ||
children.translated_text: in the rules for buying and selling, all of that is called <s>paṇya</s> (merchandise).

children.text: ṣaḍvidhas tasya tu budhair dānādānavidhiḥ smṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: The wise remember its procedure of giving and receiving as sixfold:

children.text: gaṇimaṃ tulimaṃ meyaṃ kriyayā rūpataḥ śriyā ||
children.translated_text: countable, weighable, measurable, by workmanship, by form, and by quality.

children.text: vikrīya paṇyaṃ mūlyena kretur yo na prayacchati
children.translated_text: If someone, having sold merchandise for a price, does not give it to the buyer,

children.text: sthāvarasya kṣayaṃ dāpyo jaṅgamasya kriyāphalam ||
children.translated_text: he shall be made to pay the loss of immovable property and the profit from use of movable property.

children.text: arghaś ced apahīyeta sodayaṃ paṇyam āvahet
children.translated_text: If the price should fall, he must deliver the merchandise together with its increase.

children.text: sthāyinām eṣa niyamo diglābho digvicāriṇām ||
children.translated_text: This is the rule for stationary goods; for goods moving across regions, the regional profit applies.

children.text: upahanyeta vā paṇyaṃ dahyetāpahriyeta vā
children.translated_text: If the merchandise is damaged, burned, or carried off,

children.text: vikretur eva so 'nartho vikrīyāsamprayacchataḥ ||
children.translated_text: that loss belongs only to the seller who has sold it and not delivered it.

children.text: nirdoṣaṃ darśayitvā tu sadoṣaṃ yaḥ prayacchati
children.translated_text: But someone who displays it as faultless and delivers it as defective

children.text: mūlyaṃ taddviguṇaṃ dāpyo vinayaṃ tāvad eva ca ||
children.translated_text: shall be made to pay twice its price and a fine of the same amount.

children.text: tathānyahaste vikrīya yo 'nyasmai samprayacchati
children.translated_text: Likewise, one who sells it into one person's hand and delivers it to another

children.text: so 'pi taddviguṇaṃ dāpyo vineyas tāvad eva ca ||
children.translated_text: shall also be made to pay twice that amount and shall be fined the same.

children.text: dīyamānaṃ na gṛhṇāti krītaṃ paṇyaṃ ca yaḥ krayī
children.translated_text: When a buyer does not accept purchased merchandise as it is being given,

children.text: vikrīṇānas tad anyatra vikretā nāparādhnuyāt ||
children.translated_text: the seller commits no offense if he sells it elsewhere.

children.text: dattamūlyasya paṇyasya vidhir eṣa prakīrtitaḥ
children.translated_text: This rule has been stated for merchandise whose price has been paid.

children.text: adatte 'nyatra samayān na vikretur atikramaḥ ||
children.translated_text: If the price has not been paid, apart from an agreement, there is no transgression by the seller.

children.text: lābhārthe vaṇijāṃ sarvapaṇyeṣu krayavikrayaḥ
children.translated_text: For merchants, buying and selling in all merchandise is for the sake of profit.

children.text: sa ca lābho 'rgham āsādya mahān bhavati vā na vā ||
children.translated_text: And that profit, depending on the market price, may or may not be great.

children.text: tasmād deśe ca kāle ca vaṇig arghaṃ parākramet
children.translated_text: Therefore, according to place and time, a merchant should exert himself over the price.

children.text: na jihmena pravarteta śreyān evaṃ vaṇikpathaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He should not proceed crookedly; in this way the merchant's path is better.

children.text: Chapter 12
krītvā mūlyena yaḥ paṇyaṃ kretā na bahu manyate
children.translated_text: When a buyer, after buying merchandise for a price, does not esteem it highly,

children.text: krītvānuśaya ity etad vivādapadam ucyate ||
children.translated_text: this is called <s>krītvānuśaya</s> (regret after purchase), a head of dispute.

children.text: krītvā mūlyena yat paṇyaṃ duṣkrītaṃ manyate krayī
children.translated_text: When a buyer, having bought merchandise for a price, thinks it was badly bought,

children.text: vikretuḥ pratideyaṃ tat tasmin evāhny avikṣatam ||
children.translated_text: it should be returned to the seller on that very day, undamaged.

children.text: dvitīye 'hni dadat kretā mūlyāt triṃśāṃśam āvahet
children.translated_text: If the buyer returns it on the second day, he must bear one-thirtieth of the price.

children.text: dviguṇaṃ tat tṛtīye 'hni parataḥ kretur eva tat ||
children.translated_text: On the third day he must bear twice that; after that, it is the buyer's alone.

children.text: kretā paṇyaṃ parīkṣeta prāk svayaṃ guṇadoṣataḥ
children.translated_text: The buyer should first examine the merchandise himself with respect to qualities and faults.

children.text: parīkṣyābhimataṃ krītaṃ vikretur na bhavet punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: What has been examined, approved, and bought cannot again become the seller's.

children.text: tryahād dohyaṃ parīkṣeta pañcāhād vāhyam eva tu
children.translated_text: A milch animal should be examined for three days, and a draught animal for five days.

children.text: muktāvajrapravālānāṃ saptāhaṃ syāt parīkṣaṇam ||
children.translated_text: For pearls, diamonds, and corals the examination should be seven days.

children.text: dvipadām ardhamāsaṃ syāt puṃsāṃ taddviguṇaṃ striyāḥ
children.translated_text: For bipeds it should be half a month for males, and twice that for females.

children.text: daśāhaṃ sarvabījānām ekāhaṃ lohavāsasām ||
children.translated_text: For all seeds it is ten days; for metals and garments, one day.
