children.text: paribhuktaṃ ca yad vāsaḥ kliṣṭarūpaṃ malīmasam
children.translated_text: And a garment that has been used, spoiled in appearance, and soiled,

children.text: sadoṣam api vikrītaṃ vikretur na bhavet punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: even if sold with a defect, cannot again become the seller's.

children.text: mūlyāṣṭabhāgo hīyeta sakṛd dhautasya vāsasaḥ
children.translated_text: For a garment washed once, an eighth of the price should be deducted.

children.text: dviḥ pādas tris tribhāgas tu catuḥkṛtvo 'rdham eva ca ||
children.translated_text: If washed twice, a quarter; if three times, a third; if four times, exactly half.

children.text: ardhakṣayāt tu parataḥ pādāṃśāpacayaḥ kramāt
children.translated_text: After the loss has reached half, there is a gradual diminution by quarter-parts,

children.text: yāvat kṣīṇadaśaṃ jīrṇaṃ jīrṇasyāniyamaḥ kṣaye ||
children.translated_text: until it is worn down to a tenth; for what is worn out, there is no fixed rule for loss.

children.text: lohānām api sarveṣāṃ hetur agnikriyāvidhau
children.translated_text: For all metals too, in the procedure of firing, there is a cause of loss;

children.text: kṣayaḥ saṃskriyamāṇānāṃ teṣāṃ dṛṣṭo 'gnisaṃgamāt ||
children.translated_text: when they are being refined, their loss is seen from contact with fire.

children.text: suvarṇasya kṣayo nāsti rajate dvipalaṃ śatam
children.translated_text: There is no loss of gold; in silver it is two <s>palas</s> per hundred.

children.text: śatam aṣṭapalaṃ jñeyaṃ kṣayaḥ syāt trapusīsayoḥ ||
children.translated_text: For tin and lead, the loss should be known as eight <s>palas</s> per hundred.

children.text: tāmre pañcapalaṃ vidyād vikārā ye ca tanmayāḥ
children.translated_text: For copper, one should know it as five <s>palas</s>, and the same for products made from it.

children.text: taddhātūnām anekatvād ayaso 'niyamaḥ kṣaye ||
children.translated_text: Because the constituents of iron are many, there is no fixed rule for its loss.

children.text: tāntavasya ca saṃskāre kṣayavṛddhī udāhṛte
children.translated_text: In the processing of textile material, both loss and increase are declared.

children.text: sūtrakārpāsikorṇānāṃ vṛddhir daśapalaṃ śatam ||
children.translated_text: For thread, cotton, and wool, the increase is ten <s>palas</s> per hundred.

children.text: sthūlasūtravatāṃ teṣāṃ madhyānāṃ pañcakaṃ śatam
children.translated_text: For those among them with thick thread, and for middling kinds, it is five per hundred.

children.text: tripalaṃ tu susūkṣmāṇām antaḥkṣaya udāhṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For very fine goods, an internal loss of three palas is stated.

children.text: triṃśāṃśo romaviddhasya kṣayaḥ karmakṛtasya tu
children.translated_text: For an item pierced by hairs, and for one affected by workmanship, the loss is a thirtieth part.

children.text: kauśeyavalkalānāṃ tu naiva vṛddhir na ca kṣayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: But for silk and bark garments there is neither increase nor loss.

children.text: krītvā nānuśayaṃ kuryād vaṇik paṇyavicakṣaṇaḥ
children.translated_text: Having bought, a merchant skilled in merchandise should not show regret.

children.text: vṛddhikṣayau tu jānīyāt paṇyānām āgamaṃ tathā ||
children.translated_text: He should know the increase and decrease of goods, and also their provenance.

children.text: Chapter 13
pāṣaṇḍanaigamādīnāṃ sthitiḥ samaya ucyate
children.translated_text: The established rule of heterodox sects, merchant corporations, and the like is called <s>samaya</s> (agreed custom).

children.text: samayasyānapākarma tad vivādapadaṃ smṛtam ||
children.translated_text: Failure to act according to that <s>samaya</s> is remembered as a ground of dispute.

children.text: pāṣaṇḍanaigamaśreṇīpūgavrātagaṇādiṣu
children.translated_text: Among heterodox sects, merchant corporations, guilds, associations, bands, corporate bodies, and the like,

children.text: saṃrakṣet samayaṃ rājā durge janapade tathā ||
children.translated_text: the king should protect the <s>samaya</s> in the fortified town and in the countryside alike.

children.text: yo dharmaḥ karma yac caiṣām upasthānavidhiś ca yaḥ
children.translated_text: Whatever <s>dharma</s> (norm), practice, and rule of attendance belongs to them,

children.text: yac caiṣāṃ vṛttyupādānam anumanyeta tat tathā ||
children.translated_text: and whatever means of livelihood they have, he should approve it as such.

children.text: pratikūlaṃ ca yad rājñaḥ prakṛtyavamataṃ ca yat
children.translated_text: But whatever is adverse to the king, rejected by the people,

children.text: bādhakaṃ ca yad arthānāṃ tat tebhyo vinivartayet ||
children.translated_text: or injurious to interests and wealth, he should make them desist from that.

children.text: mithaḥ saṃghātakaraṇam ahitaṃ śastradhāraṇam
children.translated_text: The king should not tolerate their forming mutual coalitions, bearing weapons for harmful purposes,

children.text: parasparopaghātaṃ ca teṣāṃ rājā na marṣayet ||
children.translated_text: or injuring one another.

children.text: pṛthag gaṇāṃś ca ye bhindyus te vineyā viśeṣataḥ
children.translated_text: Those who split apart separate corporate bodies should be punished especially,

children.text: āvaheyur bhayaṃ ghoraṃ vyādhivat te hy upekṣitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: for, if neglected, they would bring dreadful danger like a disease.

children.text: doṣavat karaṇaṃ yat syād anāmnāyaprakalpitam
children.translated_text: Any action that is faulty and devised without accepted authority,

children.text: pravṛttam api tad rājā śreyaskāmo nivartayet ||
children.translated_text: even if already in practice, the king who desires welfare should stop.

children.text: Chapter 14
setukedāramaryādāvikṛṣṭākṛṣṭaniścayāḥ
children.translated_text: Where there are determinations about embankments, fields, boundaries, cultivated and uncultivated land,

children.text: kṣetrādhikārā yatra syur vivādaḥ kṣetrajas tu saḥ ||
children.translated_text: and rights over fields, that is a dispute arising from a field.

children.text: kṣetrasīmāvirodheṣu sāmantebhyo viniścayaḥ
children.translated_text: In conflicts over field boundaries, the decision is to come from neighboring landholders,

children.text: nagaragrāmagaṇino ye ca vṛddhatamā narāḥ ||
children.translated_text: from town and village record-keepers, and from the oldest men.

children.text: grāmasīmāsu ca bahir ye syus tatkṛṣijīvinaḥ
children.translated_text: And, in village boundaries, those outside who live from cultivation there,

children.text: gopaśākunikavyādhā ye cānye vanagocarāḥ ||
children.translated_text: cowherds, bird-catchers, hunters, and others who range in the forest,

children.text: samunnayeyus te sīmāṃ lakṣaṇair upalakṣitām
children.translated_text: should trace out the boundary marked by signs,

children.text: tuṣāṅgārakapālaiś ca kumbhair āyatanair drumaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: by husks, charcoal, potsherds, jars, shrines, and trees,

children.text: abhijñātaiś ca valmīkasthalanimnonnatādibhiḥ
children.translated_text: and by recognized anthills, high and low ground, and the like,

children.text: kedārārāmamārgaiś ca purāṇaiḥ setubhis tathā ||
children.translated_text: as well as by old fields, gardens, roads, and embankments.

children.text: nimnagāpahṛtotsṛṣṭanaṣṭacihnāsu bhūmiṣu
children.translated_text: On lands where the marks have been carried away by a river, abandoned, or lost,

children.text: tatpradeśānumānāc ca pramāṇair bhogadarśanaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: they should determine it by inference from that place and by evidence showing possession and use.

children.text: atha ced anṛtaṃ brūyuḥ sāmantās tadviniścaye
children.translated_text: But if the neighboring landholders speak falsely in deciding that matter,

children.text: sarve pṛthak pṛthag daṇḍyā rājñā madhyamasāhasam ||
children.translated_text: all of them, each separately, are to be fined by the king with the middle amercement.

children.text: gaṇavṛddhādayas tv anye daṇḍaṃ dāpyāḥ pṛthak pṛthak
children.translated_text: Other people, such as elders of corporate groups, are to be made to pay a fine separately, each one individually;

children.text: vineyāḥ prathamena syuḥ sāhasenānṛte sthitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: if they stand in falsehood, they should be punished with the first amercement.

children.text: naikaḥ samunnayet sīmāṃ naraḥ pratyayavān api
children.translated_text: A single man should not determine a boundary, even if he is trustworthy,

children.text: gurutvād asya dharmasya kriyaiṣā bahuṣu sthitā ||
children.translated_text: for, because this legal matter is weighty, the procedure rests with many people.

children.text: ekaś ced unnayet sīmāṃ sopavāsaḥ samāhitaḥ
children.translated_text: If a single man should determine a boundary, he should be fasting and composed,

children.text: raktamālyāmbaradharaḥ kṣitim āropya mūrdhani ||
children.translated_text: wearing red garlands and garments, with earth placed upon his head.

children.text: yadā ca na syur jñātāraḥ sīmāyā na ca lakṣaṇam
children.translated_text: And when there are no people who know the boundary, and no marker remains,

children.text: tadā rājā dvayoḥ sīmām uddhared iṣṭataḥ svayam ||
children.translated_text: then the king himself should establish the boundary between the two parties as he thinks fit.

children.text: etenaiva gṛhodyānanipānāyatanādiṣu
children.translated_text: By this same rule, the procedure for disputes concerning houses, gardens, wells, shrines, and the like

children.text: vivādavidhir ākhyātas tathā grāmāntareṣu ca ||
children.translated_text: has been explained, and likewise for disputes between villages.

children.text: avaskarasthalaśvabhrabhramasyandanikādibhiḥ
children.translated_text: One should not obstruct crossroads, divine shrines, streets, and roads

children.text: catuṣpathasurasthānarathyāmārgān na rodhayet ||
children.translated_text: with rubbish heaps, pits, hollows, drains, and the like.

children.text: parakṣetrasya madhye tu setur na pratiṣidhyate
children.translated_text: But an embankment in the middle of another person's field is not forbidden

children.text: mahāguṇo 'lpabādhaś ca vṛddhir iṣṭā kṣaye sati ||
children.translated_text: when it brings great benefit and little harm; gain is preferred even where there is some loss.

children.text: setus tu dvividho jñeyaḥ kheyo bandhyas tathaiva ca
children.translated_text: An embankment is to be understood as twofold: excavated and dammed.

children.text: toyapravartanāt kheyo bandhyaḥ syāt tannivartanāt ||
children.translated_text: It is excavated when water is set flowing, and dammed when that water is stopped.

children.text: nāntareṇodakaṃ sasyaṃ naśyed abhyudakena tu
children.translated_text: Without water a crop would perish, but it also perishes from excessive water.

children.text: ya evānudake doṣaḥ sa evābhyudake smṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The same fault that exists in lack of water is remembered in too much water.

children.text: pūrvapravṛttam utsannam apṛṣṭvā svāminaṃ tu yaḥ
children.translated_text: If someone sets in operation an abandoned embankment that was formerly in use,

children.text: setuṃ pravartayet kaścin na sa tatphalabhāg bhavet ||
children.translated_text: without asking the owner, he shall not share in its produce.

children.text: mṛte tu svāmini punas tadvaṃśye vāpi mānave
children.translated_text: But if the owner is dead, or there is a man of his lineage,

children.text: rājānam āmantrya tataḥ prakuryāt setukarma tat ||
children.translated_text: then, after notifying the king, he should undertake that embankment work.

children.text: ato 'nyathā kleśabhāk syān mṛgavyādhānudarśanāt
children.translated_text: Otherwise he would be liable to trouble, as is seen from the example of hunters of deer:

children.text: iṣavas tasya naśyanti yo viddham anuvidhyati ||
children.translated_text: the arrows of a man who shoots again at what has already been wounded are wasted.

children.text: aśaktapretanaṣṭeṣu kṣetrikeṣv anivāritaḥ
children.translated_text: When field owners are incapable, dead, or missing, and there is no prohibition,

children.text: kṣetraṃ ced vikṛṣet kaścid aśnuvīta sa tatphalam ||
children.translated_text: if someone cultivates the field, he may enjoy its produce.

children.text: vikṛṣyamāṇe kṣetre cet kṣetrikaḥ punar āvrajet
children.translated_text: But if the field owner returns while the field is being cultivated,

children.text: khilopacāraṃ tat sarvaṃ dattvā svakṣetram āpnuyāt ||
children.translated_text: he obtains his own field after paying all the costs of improving the fallow land.

children.text: tadaṣṭabhāgāpacayād yāvat sapta gatāḥ samāḥ
children.translated_text: There is a deduction of one eighth from that amount until seven years have passed;

children.text: samprāpte tv aṣṭame varṣe bhuktaṃ kṣetraṃ labheta saḥ ||
children.translated_text: but when the eighth year has arrived, the cultivator obtains the field that he has enjoyed.

children.text: saṃvatsareṇārdhakhilaṃ khilaṃ tad vatsarais tribhiḥ
children.translated_text: In one year a field becomes half-fallow; in three years it becomes fallow.

children.text: pañcavarṣāvasannaṃ tu syāt kṣetram aṭavīsamam ||
children.translated_text: A field neglected for five years becomes like forest land.

children.text: kṣetraṃ tripuruṣaṃ yat syād gṛhaṃ vā syāt kramāgatam
children.translated_text: A field that has belonged to three generations, or a house inherited in succession,

children.text: rājaprasādād anyatra na tadbhogaḥ paraṃ nayet ||
children.translated_text: is not transferred to another by mere possession, except through the king's favor.

children.text: utkramya tu vṛtiṃ yatra sasyaghāto gavādibhiḥ
children.translated_text: Where, after crossing a fence, crop damage is done by cattle and the like,

children.text: pālaḥ śāsyo bhavet tatra na cecchaktyā nivārayet ||
children.translated_text: the herdsman should be punished there, if he does not prevent it as far as he is able.

children.text: samūlasasyanāśe tu tatsvāmī samam āpnuyāt
children.translated_text: But when the crop is destroyed root and all, its owner should receive an equal compensation.

children.text: vadhena pālo mucyeta daṇḍaṃ svāmini pātayet ||
children.translated_text: The herdsman may be discharged with corporal punishment; the fine should be made to fall on the owner.

children.text: gauḥ prasūtā daśāhāt ca mahokṣājāvikuñjarāḥ
children.translated_text: A cow that has calved within ten days, a powerful bull, goats, sheep, and elephants

children.text: nivāryās tu prayatnena teṣāṃ svāmī na daṇḍabhāk ||
children.translated_text: are to be warded off carefully; their owner is not liable to a fine.

children.text: māṣaṃ gāṃ dāpayed daṇḍaṃ dvau māṣau mahiṣīṃ tathā
children.translated_text: He should make the owner pay a fine of one <s>māṣa</s> for a cow, and likewise two <s>māṣas</s> for a buffalo.

children.text: ajāvike savatse tu daṇḍaḥ syād ardhamāṣakaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For a goat or sheep with its young, the fine should be half a <s>māṣa</s>.

children.text: adaṇḍyā hastino 'śvāś ca prajāpālā hi te smṛtāḥ
children.translated_text: Elephants and horses are not to be fined, for they are traditionally regarded as protectors of the people.

children.text: adaṇḍyā garbhiṇī gauś ca sūtikā cābhisāriṇī ||
children.translated_text: A pregnant cow too is not to be fined, nor one that has recently calved, nor one going to the bull.

children.text: proktas tu dvir niṣaṇṇānāṃ vasantyāṃ tu caturguṇam
children.translated_text: For animals that have settled down twice, a doubled penalty is prescribed; for one actually staying there, a fourfold penalty.

children.text: pratyakṣacārakāṇāṃ tu cauradaṇḍaḥ smṛtas tathā ||
children.translated_text: Likewise, for those that roam there in plain sight, the penalty is remembered as the penalty for a thief.

children.text: yā naṣṭāḥ pāladoṣeṇa gāvaḥ kṣetraṃ samāśritāḥ
children.translated_text: When cows, lost through the herdsman's fault, have entered a field,

children.text: na tatra gomino daṇḍaḥ pālas taṃ daṇḍam arhati ||
children.translated_text: there is no fine there for the cattle-owner; the herdsman deserves that fine.

children.text: rājagrāhagṛhīto vā vajrāśanihato 'pi vā
children.translated_text: If an animal has been seized by royal officers, or even struck by lightning,

children.text: atha sarpeṇa daṣṭo vā giryagrāt patito 'pi vā ||
children.translated_text: or bitten by a snake, or even fallen from a mountain peak,

children.text: siṃhavyāghrahato vāpi vyādhibhiḥ caiva pātitaḥ
children.translated_text: or killed by a lion or tiger, or brought down by diseases,

children.text: na tatra doṣaḥ pālasya na ca doṣo 'sti gominām ||
children.translated_text: there is no fault there on the herdsman's part, and no fault belongs to the cattle-owners.

children.text: gobhis tu bhakṣitaṃ dhānyaṃ yo naraḥ pratimārgati
children.translated_text: When a man seeks compensation for grain eaten by cows,

children.text: sāmantasya śado deyo dhānyaṃ yat tatra vāpitam
children.translated_text: the grain that was sown there should be paid according to the neighboring holder's assessment.

children.text: gavatraṃ gomine deyaṃ dhānyaṃ tatkarṣikasya tu ||
children.translated_text: What belongs to the cows is to be given to the cattle-owner, but the grain belongs to the cultivator.

children.text: grāmopānte ca yat kṣetraṃ vivītānte mahāpathe
children.translated_text: When a field lies at the edge of a village, at the edge of common pasture, or on a great road,

children.text: anāvṛte cet tannāśe na pālasya vyatikramaḥ ||
children.translated_text: if it is unenclosed, there is no transgression by the herdsman when it is damaged.

children.text: pathi kṣetre vṛtiḥ kāryā yām uṣṭro nāvalokayet
children.translated_text: By a road-side field a fence should be made which a camel cannot look over,

children.text: na laṅghayet paśur nāśvo na bhindyād yāṃ ca sūkaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: which cattle or horses cannot leap across, and which a pig cannot break.

children.text: gṛhaṃ kṣetraṃ ca vijñeyaṃ vāsahetuḥ kuṭumbinām
children.translated_text: A house and a field should be understood as the basis of residence for householders.

children.text: tasmāt tan nākṣiped rājā taddhi mūlaṃ kuṭumbinām ||
children.translated_text: Therefore the king should not confiscate them, for that is the root of householders' livelihood.

children.text: vṛddhe janapade rājño dharmaḥ kośaś ca vardhate
children.translated_text: When the countryside prospers, the king's <s>dharma</s> and treasury prosper.

children.text: hīyate hīyamāne ca vṛddhihetum ataḥ śrayet ||
children.translated_text: When it declines, they decline; therefore he should resort to what causes prosperity.

children.text: Chapter 15
vivāhādividhiḥ strīṇāṃ yatra puṃsāṃ ca kīrtyate
children.translated_text: The rule beginning with marriage, where it is stated for women and for men,

children.text: strīpuṃsayoganāmaitad vivādapadam ucyate ||
children.translated_text: is called this litigation topic named the union of woman and man.

children.text: strīpuṃsayos tu saṃbandhād varaṇaṃ prāg vidhīyate
children.translated_text: From the relation of woman and man, choosing is first prescribed.

children.text: varaṇād grahaṇaṃ pāṇeḥ saṃskāro 'tha dvilakṣaṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: After choosing comes the taking of the hand; then the consecration has a twofold mark.

children.text: tayor aniyataṃ proktaṃ varaṇaṃ doṣadarśanāt
children.translated_text: Of these two, choosing is said to be uncertain, because faults may be observed.

children.text: pāṇigrahaṇamantrābhyāṃ niyataṃ dāralakṣaṇam ||
children.translated_text: By the hand-taking and the mantras, the defining mark of wifehood becomes fixed.

children.text: brāhmaṇakṣatriyaviśāṃ śūdrāṇāṃ ca parigrahe
children.translated_text: In taking wives among <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, <s>kṣatriyas</s>, <s>vaiśyas</s>, and <s>śūdras</s>,

children.text: svajātyā śreyasī bhāryā svajātyaś ca patiḥ striyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: a wife of one's own caste is best, and for a woman a husband of her own caste is best.

children.text: brāhmaṇasyānulomyena striyo 'nyās tisra eva tu
children.translated_text: For a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, in the regular descending order, there are three other women as wives.

children.text: śūdrāyāḥ prātilomyena tathānye patayas trayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For a <s>śūdra</s> woman, in the inverse order, there are likewise three other husbands.

children.text: dve bhārye kṣatriyasyānye vaiśyasyaikā prakīrtitā
children.translated_text: For a <s>kṣatriya</s>, two other wives are declared; for a <s>vaiśya</s>, one.

children.text: vaiśyāyā dvau patī jñeyāv eko 'nyaḥ kṣatriyāpatiḥ ||
children.translated_text: For a <s>vaiśya</s> woman, two husbands should be known; one further husband is a <s>kṣatriya</s>.

children.text: ā saptamāt pañcamād vā bandhubhyaḥ pitṛmātṛtāḥ
children.translated_text: From relatives on the father's and mother's sides, up to the seventh or the fifth degree,

children.text: avivāhyāḥ sagotrāḥ syuḥ samānapravarās tathā ||
children.translated_text: those of the same <s>gotra</s> are not marriageable, nor are those of the same <s>pravara</s>.

children.text: parīkṣyaḥ puruṣaḥ puṃstve nijair evāṅgalakṣaṇaiḥ
children.translated_text: A man should be examined for manhood by his own bodily marks.

children.text: pumāṃś ced avikalpena sa kanyāṃ labdhum arhati ||
children.translated_text: If he is unmistakably male, he is fit to obtain a maiden.

children.text: subaddhajatrujānvasthiḥ subaddhāṃsaśirodharaḥ
children.translated_text: His collarbones, knees, and bones should be well joined, and his shoulders, head, and neck well formed.

children.text: sthūlaghāṭas tanūrutvag avilagnagatisvaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: He should have large joints, thin thigh-skin, and an unimpeded gait and voice.

children.text: viṭ cāsya plavate nāpsu hlādi mūtraṃ ca phenilam
children.translated_text: His feces float on water, and his urine is pleasant and foamy.

children.text: pumān syāṃl lakṣaṇair etair viparītais tu paṇḍakaḥ ||
children.translated_text: By these marks he is male; by the opposite marks he is a <s>paṇḍaka</s>.

children.text: caturdaśavidhaḥ śāstre sa tu dṛṣṭo manīṣibhiḥ
children.translated_text: In the <s>śāstra</s>, the wise have seen that he is of fourteen kinds.

children.text: cikitsyaś cācikitsyaś ca teṣām ukto vidhiḥ kramāt ||
children.translated_text: Some are curable and some incurable; the rule for them is stated in order.

children.text: nisargapaṇḍo vadhriś ca pakṣapaṇḍas tathaiva ca
children.translated_text: There is the natural <s>paṇḍaka</s>, the castrated man, and likewise the periodic <s>paṇḍaka</s>;

children.text: abhiśāpād guro rogād devakrodhāt tathaiva ca ||
children.translated_text: also one caused by a curse, by a grave disease, and by the anger of a deity.

children.text: īrṣyāpaṇḍaś ca sevyaś ca vātaretā mukhebhagaḥ
children.translated_text: There are the jealous <s>paṇḍaka</s>, the passive one, the one whose semen is wind-like, and the oral one;

children.text: ākṣipto moghabījaś ca śālīno 'nyapatis tathā ||
children.translated_text: the displaced one, the one with futile seed, the shy one, and the one who is a man with another's wife.

children.text: tatrādyāv apratīkarau pakṣākhyo māsam ācaret
children.translated_text: Of these, the first two are beyond remedy; the one called periodic should observe treatment for a month.

children.text: anukramāt trayasyāsya kālaḥ saṃvatsaraḥ smṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For the next three of this set, in sequence, the period is remembered as a year.

children.text: īrṣyāpaṇḍādayo ye 'nye catvāraḥ samudāhṛtāḥ
children.translated_text: The other four that are mentioned beginning with the jealous <s>paṇḍaka</s>

children.text: saṃtyaktavyāḥ patitavat kṣatayonyā api striyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: are to be abandoned like fallen persons, as are women whose sexual organ is injured.

children.text: ākṣiptamoghabījābhyām patyāv apratikarmaṇi
children.translated_text: When husbands are of the displaced or futile-seed kinds and no remedy is possible,

children.text: patir anyaḥ smṛto nāryā vatsaraṃ saṃpratīkṣya tu ||
children.translated_text: another husband is prescribed for the woman after she has waited a year.

children.text: śālīnasyāpi dhṛṣṭastrīsaṃyogād bhajyate dhvajaḥ
children.translated_text: Even in the shy man, his organ fails from union with a bold woman.

children.text: taṃ hīnavegam anyastrībālādyābhir upakramet ||
children.translated_text: One should treat him, whose vigor is weak, by means of other women, young women, and the like.

children.text: anyasyām yo manuṣyaḥ syād amanuṣyaḥ svayoṣiti
children.translated_text: If a man is a man with another woman but not a man with his own wife,

children.text: labheta sānyaṃ bhartāram etat kāryaṃ prajāpateḥ ||
children.translated_text: she may obtain another husband; this is the ordinance of <s>Prajāpati</s>.

children.text: apatyārthaṃ striyaḥ sṛṣṭāḥ strī kṣetraṃ bījinaḥ prajāḥ
children.translated_text: Women were created for offspring: the woman is the field, and progeny belongs to the possessor of seed.

children.text: kṣetraṃ bījavate deyaṃ nābījī kṣetram arhati ||
children.translated_text: The field should be given to one who has seed; one without seed is not entitled to the field.

children.text: pitā dadyāt svayaṃ kanyām bhrātā vānumate pituḥ
children.translated_text: The father should give the maiden himself, or the brother with the father's consent.

children.text: mātāmaho mātulaś ca sakulyā bāndhavās tathā ||
children.translated_text: The maternal grandfather and maternal uncle, and also members of the family and relatives, may do so likewise.

children.text: mātābhāve tu sarveṣāṃ prakṛtau yadi vartate
children.translated_text: In the absence of all of them, the mother may give her, if she is in her proper state.

children.text: tasyām aprakṛtisthāyāṃ dadyuḥ kanyāṃ svajātayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: If she is not in her proper state, people of the maiden's own caste should give her.

children.text: yadā tu naiva kaścit syāt kanyā rājānam āvrajet
children.translated_text: But when there is no one at all, the maiden should approach the king.

children.text: anujñayā tasya varaṃ pratītya varayet svayam ||
children.translated_text: With his permission, having accepted a suitor, she may choose for herself.

children.text: savarṇam anurūpaṃ ca kularūpavayaḥśrutaiḥ
children.translated_text: He should be of the same caste and suitable in family, appearance, age, and learning.

children.text: saha dharmaṃ caret tena putrāṃś cotpādayet tataḥ ||
children.translated_text: With him she should practice <s>dharma</s> and then produce sons.

children.text: pratigṛhya ca yaḥ kanyāṃ naro deśāntaraṃ vrajet
children.translated_text: If a man, after receiving a maiden, goes to another country,

children.text: trīn ṛtūn samatikramya kanyānyaṃ varayed varam ||
children.translated_text: after three menstrual periods have passed, the maiden may choose another suitor.

children.text: kanyā nartum upekṣeta bāndhavebhyo nivedayet
children.translated_text: A maiden should not let her season pass; she should inform her relatives.

children.text: te cen na dadyus tāṃ bhartre te syur bhrūṇahabhiḥ samāḥ ||
children.translated_text: If they do not give her to a husband, they become equal to embryo-killers.

children.text: yāvantaś cartavas tasyāḥ samatītā patiṃ vinā
children.translated_text: As many seasons of hers as pass without a husband,

children.text: tāvatyo bhrūṇahatyāḥ syus tasya yo na dadāti tām ||
children.translated_text: so many embryo-killings belong to the one who does not give her in marriage.

children.text: ato 'pravṛtte rajasi kanyāṃ dadyāt pitā sakṛt
children.translated_text: Therefore, before menstruation has begun, a father should give a maiden once in marriage.

children.text: mahad enaḥ spṛśed enam anyathaiṣa vidhiḥ satām ||
children.translated_text: Otherwise great sin would touch him; this is the rule of the virtuous.

children.text: sakṛd aṃśo nipatati sakṛt kanyā pradīyate
children.translated_text: A share falls only once; a maiden is given only once;

children.text: sakṛd āha dadānīti trīṇy etāni sakṛt sakṛt ||
children.translated_text: one says, "I give," only once: these three things are once and once only.

children.text: brāhmādiṣu vivāheṣu pañcasv eṣu vidhiḥ smṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: In the five marriages beginning with <s>Brāhma</s>, this rule is remembered;

children.text: guṇāpekṣaṃ bhaved dānam āsurādiṣu ca triṣu ||
children.translated_text: and in the three beginning with <s>Āsura</s>, the giving should depend on qualities.

children.text: kanyāyām prāptaśulkāyāṃ jyāyāṃś ced vara āvrajet
children.translated_text: When a superior suitor approaches a maiden for whom bride-price has already been received,

children.text: dharmārthakāmasaṃyuktaṃ vācyaṃ tatrānṛtaṃ bhavet ||
children.translated_text: in that case an untruth connected with <s>dharma</s>, wealth, and desire may be spoken.

children.text: nāduṣṭāṃ dūṣayet kanyāṃ nāduṣṭaṃ dūṣayed varam
children.translated_text: One should not fault a maiden who has no defect, nor fault a suitor who has no defect.

children.text: doṣe tu sati nāgaḥ syād anyonyaṃ tyajatos tayoḥ ||
children.translated_text: But when a defect is present, there is no offense if the two abandon one another.

children.text: dattvā nyāyena yaḥ kanyāṃ varāya na dadāti tām
children.translated_text: If, after giving a maiden lawfully to a suitor, a man does not hand her over to him,

children.text: aduṣṭaś ced varo rājñā sa daṇḍyas tatra coravat ||
children.translated_text: then, if the suitor is without defect, that man should be punished by the king there like a thief.

children.text: yas tu doṣavatīṃ kanyām anākhyāya prayacchati
children.translated_text: But one who gives a defective maiden without declaring it

children.text: tasya kuryān nṛpo daṇḍaṃ pūrvasāhasacoditam ||
children.translated_text: should be made by the king to pay the fine prescribed as the first <s>sāhasa</s> penalty.

children.text: akanyeti tu yaḥ kanyāṃ brūyād dveṣeṇa mānavaḥ
children.translated_text: If a man, out of hatred, says of a maiden, "She is not a maiden,"

children.text: sa śataṃ prāpnuyād daṇḍaṃ tasyā doṣam adarśayan ||
children.translated_text: without showing a defect in her, he should incur a fine of one hundred.

children.text: pratigṛhya tu yaḥ kanyām aduṣṭām utsṛjed varaḥ
children.translated_text: But if a suitor, after accepting a maiden who has no defect, abandons her,

children.text: vineyaḥ so 'py akāmo 'pi kanyāṃ tām eva codvahet ||
children.translated_text: he too should be disciplined; even unwilling, he must marry that same maiden.

children.text: dīrghakutsitarogārtā vyaṅgā saṃsṛṣṭamaithunā
children.translated_text: Afflicted with a long or loathsome disease, deformed, one who has had sexual intercourse,

children.text: dhṛṣṭānyagatabhāvā ca kanyādoṣāḥ prakīrtitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: bold, and one whose feeling has gone to another: these are declared to be defects of a maiden.

children.text: unmattaḥ patitaḥ klībo durbhagas tyaktabāndhavaḥ
children.translated_text: Insane, fallen, impotent, unfortunate, abandoned by relatives,

children.text: kanyādoṣau ca yau pūrvau eṣa doṣagaṇo vare ||
children.translated_text: and the two earlier defects listed for a maiden: this is the group of defects in a suitor.

children.text: aṣṭau vivāhā varṇānāṃ saṃskārārthaṃ prakīrtitāḥ
children.translated_text: Eight marriages for the <s>varṇas</s> are proclaimed for the sake of sacramental consecration.

children.text: brāhmas tu prathamas teṣāṃ prājāpatyas tathaiva ca ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Brāhma</s> is the first of them, and likewise the <s>Prājāpatya</s>;

children.text: ārṣaś caivātha daivaś ca gāndharvaś cāsuras tathā
children.translated_text: then the <s>Ārṣa</s> and the <s>Daiva</s>, also the <s>Gāndharva</s> and the <s>Āsura</s>;

children.text: rākṣaso 'nantaras tasmāt paiśācas tv aṣṭamaḥ smṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: after that is the <s>Rākṣasa</s>, while the <s>Paiśāca</s> is remembered as the eighth.

children.text: satkṛtyāhūya kanyāṃ tu brāhme dadyāttv alaṃkṛtām
children.translated_text: In the <s>Brāhma</s> rite, one should honorably invite the man and give the adorned maiden.

children.text: saha dharmaṃ carety uktvā prājāpatyo vidhīyate ||
children.translated_text: When he says, "Practice <s>dharma</s> together," it is prescribed as the <s>Prājāpatya</s> rite.

children.text: vastragomithune dattvā vivāhas tv ārṣa ucyate
children.translated_text: When a pair of garments and cattle has been given, the marriage is called <s>Ārṣa</s>.

children.text: antarvedyāṃ tu daivaḥ syād ṛtvije karma kurvate ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Daiva</s> occurs within the altar-enclosure, to the officiating priest who is performing the rite.

children.text: icchantīm icchate prāhur gāndharvo nāma pañcamam
children.translated_text: When a willing woman desires a willing man, they call the fifth marriage <s>Gāndharva</s> by name.

children.text: vivāhas tv āsuro jñeyaḥ śulkasaṃvyavahārataḥ ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Āsura</s> marriage should be understood from the transaction in bride-price.

children.text: prasahya haraṇād ukto vivāho rākṣasas tathā
children.translated_text: Because of forcible carrying off, a marriage is called <s>Rākṣasa</s>.

children.text: suptamattopagamanāt paiśācas tv aṣṭamo 'dhamaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Because of approaching a sleeping or intoxicated woman, the eighth, <s>Paiśāca</s>, is the lowest.

children.text: eṣāṃ tu dharmyāś catvāro brāhmādyāḥ samudāhṛtāḥ
children.translated_text: Of these, the four lawful ones are said to be the <s>Brāhma</s> and those beginning with it.

children.text: sādhāraṇaḥ syād gāndharvas trayo 'dharmyās tv ataḥ pare ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Gāndharva</s> is common to both; the three after it are unlawful.

children.text: parapūrvāḥ striyas tv anyāḥ sapta proktā yathākramam
children.translated_text: Other women who have had a previous man are declared to be seven, in order.

children.text: punarbhūs trividhā tāsāṃ svairiṇī tu caturvidhā ||
children.translated_text: Among them, the <s>punarbhū</s> (remarried woman) is threefold, while the <s>svairiṇī</s> (self-willed woman) is fourfold.

children.text: kanyaivākṣatayonir yā pāṇigrahaṇadūṣitā
children.translated_text: A woman who is still a maiden, with her womb intact, but has been affected by the taking of her hand,

children.text: punarbhūḥ prathamā soktā punaḥ saṃskāram arhati ||
children.translated_text: is called the first <s>punarbhū</s>; she is eligible for a second marriage rite.

children.text: kaumāraṃ patim utsṛjya yānyaṃ puruṣam āśritā
children.translated_text: She who abandons the husband of her maidenhood and resorts to another man,

children.text: punaḥ patyur gṛham yāyāt sā dvitīyā prakīrtitā ||
children.translated_text: and then goes again to her husband's house, is declared to be the second.

children.text: asatsu devareṣu strī bāndhavair yā pradīyate
children.translated_text: A woman who, when there are no suitable brothers-in-law, is given by her relatives

children.text: savarṇāyāsapiṇḍāya sā tṛtīyā prakīrtitā ||
children.translated_text: to a man of the same <s>varṇa</s> and not a <s>sapiṇḍa</s> relative is declared to be the third.

children.text: strī prasūtāprasūtā vā patyāv eva tu jīvati
children.translated_text: A woman, whether she has borne children or not, while her husband is still alive,

children.text: kāmāt samāśrayed anyaṃ prathamā svairiṇī tu sā ||
children.translated_text: who from desire resorts to another man: she is the first <s>svairiṇī</s>.

children.text: mṛte bhartari yā prāptān devarān apy apāsya tu
children.translated_text: When her husband has died, she who, even rejecting available brothers-in-law,

children.text: upagacchet paraṃ kāmāt sā dvitīyā prakīrtitā ||
children.translated_text: goes to another man from desire is declared to be the second.

children.text: prāptā deśād dhanakrītā kṣutpipāsāturā ca yā
children.translated_text: She who has come from another region, been bought with money, or is afflicted by hunger and thirst,

children.text: tavāham ity upagatā sā tṛtīyā prakīrtitā ||
children.translated_text: and approaches saying, "I am yours," is declared to be the third.

children.text: deśadharmān apekṣya strī gurubhir yā pradīyate
children.translated_text: A woman who, with regard for local custom, is given by her elders

children.text: utpannasāhasānyasmai sāntyā vai svairiṇī smṛtā ||
children.translated_text: to another man after an act of force has occurred: she is remembered as the last <s>svairiṇī</s>.

children.text: punarbhuvāṃ eṣa vidhiḥ svairiṇīnāṃ ca kīrtitaḥ
children.translated_text: This rule has been stated for <s>punarbhū</s> women and for <s>svairiṇī</s> women.

children.text: pūrvā pūrvā jaghanyāsāṃ śreyasī tūttarottarā ||
children.translated_text: Among these inferior categories, each earlier one is better than the one that follows.

children.text: apatyam utpādayitus tāsāṃ yā śulkato hṛtā
children.translated_text: Among them, the child of a woman taken for bride-price belongs to the begetter.

children.text: aśulkopanatāyāṃ tu kṣetrikasyaiva tat phalam ||
children.translated_text: But in the case of one brought without bride-price, that fruit belongs only to the owner of the field.

children.text: kṣetrikasya yad ajñātaṃ kṣetre bījaṃ pradīyate
children.translated_text: When seed unknown to the field-owner is deposited in a field,

children.text: na tatra bījino bhāgaḥ kṣetrikasyaiva tad bhavet ||
children.translated_text: the sower has no share there; it belongs only to the field-owner.

children.text: oghavātāhṛtaṃ bījaṃ kṣetre yasya prarohati
children.translated_text: When seed carried by flood or wind sprouts in someone's field,

children.text: phalabhug yasya tat kṣetraṃ na bījī phalabhāg bhavet ||
children.translated_text: the one whose field it is enjoys the fruit; the sower does not share in the fruit.

children.text: mahokṣo janayed vatsān yasya goṣu vraje caran
children.translated_text: If a great bull, roaming in a herd, begets calves among someone's cows,

children.text: tasya te yasya tā gāvo moghaṃ syanditam ārṣabham ||
children.translated_text: they belong to the one whose cows they are; the bull's discharge is in vain.

children.text: kṣetrikānumataṃ bījaṃ yasya kṣetre pramucyate
children.translated_text: When seed permitted by the field-owner is released in someone's field,

children.text: tadapatyaṃ dvayor eva bījikṣetrikayor matam ||
children.translated_text: that offspring is considered to belong to both, the <s>bījī</s> (seed-giver) and the <s>kṣetrika</s> (field-owner).

children.text: narte kṣetraṃ bhavet sasyaṃ na ca bījaṃ vināsti tat
children.translated_text: Without a field there is no crop, and without seed that crop does not exist either.

children.text: ato 'patyaṃ dvayor iṣṭaṃ pitur mātuś ca dharmataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, according to <s>dharma</s>, offspring is held to belong to both father and mother.

children.text: nāthavatyā paragṛhe saṃyuktasya striyā saha
children.translated_text: When a woman who has a protector is joined with a man in another's house,

children.text: dṛṣṭaṃ saṃgrahaṇaṃ tajjñair nāgatāyāḥ svayaṃ gṛhe ||
children.translated_text: experts recognize that as <s>saṃgrahaṇa</s> (illicit association), not when she has come by herself to his own house.

children.text: praduṣṭatyaktadārasya klībasya kṣamakasya ca
children.translated_text: For a man whose wife is corrupt and abandoned, for an impotent man, and for one who is tolerant,

children.text: svecchayopeyuṣo dārān na doṣaḥ sāhaso bhavet ||
children.translated_text: there is no fault or violent offense when another approaches the wife by her own wish.

children.text: parastriyā sahākāle 'deśe vā bhavato mithaḥ
children.translated_text: When a man and another's wife are together at an improper time or in an improper place,

children.text: sthānasaṃbhāṣaṇāmodās trayaḥ saṃgrahaṇakramāḥ ||
children.translated_text: standing together, conversation, and pleasurable contact are the three stages of <s>saṃgrahaṇa</s>.

children.text: nadīnāṃ saṃgame tīrtheṣv ārāmeṣu vaneṣu ca
children.translated_text: At river confluences, at sacred fords, in parks, and in forests,

children.text: strī pumāṃś ca sameyātāṃ grāhyaṃ saṃgrahaṇaṃ bhavet ||
children.translated_text: if a woman and a man meet, it should be treated as <s>saṃgrahaṇa</s>.

children.text: dūtīprasthāpanaiś caiva lekhāsaṃpreṣaṇair api
children.translated_text: By sending a female go-between, and also by dispatching letters,

children.text: anyair api vyabhicāraiḥ sarvaṃ saṃgrahaṇaṃ smṛtam ||
children.translated_text: and by any other adulterous approaches, all this is regarded as <s>saṃgrahaṇa</s> (illicit sexual approach).

children.text: striyaṃ spṛśed adeśe yaḥ spṛṣṭo vā marśayet tathā
children.translated_text: A man who touches a woman in an improper place, or, when touched, fondles her likewise,

children.text: parasparasyānumate tac ca saṃgrahaṇaṃ bhavet ||
children.translated_text: with the other's consent: that too becomes <s>saṃgrahaṇa</s>.

children.text: bhakṣair vā yadi vā bhojyair vastrair mālyais tathaiva ca
children.translated_text: With chewable foods or with prepared foods, and likewise with garments and garlands,

children.text: saṃpreṣyamānair gandhaiś ca sarvaṃ saṃgrahaṇaṃ smṛtam ||
children.translated_text: and with perfumes that are sent, all this is regarded as <s>saṃgrahaṇa</s>.

children.text: darpād vā yadi vā mohācchlāghayā vā svayaṃ vadet
children.translated_text: If, from pride, delusion, or boasting, he himself should say,

children.text: mameyaṃ bhuktapūrveti sarvaṃ saṃgrahaṇaṃ smṛtam ||
children.translated_text: 'This woman was formerly enjoyed by me,' all this is regarded as <s>saṃgrahaṇa</s>.

children.text: pāṇau yaś ca nigṛhṇīyād veṇyāṃ vastrāntare 'pi vā
children.translated_text: And if he should seize her by the hand, by the braid, or even by the edge of her garment,

children.text: tiṣṭha tiṣṭheti vā brūyāt sarvaṃ saṃgrahaṇaṃ smṛtam ||
children.translated_text: or should say, 'Stay, stay,' all this is regarded as <s>saṃgrahaṇa</s>.

children.text: svajātyatikrame puṃsāṃ uktam uttamasāhasam
children.translated_text: For men, in a same-caste sexual offense, the highest <s>sāhasa</s> fine is prescribed;

children.text: viparyaye madhyamas tu prātilome pramāpaṇam ||
children.translated_text: in the opposite case the middle fine, but in a <s>prātiloma</s> offense, execution.

children.text: kanyāyām asakāmāyāṃ dvyaṅgulasyāvakartanam
children.translated_text: In the case of an unwilling maiden, the penalty is cutting off two fingers;

children.text: uttamāyāṃ vadhas tv eva sarvasvaharaṇaṃ tathā ||
children.translated_text: if she is of higher rank, it is death itself, and likewise confiscation of all property.

children.text: sakāmāyāṃ tu kanyāyāṃ savarṇe nāsty atikramaḥ
children.translated_text: But in the case of a willing maiden of the same caste there is no offense;

children.text: kiṃtv alaṃkṛtya satkṛtya sa evaināṃ samudvahet ||
children.translated_text: rather, after adorning and honoring her, that very man should marry her.

children.text: mātā mātṛṣvasā śvaśrūr mātulānī pitṛṣvasā
children.translated_text: A mother, maternal aunt, mother-in-law, maternal uncle's wife, paternal aunt,

children.text: pitṛvyasakhiśiṣyastrī bhaginī tatsakhī snuṣā ||
children.translated_text: a paternal uncle's female friend, a pupil's wife, a sister, her female friend, and a daughter-in-law,

children.text: duhitācāryabhāryā ca sagotrā śaraṇāgatā
children.translated_text: a daughter, the teacher's wife, a woman of the same <s>gotra</s>, one who has sought refuge,

children.text: rājñī pravrajitā dhātrī sādhvī varṇottamā ca yā ||
children.translated_text: a queen, a woman who has gone forth, a nurse, a chaste woman, and one superior in caste:

children.text: āsām anyatamāṃ gatvā gurutalpaga ucyate
children.translated_text: having intercourse with any one of these, a man is called a <s>gurutalpaga</s> (violator of the guru's bed);

children.text: śiśnasyotkartanaṃ daṇḍo nānyas tatra vidhīyate ||
children.translated_text: the penalty is cutting off the penis; no other penalty is prescribed there.

children.text: paśuyonyām atikrāman vineyaḥ sa damaṃ śatam
children.translated_text: A man committing sexual violation with an animal is to be punished with a fine of one hundred;

children.text: madhyamaṃ sāhasaṃ goṣu tad evāntyāvasāyiṣu ||
children.translated_text: with cows, the middle <s>sāhasa</s> fine applies, and the same with <s>antyāvasāyins</s> (outcaste residents).

children.text: agamyāgāminaḥ śāsti daṇḍo rājñā pracoditaḥ
children.translated_text: For one who goes to a woman who must not be approached, punishment imposed by the king chastises him;

children.text: prāyaścittavidhāv atra prāyaścittaṃ viśodhanam ||
children.translated_text: in the rule for expiation here, <s>prāyaścitta</s> (expiation) is the purification.

children.text: svairiṇy abrāhmaṇī veśyā dāsī niṣkāsinī ca yā
children.translated_text: A wanton woman, a non-Brahmin woman, a prostitute, a slave woman, and one who has been cast out,

children.text: gamyāḥ syur ānulomyena striyo na pratilomataḥ ||
children.translated_text: may be approached in the <s>ānulomya</s> order, but not in reverse caste order.

children.text: āsv eva tu bhujiṣyāsu doṣaḥ syāt paradāravat
children.translated_text: But with these very women, if they are in another's possession, the fault is like that for another man's wife;

children.text: gamyā api hi nopeyās tāś ced anyaparigrahāḥ ||
children.translated_text: for even women who are otherwise approachable must not be approached if they are in another's keeping.

children.text: anutpannaprajāyās tu patiḥ preyād yadi striyāḥ
children.translated_text: But if a woman's husband should die before offspring has been produced,

children.text: niyuktā gurubhir gacched devaraṃ putrakāmyayā ||
children.translated_text: then, appointed by her elders and desiring a son, she should approach the <s>devara</s> (her husband's brother).

children.text: sa ca tāṃ pratipadyeta tathaiva putrajanmataḥ
children.translated_text: He too should approach her in the same way until the birth of a son;

children.text: putre jāte nivarteta viplavaḥ syād ato 'nyathā ||
children.translated_text: once a son is born he should desist, for otherwise there would be disorder.

children.text: ghṛtenābhyajya gātrāṇi tailenāvikṛtena vā
children.translated_text: Having anointed his limbs with ghee, or with oil that has not been altered,

children.text: mukhān mukhaṃ pariharan gātrair gātrāṇy asaṃspṛśan ||
children.translated_text: he should avoid mouth-to-mouth contact and should not touch her limbs with his limbs.

children.text: striyaṃ putravatīṃ vandhyāṃ nīrajaskām anicchantīm
children.translated_text: He must not approach a woman who already has a son, is barren, has no menstrual flow, or is unwilling,

children.text: na gacched garbhiṇīṃ nindyām aniyuktāṃ ca bandhubhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: nor one who is pregnant, blameworthy, or not appointed by her kinsmen.

children.text: aniyuktā tu yā nārī devarāj janayet sutam
children.translated_text: But a woman who, without being appointed, bears a son from a <s>devara</s>,

children.text: jārajātam arikthīyaṃ tam āhur dharmavādinaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the expounders of <s>dharma</s> call that son adulterine-born and without inheritance.

children.text: tathāniyukto bhāryāyāṃ yavīyāñ jyāyaso vrajet
children.translated_text: Likewise, if a younger brother, unappointed, approaches the wife of his elder brother,

children.text: yavīyaso vā yo jyāyān ubhau tau gurutalpagau ||
children.translated_text: or if an elder approaches the wife of the younger, both are <s>gurutalpagas</s>.

children.text: kule tadavaśeṣe tu saṃtānārthaṃ na kāmataḥ
children.translated_text: But when only that remnant of the family remains, for the sake of lineage and not from desire,

children.text: niyukto gurubhir gacched bhrātṛbhāryāṃ yavīyasaḥ ||
children.translated_text: one appointed by the elders may approach the wife of his younger brother.

children.text: avidyamāne tu gurau rājño vācyaḥ kulakṣayaḥ
children.translated_text: But when no elder is present, the extinction of the family should be reported to the king;

children.text: tatas tadvacanād gacched anuśiṣya striyā saha ||
children.translated_text: then, at his command, having instructed the woman, he may approach her.

children.text: pūrvoktenaiva vidhinā snātāṃ puṃsavane śuciḥ
children.translated_text: By the very procedure stated earlier, when she has bathed at the time for begetting a male and is pure,

children.text: sakṛd ā garbhādhānād vā kṛte garbhe snuṣaiva sā ||
children.translated_text: he may approach once, or until conception; when pregnancy has occurred, she is simply a daughter-in-law.

children.text: ato 'nyathā vartamānaḥ pumān strī vāpi kāmataḥ
children.translated_text: A man or woman behaving otherwise from desire

children.text: vineyau subhṛśaṃ rājñā kilbiṣī syād anigrahāt ||
children.translated_text: should be punished very severely by the king, for if not restrained the person becomes guilty.

children.text: īrṣyāsūyasamutthe tu saṃrambhe rāgahetuke
children.translated_text: In a quarrel arising from jealousy or resentment and caused by passion,

children.text: dampatī vivadeyātāṃ na jñātiṣu na rājani ||
children.translated_text: husband and wife may dispute with one another, but not before relatives and not before the king.

children.text: anyonyaṃ tyajator nāgaḥ syād anyonyaviruddhayoḥ
children.translated_text: There is no fault when two mutually opposed spouses abandon one another,

children.text: strīpuṃsayor nigūḍhāyā vyabhicārād ṛte striyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: except in the case of concealed adultery by the woman.

children.text: vyabhicāre striyā mauṇḍyam adhaḥśayanam eva ca
children.translated_text: For a woman's adultery, the punishment is shaving her head and sleeping on the ground,

children.text: kadannaṃ vā kuvāsaś ca karma cāvaskaroñjhanam ||
children.translated_text: bad food or poor clothing, and the work of removing refuse.

children.text: strīdhanabhraṣṭasarvasvāṃ garbhavisraṃsinīṃ tathā
children.translated_text: After stripping her of her <s>strīdhana</s> (woman's property) and all possessions, and likewise if she causes miscarriage,

children.text: bhartuś ca vadham icchantīṃ striyaṃ nirvāsayed gṛhāt ||
children.translated_text: or seeks her husband's death, one should expel such a woman from the house.

children.text: anarthaśīlāṃ satataṃ tathaivāpriyavādinīm
children.translated_text: A woman whose conduct is harmful and who constantly speaks unpleasantly,

children.text: pūrvāśinīṃ ca yā bhartuḥ striyaṃ nirvāsayed budhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and who eats before her husband: the wise man should expel such a woman.

children.text: vandhyāṃ strījananīṃ nindyāṃ pratikulāṃ ca sarvadā
children.translated_text: A barren wife, one who bears only female children, one blameworthy and always hostile,

children.text: kāmato nābhinandeta kurvann evaṃ sa doṣabhāk ||
children.translated_text: he should not favor out of desire; acting so, he incurs fault.

children.text: anukūlām avāgduṣṭāṃ dakṣāṃ sādhvīṃ prajāvatīm
children.translated_text: But if he abandons a wife who is compliant, not foul in speech, capable, virtuous, and has offspring,

children.text: tyajan bhāryām avasthāpyo rājñā daṇḍena bhūyasā ||
children.translated_text: he should be made to remain by the king through a very heavy fine.

children.text: ajñātadoṣeṇoḍhā yā nirgatā nānyam āśritā
children.translated_text: A woman who was married when the man's fault was unknown, and who has gone away without resorting to another,

children.text: bandhubhiḥ sā niyoktavyā nirbandhuḥ svayam āśrayet ||
children.translated_text: should be assigned by her relatives; if she has no relatives, she may choose her own support.

children.text: naṣṭe mṛte pravrajite klībe ca patite patau
children.translated_text: When a husband is lost, dead, has gone forth, is impotent, or has fallen,

children.text: pañcasv āpatsu nārīṇāṃ patir anyo vidhīyate ||
children.translated_text: in these five calamities another husband is prescribed for women.

children.text: aṣṭau varṣāṇy udīkṣeta brāhmaṇī proṣitaṃ patim
children.translated_text: A <s>brāhmaṇī</s> should wait eight years for a husband who is away abroad;

children.text: aprasūtā tu catvāri parato 'nyaṃ samāśrayet ||
children.translated_text: if she has not borne children, four years; after that she may resort to another.

children.text: kṣatriyā ṣaṭ samās tiṣṭhed aprasūtā samātrayam
children.translated_text: A <s>kṣatriyā</s> with children should remain six years; if childless, three years;

children.text: vaiśyā prasūtā catvāri dve same tv itarā vaset ||
children.translated_text: a <s>vaiśyā</s> with children should remain four years, while the other should stay two years.

children.text: na śūdrāyāḥ smṛtaḥ kālo na ca dharmavyatikramaḥ
children.translated_text: For a <s>śūdrā</s> no fixed time is remembered, nor is there a transgression of <s>dharma</s>;

children.text: viśeṣato 'prasūtāyāḥ saṃvatsaraparā sthitiḥ ||
children.translated_text: especially for one without children, her stay is limited to one year.

children.text: apravṛttau smṛtaḥ dharma eṣa proṣitayoṣitām
children.translated_text: In the absence of offspring, this is the <s>dharma</s> prescribed for women whose husbands are abroad.

children.text: jīvati śrūyamāṇe tu syād eṣa dviguṇo vidhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: But if he is heard to be alive, this rule should be twice as long.

children.text: prajāpravṛttau bhūtānāṃ sṛṣṭir eṣā prajāpateḥ
children.translated_text: For the production of offspring among beings, this is the creation ordained by <s>Prajāpati</s>.

children.text: ato 'nyagamane strīṇām evaṃ doṣo na vidyate ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, when women go to another man in this way, no fault is found.

children.text: ānulomyena varṇānāṃ yaj janma sa vidhiḥ smṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: The birth that occurs among the <s>varṇas</s> in regular descending order is remembered as the rule.

children.text: prātilomyena yaj janma sa jñeyo varṇasaṃkaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: The birth that occurs in the reverse order should be known as <s>varṇasaṃkara</s> (mixing of social classes).

children.text: anantaraḥ smṛtaḥ putraḥ putra ekāntaras tathā
children.translated_text: A son is remembered as immediate, as separated by one interval,

children.text: dvyantaraś cānulomyena tathaiva pratilomataḥ ||
children.translated_text: and as separated by two intervals, both in the regular and in the reverse order.

children.text: ugraḥ pāraśavaś caiva niṣādaś cānulomataḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Ugra</s>, <s>Pāraśava</s>, and <s>Niṣāda</s>, in the regular order,

children.text: uttamebhyas trayas tribhyaḥ śūdrāputrāḥ prakīrtitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: are declared to be the three sons of a <s>Śūdrā</s> by the three higher classes.

children.text: brāhmaṇyā api cāṇḍālasūtavaidehakā api
children.translated_text: And <s>Cāṇḍāla</s>, <s>Sūta</s>, and <s>Vaidehaka</s>, born from a <s>Brāhmaṇī</s>,

children.text: aparebhyas trayas tribhyo vijñeyaḥ pratilomataḥ ||
children.translated_text: are to be understood as the three from the three lower classes, in the reverse order.

children.text: ambaṣṭho māgadhaś caiva kṣattā ca kṣatriyāsutāḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Ambaṣṭha</s>, <s>Māgadha</s>, and <s>Kṣattṛ</s> are sons of a <s>Kṣatriyā</s>;

children.text: ānulomyena tatraiko dvau jñeyau pratilomataḥ ||
children.translated_text: among them one is in the regular order, while two are to be known as in the reverse order.

children.text: vaiśyāputrās tu dauṣṣantayavanāyogavā api
children.translated_text: The sons of a <s>Vaiśyā</s> are also <s>Dauṣṣanta</s>, <s>Yavana</s>, and <s>Āyogava</s>;

children.text: prātilomyena yatraiko dvau jñeyau cānulomajau ||
children.translated_text: where one is by reverse order, and two are to be known as born in the regular order.

children.text: sūtādyāḥ pratilomās tu ye jātipratilomajāḥ
children.translated_text: But those beginning with <s>Sūta</s>, who are reverse-order births of their classes, are reverse-order offspring;

children.text: te saṃkarāḥ śvapākādyās teṣāṃ triḥ saptako gaṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: they are mixed classes, beginning with <s>Śvapāka</s>; their group numbers three times seven.

children.text: savarṇo brāhmaṇīputraḥ kṣatriyāyām anantaraḥ
children.translated_text: The son of a <s>Brāhmaṇī</s> is of the same class; in a <s>Kṣatriyā</s> he is immediately next.

children.text: ambaṣṭhograu tathā putrāv evaṃ kṣatriyavaiśyayoḥ ||
children.translated_text: So too <s>Ambaṣṭha</s> and <s>Ugra</s> are sons in the cases of the <s>Kṣatriya</s> and the <s>Vaiśya</s>.

children.text: ekāntaras tu dauṣṣanto vaiśyāyāṃ brāhmaṇāt sutaḥ
children.translated_text: The one-interval son <s>Dauṣṣanta</s> is born from a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> in a <s>Vaiśyā</s>.

children.text: śūdrāyāṃ kṣatriyāt tadvan niṣādo nāma jāyate ||
children.translated_text: In the same way, from a <s>Kṣatriya</s> in a <s>Śūdrā</s>, one called <s>Niṣāda</s> is born.

children.text: śūdrā pāraśavaṃ sūte brāhmaṇād uttaraṃ sutam
children.translated_text: A <s>Śūdrā</s> bears a <s>Pāraśava</s>, the further son from a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>.

children.text: ānulomyena varṇānāṃ putrā hy ete prakīrtitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: These indeed are declared to be the sons of the <s>varṇas</s> in the regular order.

children.text: sūtaś ca māgadhaś caiva putrāv āyogavas tathā
children.translated_text: <s>Sūta</s>, <s>Māgadha</s>, and likewise <s>Āyogava</s> as sons

children.text: prātilomyena varṇānāṃ tadvad ete 'py anantarāḥ ||
children.translated_text: are similarly immediate offspring of the <s>varṇas</s> in the reverse order.

children.text: anantaraḥ smṛtaḥ sūto brāhmaṇyāṃ kṣatriyāt sutaḥ
children.translated_text: An immediate reverse-order son is <s>Sūta</s>, born from a <s>Kṣatriya</s> in a <s>Brāhmaṇī</s>.

children.text: māgadhāyogavau tadvad dvī putrau vaiśyaśūdrayoḥ ||
children.translated_text: Likewise <s>Māgadha</s> and <s>Āyogava</s> are the two sons of a <s>Vaiśya</s> and a <s>Śūdra</s>.

children.text: brāhmaṇy ekāntaraṃ vaiśyāt sūte vaidehakaṃ sutam
children.translated_text: From a <s>Vaiśya</s>, a <s>Brāhmaṇī</s> bears <s>Vaidehaka</s>, a one-interval son.

children.text: kṣattāraṃ kṣatriyā śūdrāt putram ekāntaraṃ tathā ||
children.translated_text: A <s>Kṣatriyā</s> likewise bears from a <s>Śūdra</s> a one-interval son, <s>Kṣattṛ</s>.

children.text: dvyantaraḥ prātilomyena pāpiṣṭhaḥ sati saṃkare
children.translated_text: In the reverse order, the two-interval offspring is most sinful when mixture occurs.

children.text: cāṇḍālo jāyate śūdrād brāhmaṇī yatra muhyati ||
children.translated_text: A <s>Cāṇḍāla</s> is born from a <s>Śūdra</s> when a <s>Brāhmaṇī</s> goes astray.

children.text: rājñā parīkṣyaṃ na yathā jāyate varṇasaṃkaraḥ
children.translated_text: The king must investigate, so that <s>varṇasaṃkara</s> may not arise.

children.text: tasmād rājñā viśeṣeṇa trayī rakṣyā tu saṃkarāt ||
children.translated_text: Therefore the king must especially protect the threefold Vedic order from mixture.

children.text: Chapter 16
vibhāgo 'rthasya pitryasya putrair yatra prakalpyate
children.translated_text: Where a division of paternal property is arranged by the sons,

children.text: dāyabhāga iti proktaṃ tad vivādapadaṃ budhaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: that is called <s>dāyabhāga</s> (division of inheritance), declared by the wise to be a head of dispute.

children.text: pitary ūrdhvaṃ mṛte putrā vibhajeyur dhanaṃ pituḥ
children.translated_text: After the father has died, the sons should divide the father's wealth.

children.text: mātur duhitaro 'bhāve duhitāraṃ tadanvayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The daughters take the mother's wealth; in their absence, the daughter's descendants take it.

children.text: mātur nivṛtte rajasi prattāsu bhaginīṣu ca
children.translated_text: When the mother's menstruation has ceased and the sisters have been given in marriage,

children.text: niraṣṭe vāpy amaraṇe pitary uparataspṛhe ||
children.translated_text: or when the father, though not dead, has lost desire for possession,

children.text: pitaiva vā svayaṃ putrān vibhajed vayasi sthitaḥ
children.translated_text: or else the father himself, being advanced in age, may divide his sons,

children.text: jyeṣṭhaṃ śreṣṭhavibhāgena yathā vāsya matir bhavet ||
children.translated_text: giving the eldest a superior share, or otherwise as his judgment may be.

children.text: bibhṛyād vecchataḥ sarvāñ jyeṣṭho bhrātā yathā pitā
children.translated_text: The eldest brother, like a father, should support all of them if he wishes;

children.text: bhrātā śaktaḥ kaniṣṭho vā śaktyapekṣaḥ kule kriyā ||
children.translated_text: or a capable younger brother may do so, for family duty depends upon capacity.

children.text: śauryabhāryādhane hitvā yac ca vidyādhanaṃ bhavet
children.translated_text: Leaving aside wealth gained by valor, wealth from a wife, and wealth from learning,

children.text: trīṇy etāny avibhājyāni prasādo yaś ca paitṛkaḥ ||
children.translated_text: these three are indivisible, as is also any paternal favor.

children.text: mātrā ca svadhanaṃ dattaṃ yasmai syāt prītipūrvakam
children.translated_text: And whatever private property has been given by the mother with affection,

children.text: tasyāpy eṣa vidhir dṛṣṭo mātāpīṣṭe yathā pitā ||
children.translated_text: the same rule is seen for that too; when she chooses, the mother is like the father.

children.text: adhyagnyadhyāvahanikaṃ bhartṛdāyas tathaiva ca
children.translated_text: The gift at the nuptial fire, the bridal-procession gift, and the husband's gift as well,

children.text: bhrātṛmātṛpitṛbhyaś ca ṣaḍvidhaṃ strīdhanaṃ smṛtam ||
children.translated_text: and gifts from brother, mother, and father: these are remembered as the sixfold <s>strīdhana</s> (woman's property).

children.text: strīdhanaṃ tadapatyānāṃ bhartṛgāmy aprajāsu ca
children.translated_text: That <s>strīdhana</s> belongs to her children; for women without children, it goes to the husband

children.text: brāhmādiṣu catuḥṣv āhuḥ pitṛgāmītareṣu tu ||
children.translated_text: in the four marriage forms beginning with <s>Brāhma</s>, they say, but in the others it goes to the father.

children.text: kuṭumbaṃ bibhṛyād bhrātur yo vidyām adhigacchataḥ
children.translated_text: He who supports the household of a brother while that brother is acquiring learning

children.text: bhāgaṃ vidyādhanāt tasmāt sa labhetāśruto 'pi san ||
children.translated_text: should receive a share from the wealth gained through that learning, even if he himself is unlearned.

children.text: vaidyo 'vaidyāya nākāmo dadyād aṃśaṃ svato dhanāt
children.translated_text: A physician, if unwilling, need not give a share from his own wealth to a non-physician,

children.text: pitṛdravyaṃ tad āśritya na cet tena tad āhṛtam ||
children.translated_text: provided that it was not acquired by relying on paternal property.

children.text: dvāv āṃśau pratipadyeta vibhajann ātmanaḥ pitā
children.translated_text: When dividing his own property, the father may take two shares for himself.

children.text: samāṃśabhāginī mātā putrāṇāṃ syān mṛte patau ||
children.translated_text: When the husband is dead, the mother should share equally with the sons.

children.text: jyeṣṭhāyāṃśo 'dhiko deyaḥ jyeṣṭhāya tu varaḥ smṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: An additional share should be given to the eldest; the best portion is prescribed for the eldest.

children.text: samāṃśabhājaḥ śeṣāḥ syur aprattā bhaginī tathā ||
children.translated_text: The rest should have equal shares, and likewise an unmarried sister.

children.text: kṣetrajeṣv api putreṣu tadvaj jāteṣu dharmataḥ
children.translated_text: Even among <s>kṣetraja</s> sons, and among those born according to <s>dharma</s>, the same applies.

children.text: varṇāvareṣv aṃśahānir ūḍhājāteṣv anukramāt ||
children.translated_text: For those born from married wives of lower <s>varṇas</s>, the share diminishes in order.

children.text: pitraiva tu vibhaktā ye hīnādhikasamair dhanaiḥ
children.translated_text: Those whom the father himself has divided with lesser, greater, or equal amounts of wealth

children.text: teṣāṃ sa eva dharmaḥ syāt sarvasya hi pitā prabhuḥ ||
children.translated_text: have that very rule; for the father is lord of everything.

children.text: kānīnaś ca sahoḍhaś ca gūḍhāyāṃ yaś ca jāyate
children.translated_text: The <s>kānīna</s> son, the <s>sahoḍha</s> son, and one born secretly

children.text: teṣāṃ voḍhāpitā jñeyas te ca bhāgaharāḥ smṛtāḥ ||
children.translated_text: should have the marrying husband known as their father, and they are remembered as share-takers.

children.text: ajñātapitṛko yaś ca kānīno 'nūḍhamātṛkaḥ
children.translated_text: And the <s>kānīna</s> whose father is unknown and whose mother is unmarried

children.text: mātāmahāya dadyāt sa piṇḍaṃ rikthaṃ hareta ca ||
children.translated_text: should offer the ancestral ball to his maternal grandfather and inherit his estate.

children.text: jātā ye tv aniyuktāyām ekena bahubhis tathā
children.translated_text: Those born from an unappointed woman, whether by one man or by many,

children.text: arikthabhājas te sarve bījinām eva te sutāḥ ||
children.translated_text: are all without shares; they are sons only of the seed-givers.

children.text: dadyus te bījine piṇḍaṃ mātā cecchulkato hṛtā
children.translated_text: They should offer the ancestral ball to the seed-giver if the mother was taken for a bride-price.

children.text: aśulkopagatāyāṃ tu piṇḍadā voḍhur eva te ||
children.translated_text: But when she came without bride-price, they are offerers of the ancestral ball to the husband alone.

children.text: pitṛdviṭ patitaḥ paṇḍo yaś ca syād aupapātikaḥ
children.translated_text: One who hates his father, a fallen man, an impotent man, and one who is <s>aupapātika</s> (irregularly begotten),

children.text: aurasā api naite 'ṃśaṃ labheran kṣetrajāḥ kutaḥ ||
children.translated_text: even if they are <s>aurasa</s> sons, would not receive a share; how much less <s>kṣetraja</s> sons?

children.text: dīrghatīvrāmayagrastā jaḍonmattāndhapaṅgavaḥ
children.translated_text: Those afflicted by long and severe illness, the dull-witted, the mad, the blind, and the lame

children.text: bhartavyāḥ syuḥ kule caite tatputrās tv aṃśabhāginaḥ ||
children.translated_text: should be maintained within the family; but their sons are entitled to shares.

children.text: dvirāmuṣyāyaṇā dadyur dvābhyāṃ piṇḍodake pṛthak
children.translated_text: Sons belonging to two lineages should offer the ancestral ball and water separately to both fathers,

children.text: rikthād ardhāṃśam ādadyur bījikṣetrikayos tathā ||
children.translated_text: and they should likewise take a half share from the estates of the seed-giver and the field-owner.

children.text: saṃsṛṣṭināṃ tu yo bhāgas teṣām eva sa iṣyate
children.translated_text: But whatever share belongs to reunited coparceners is held to belong to them alone;

children.text: ato 'nyathāṃśabhājo hi nirbījiṣv itarān iyāt ||
children.translated_text: apart from that, when there are no descendants, it should pass to the other share-takers.

children.text: bhrātām aprajaḥ preyāt kaścic cet pravrajet tu vā
children.translated_text: If, among brothers, one without offspring should die, or should renounce the world,

children.text: vibhajeyur dhanaṃ tasya śeṣās tu strīdhanaṃ vinā ||
children.translated_text: the remaining brothers should divide his wealth, except for the <s>strīdhana</s> (woman's property).

children.text: bharaṇam cāsya kurvīran strīṇām ā jīvitakṣayāt
children.translated_text: They should also provide maintenance for his wives until the end of their lives,

children.text: rakṣanti śayyāṃ bhartuś ced āchindyur itarāsu tu ||
children.translated_text: if they preserve the husband's bed; but in the case of others they should cut it off.

children.text: syād yasya duhitā tasyāḥ pitraṃśo bharaṇe mataḥ
children.translated_text: If he has a daughter, her father's share is regarded as meant for her maintenance;

children.text: ā saṃskārād bhajed enāṃ parato bibhṛyāt patiḥ ||
children.translated_text: she should enjoy it until her marriage rite, and after that her husband should support her.

children.text: mṛte bhartary aputrāyāḥ patipakṣaḥ prabhuḥ striyāḥ
children.translated_text: When her husband has died and she has no son, the husband's side has authority over the woman;

children.text: viniyogātmarakṣāsu bharaṇe ca sa īśvaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: it is master in matters of assignment, protection of her person, and maintenance.

children.text: parikṣīṇe patikule nirmanuṣye nirāśraye
children.translated_text: When the husband's family is exhausted, without men and without support,

children.text: tatsapiṇḍeṣu vāsatsu pitṛpakṣaḥ prabhuḥ striyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: or when his <s>sapiṇḍas</s> (agnatic kin) are absent, the father's side has authority over the woman.

children.text: pakṣadvayāvasāne tu rājā bhartā smṛtaḥ striyāḥ
children.translated_text: But when both sides have come to an end, the king is remembered as the woman's protector;

children.text: sa tasyā bharaṇaṃ kuryān nigṛhṇīyāt pathaś cyutām ||
children.translated_text: he should provide her maintenance and restrain her if she strays from the path.

children.text: svātantryād vipraṇaśyanti kule jātā api striyaḥ
children.translated_text: Through independence women go to ruin, even when born in a good family;

children.text: asvātantryam atas tāsāṃ prajāpatir akalpayat ||
children.translated_text: therefore <s>Prajāpati</s> established non-independence for them.

children.text: pitā rakṣati kaumāre bhartā rakṣati yauvane
children.translated_text: The father protects her in girlhood, the husband protects her in youth,

children.text: putrā rakṣanti vaidhavye na strī svātantryam arhati ||
children.translated_text: and the sons protect her in widowhood; a woman is not entitled to independence.

children.text: yacchiṣṭaṃ pitṛdāyebhyo dattvarṇaṃ paitṛkaṃ ca yat
children.translated_text: Whatever remains from the paternal estate after paying whatever paternal debt there is

children.text: bhrātṛbhis tad vibhaktavyam ṛṇī na syād yathā pitā ||
children.translated_text: should be divided by the brothers, so that the father may not remain indebted.

children.text: yeṣāṃ ca na kṛtāḥ pitrā saṃskāravidhayaḥ kramāt
children.translated_text: For those whose prescribed <s>saṃskāra</s> rites were not performed by the father in due order,

children.text: kartavyā bhrātṛbhis teṣāṃ paitṛkād eva te dhanāt ||
children.translated_text: the brothers must perform them from that very paternal wealth.

children.text: avidyamāne pitrye 'rthe svāṃśād uddhṛtya vā punaḥ
children.translated_text: If paternal property is lacking, then taking it from their own shares,

children.text: avaśyakāryāḥ saṃskārā bhrātaraṃ pūrvasaṃskṛtaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: the already consecrated brothers must perform the indispensable <s>saṃskāras</s> for a brother.

children.text: kuṭumbārtheṣu codyuktas tatkāryaṃ kurute ca yaḥ
children.translated_text: And the one who is employed in the affairs of the family and performs its work

children.text: sa bhrātṛbhir bṛṃhaṇīyo grāsācchādanavāhanaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: should be supported by his brothers with food, clothing, and conveyances.

children.text: vibhāgadharmasaṃdehe dāyādānāṃ vinirṇaye
children.translated_text: When there is doubt about the law of partition and the heirs must be determined,

children.text: jñātibhir bhāgalekhyaiś ca pṛthakkāryapravartanāt ||
children.translated_text: one should proceed by means of relatives, documents of shares, and the carrying on of separate affairs.

children.text: bhrātām avibhaktānām eko dharmaḥ pravartate
children.translated_text: For undivided brothers, one common <s>dharma</s> (legal and ritual duty) operates;

children.text: vibhāge sati dharmo 'pi bhaved eṣāṃ pṛthak pṛthak ||
children.translated_text: when partition has taken place, even their <s>dharma</s> becomes separate for each one.

children.text: dānagrahaṇapaśvannagṛhakṣetraparigrahāḥ
children.translated_text: Gifts and acceptances, acquisition of cattle, food, houses, and fields,

children.text: vibhaktānāṃ pṛthag jñeyāḥ pākadharmāgamavyayāḥ ||
children.translated_text: and cooking, ritual duty, income, and expenditure are to be known as separate for divided brothers.

children.text: sākṣitvaṃ prātibhāvyaṃ ca dānaṃ grahaṇam eva ca
children.translated_text: Witnessing, suretyship, giving, and receiving too

children.text: vibhaktā bhrātaraḥ kuryur nāvibhaktā parasparam ||
children.translated_text: may be done by divided brothers toward one another, but not by undivided brothers.

children.text: yeṣām etāḥ kriyā loke pravartante svarikthinām
children.translated_text: Those co-heirs among whom these transactions are current in the world

children.text: vibhaktān avagaccheyur lekhyam apy antareṇa tān ||
children.translated_text: should be understood as divided, even without a written document.

children.text: yady ekajātā bahavaḥ pṛthagdharmāḥ pṛthakkriyāḥ
children.translated_text: If many persons of one birth have separate duties and separate rites,

children.text: pṛthakkarmaguṇopetā na te kṛtyeṣu saṃmatāḥ ||
children.translated_text: and are endowed with separate occupations and qualities, they are not mutually recognized in legal acts.

children.text: svān bhāgān yadi dadyus te vikrīṇīrann athāpi vā
children.translated_text: If they give away their own shares, or even sell them,

children.text: kuryur yatheṣṭaṃ tat sarvam īśante svadhanasya te ||
children.translated_text: they may do all that as they wish; they are masters of their own property.

children.text: aurasaḥ kṣetrajaś caiva putrikāputra eva ca
children.translated_text: The <s>aurasa</s> son, the <s>kṣetraja</s> son, and the <s>putrikāputra</s> son,

children.text: kānīnaś ca sahoḍhaś ca gūḍhotpannas tathaiva ca ||
children.translated_text: the <s>kānīna</s> son, the <s>sahoḍha</s> son, and likewise the secretly born son,

children.text: paunarbhavo 'paviddhaś ca labdhaḥ krītaḥ kṛtas tathā
children.translated_text: the <s>paunarbhava</s> son, the <s>apaviddha</s> son, the obtained son, the purchased son, the made son,

children.text: svayaṃ copagataḥ putrā dvādaśaita udāhṛtāḥ ||
children.translated_text: and the son who has come of himself: these are declared to be the twelve sons.

children.text: teṣāṃ ṣaḍ bandhudāyādāḥ ṣaḍ adāyādabāndhavāḥ
children.translated_text: Of these, six are kinsmen and heirs, while six are kinsmen but not heirs;

children.text: pūrvaḥ pūrvaḥ smṛtaḥ śreyāj jaghanyo yo ya uttaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: each earlier one is remembered as superior, and each later one as inferior.

children.text: kramāddhy ete prapadyeran mṛte pitari taddhanam
children.translated_text: For in order these sons should inherit that wealth when the father has died;

children.text: jyāyaso jyāyaso 'bhāve jaghanyas tad avāpnuyāt ||
children.translated_text: in the absence of each superior one, the inferior one should obtain it.

children.text: putrābhāve tu duhitā tulyasaṃtānadarśanāt
children.translated_text: But in the absence of a son, the daughter inherits, because equal offspring is recognized;

children.text: putraś ca duhitā coktau pituḥ saṃtānakārakau ||
children.translated_text: the son and the daughter are both said to continue the father's line.

children.text: abhāve tu duhitṝṇāṃ sakulyā bāndhavās tataḥ
children.translated_text: In the absence of daughters, the <s>sakulyas</s> (same-family kin) inherit, and after them the relatives;

children.text: tataḥ sajātyāḥ sarveṣām abhāve rājagāmi tat ||
children.translated_text: then those of the same birth-group; when all are absent, it goes to the king.

children.text: anyatra brāhmaṇāt kiṃtu rājā dharmaparāyaṇaḥ
children.translated_text: This does not apply to a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>; but the king, devoted to <s>dharma</s>,

children.text: sa strīṇāṃ jīvanaṃ dadyād eṣa dāyavidhiḥ smṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: should provide livelihood for the women. This is remembered as the rule of inheritance.

children.text: Chapter 17
sahasā kriyate karma yat kiṃcid baladarpitaiḥ
children.translated_text: Any act that is done forcibly by persons arrogant with strength

children.text: tat sāhasam iti proktaṃ saho balam ihocyate ||
children.translated_text: is called <s>sāhasa</s> (violent offense); here <s>sahas</s> means force.

children.text: tat punas trividhaṃ jñeyaṃ prathamaṃ madhyamaṃ tathā
children.translated_text: That again should be known as threefold: first, middle,

children.text: uttamaṃ ceti śāstreṣu tasyoktaṃ lakṣaṇaṃ pṛthak ||
children.translated_text: and highest; in the treatises its characteristic is stated separately.

children.text: phalamūlodakādīnāṃ kṣetropakaraṇasya ca
children.translated_text: With respect to fruits, roots, water, and the like, and also field implements,

children.text: bhaṅgākṣepopamardādyaiḥ prathamaṃ sāhasaṃ smṛtam ||
children.translated_text: breaking, carrying off, crushing, and similar acts are remembered as first-degree <s>sāhasa</s>.

children.text: vāsaḥpaśvannapānānām gṛhopakaraṇasya ca
children.translated_text: With respect to clothing, cattle, food and drink,

children.text: etenaiva prakāreṇa madhyamaṃ sāhasaṃ smṛtam ||
children.translated_text: and household implements, the same kind of act is remembered as middle-degree <s>sāhasa</s>.

children.text: vyāpādo viṣaśastrādyaiḥ paradārapradharṣaṇam
children.translated_text: Killing or injury by poison, weapons, and the like, the violation of another man's wife,

children.text: prāṇoparodhi yac cānyad uktam uttamasāhasam ||
children.translated_text: and whatever else obstructs life are called highest-degree <s>sāhasa</s>.

children.text: tasya daṇḍaḥ kriyāpekṣaḥ prathamasya śatāvaraḥ
children.translated_text: Its penalty depends on the act; for the first degree, the minimum is one hundred,

children.text: madhyamasya tu śāstrajñair jñeyaḥ pañcaśatāvaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: while for the middle degree the knowers of the treatises recognize a minimum of five hundred.

children.text: vadhaḥ sarvasvaharaṇaṃ purān nirvāsanāṅkane
children.translated_text: Execution, confiscation of all property, banishment from the city, branding,

children.text: tadaṅgaccheda ity ukto daṇḍa uttamasāhase ||
children.translated_text: and cutting off the relevant limb are said to be the penalty for highest-degree <s>sāhasa</s>.

children.text: aviśeṣeṇa sarveṣām eṣa daṇḍavidhiḥ smṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: This rule of punishment is remembered for everyone without distinction,

children.text: vadhād ṛte brāhmaṇasya na vadhaṃ brāhmaṇo 'rhati ||
children.translated_text: except for execution of a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>; a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> does not deserve execution.

children.text: śiraso muṇḍanaṃ daṇḍas tasya nirvāsanaṃ purāt
children.translated_text: The punishment for him is shaving the head and banishment from the city;

children.text: lalāṭe cābhiśastāṅkaḥ prayāṇaṃ gardabhena ca ||
children.translated_text: also the stigma-mark of a convicted man on the forehead, and being sent off on a donkey.

children.text: syātāṃ saṃvyavahāryau tau dhṛtadaṇḍau tu pūrvayoḥ
children.translated_text: In the two earlier cases, once they have undergone punishment, those two may again be admitted to dealings;

children.text: dhṛtadaṇḍo 'py asaṃbhojyo jñeya uttamasāhase ||
children.translated_text: but even one who has undergone punishment for the highest <s>sāhasa</s> is to be known as unfit to dine with.
