children.text: tasyaiva bhedaḥ steyaṃ syād viśeṣas tatra cocyate
children.translated_text: A subdivision of that very offense is <s>steya</s> (theft); the special rule for it is now stated.

children.text: atisāhasam ākramya steyam āhuś chalena tu ||
children.translated_text: When it enters the sphere of grave force but is done by deceit, they call it theft.

children.text: tad api trividhaṃ proktaṃ dravyāpekṣaṃ manīṣibhiḥ
children.translated_text: That too is declared threefold by the wise, depending on the property;

children.text: kṣudramadhyottamānāṃ tu dravyāṇām apakarṣaṇāt ||
children.translated_text: because there is taking away of property that is small, middling, or excellent.

children.text: mṛdbhāṇḍāsanakhaṭvāsthidārucarmatṛṇādi yat
children.translated_text: Earthen vessels, seats, cots, bone, wood, leather, grass, and the like,

children.text: śamīdhānyamudgādīni kṣudradravyam udāhṛtam ||
children.translated_text: and <s>śamī</s>, grain, mung beans, and similar things are called low-value property.

children.text: vāsaḥ kauśeyavarjaṃ ca govarjaṃ paśavas tathā
children.translated_text: Clothing, except for silk, and animals, except for cows,

children.text: hiraṇyavarjaṃ lohaṃ ca madhyaṃ vrīhiyavā api ||
children.translated_text: as well as metal, except for gold, and also rice and barley, are middling property.

children.text: hiraṇyaratnakauśeyastrīpuṃgogajavājinaḥ
children.translated_text: Gold, jewels, silk, women and men, cows, elephants, and horses,

children.text: devabrāhmaṇarājñāṃ ca dravyaṃ vijñeyam uttamam ||
children.translated_text: and the property of deities, <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, and kings should be known as excellent.

children.text: upāyair vividhair eṣāṃ chalayitvāpakarṣaṇam
children.translated_text: Taking these away by deceiving someone with various devices,

children.text: suptapramattamattebhyaḥ steyam āhur manīṣiṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: from people who are asleep, inattentive, or intoxicated, the wise call <s>steya</s> (theft).

children.text: sahoḍhagrahaṇāt steyaṃ hoḍhe 'saty upabhogataḥ
children.translated_text: Theft is proved by arrest together with the stolen goods; when such possession is absent, by use of the goods;

children.text: śaṅkā tv asajjanaikārthyād anāyavyayatas tathā ||
children.translated_text: but suspicion arises from being in league with bad people and likewise from spending without income.

children.text: bhaktāvakāśadātāraḥ stenānāṃ ye prasarpatām
children.translated_text: Those who give food and shelter to thieves who are moving about,

children.text: śaktāś ca ya upekṣante te 'pi taddoṣabhāginaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and those who, though able to act, ignore them, also share in their guilt.

children.text: utkrośatāṃ janānāṃ ca hriyamāṇe dhane 'pi ca
children.translated_text: And when people are crying out while property is being carried off,

children.text: śrutvā ye nābhidhāvanti te 'pi taddoṣabhāginaḥ ||
children.translated_text: those who hear but do not run to help also share in that guilt.

children.text: sāhaseṣu ya evoktas triṣu daṇḍo manīṣibhiḥ
children.translated_text: The very penalty that the wise have stated for the three <s>sāhasas</s>

children.text: sa eva daṇḍaḥ steye 'pi dravyeṣu triṣv anukramāt ||
children.translated_text: is the penalty for theft also, in the three classes of property, in order.

children.text: gavādiṣu praṇaṣṭeṣu dravyeṣv apahṛteṣu vā
children.translated_text: When cows and the like are lost, or when goods have been stolen,

children.text: padenānveṣaṇaṃ kuryur ā mūlāt tadvido janāḥ ||
children.translated_text: people skilled in it should track them by footprints from the very starting point.

children.text: grāme vraje vivīte vā yatra saṃnipatet padam
children.translated_text: Where the track enters a village, cattle pen, or open pasture,

children.text: voḍhavyaṃ tad bhavet tena na cet so 'nyatra tan nayet ||
children.translated_text: that place must bear liability for it, unless it carries the track on elsewhere.

children.text: pade pramūḍhe bhagne vā viṣamatvāj janāntike
children.translated_text: When the track is confused or broken because the ground is uneven or because people are nearby,

children.text: yas tv āsannataro grāmo vrajo vā tatra pātayet ||
children.translated_text: one should place the liability on whichever village or cattle pen is nearest.

children.text: same 'dhvani dvayor yatra tena prāyo 'śucir janaḥ
children.translated_text: Where, on a level road, the case lies between two places, the person generally of bad character is liable;

children.text: pūrvāpadānair dṛṣṭo vā saṃsṛṣṭo vā durātmabhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: or one known from previous offenses, or one associated with wicked men.

children.text: grāmeṣv anveṣaṇaṃ kuryuś caṇḍālavadhakādayaḥ
children.translated_text: In villages, <s>Caṇḍālas</s>, executioners, and the like should carry out the search;

children.text: rātrisaṃcāriṇo ye ca bahiḥ kuryur bahiścarāḥ ||
children.translated_text: and those who roam at night should do so; outside the village, outlying people should conduct it.

children.text: steneṣv alabhyamāneṣu rājā dadyāt svakād dhanāt
children.translated_text: When the thieves cannot be found, the king should pay from his own wealth;

children.text: upekṣamāṇo hy enasvī dharmād arthāc ca hīyate ||
children.translated_text: for if he is negligent, he is guilty and falls away from <s>dharma</s> and from wealth.

children.text: Chapter 18
deśajātikulādīnām ākrośanyaṅgasaṃhitam
children.translated_text: Speech that contains abuse and disparagement of region, caste, family, and the like,

children.text: yad vacaḥ pratikūlārthaṃ vākpāruṣyaṃ tad ucyate ||
children.translated_text: and has a hostile meaning, is called <s>vākpāruṣya</s> (verbal harshness).

children.text: niṣṭhurāślīlatīvratvāt tad api trividhaṃ smṛtam
children.translated_text: That too is remembered as threefold, because it may be harsh, obscene, or severe;

children.text: gauravānukramād asya daṇḍo 'py atra kramād guruḥ ||
children.translated_text: and according to the sequence of its gravity, the penalty here too becomes heavy in order.

children.text: sākṣepaṃ niṣṭhuraṃ jñeyam aślīlaṃ nyaṅgasaṃyutam
children.translated_text: Harsh speech is to be known as that which contains accusation; obscene speech is joined with degrading insult;

children.text: pātanīyair upakrośais tīvram āhur manīṣiṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the wise call it severe when the reproaches allege acts that cause loss of caste.

children.text: paragātreṣv abhidroho hastapādāyudhādibhiḥ
children.translated_text: An attack on another's body with hands, feet, weapons, and the like,

children.text: bhasmādibhiś copaghāto daṇḍapāruṣyam ucyate ||
children.translated_text: and injury with ashes and similar things, is called <s>daṇḍapāruṣya</s> (physical assault).

children.text: tasyāpi dṛṣṭaṃ traividhyaṃ mṛdumadhyottamaṃ kramāt
children.translated_text: Its threefold division too is seen: mild, middling, and highest in order,

children.text: avagūraṇaniḥsaṅgapātanakṣatadarśanaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: through threatening, bodily contact, throwing down, and the appearance of wounds.

children.text: hīnamadhyottamānāṃ tu dravyāṇām samatikramāt
children.translated_text: From transgressions involving low, middling, and excellent property,

children.text: trīṇy eva sāhasāny āhus tatra kaṇṭakaśodhanam ||
children.translated_text: they speak of just three <s>sāhasas</s>; here this is the suppression of criminals.

children.text: vidhiḥ pañcavidhas tūkta etayor ubhayor api
children.translated_text: For both of these, however, the rule is said to be fivefold;

children.text: viśuddhir daṇḍabhāktvaṃ ca tatra sambadhyate yathā ||
children.translated_text: how acquittal and liability to punishment are connected there is as follows.

children.text: pāruṣye sati saṃrambhād utpanne kṣubdhayor dvayoḥ
children.translated_text: When harsh abuse has arisen from anger between two agitated persons,

children.text: sa manyate yaḥ kṣamate daṇḍabhāg yo 'tivartate ||
children.translated_text: the one who bears it is approved; the one who goes beyond bounds is liable to punishment.

children.text: pāruṣyadoṣāvṛtayor yugapat sampravṛttayoḥ
children.translated_text: When both, covered by the fault of harsh abuse, proceed at the same time,

children.text: viśeṣaś cen na dṛśyeta vinayaḥ syāt samas tayoḥ ||
children.translated_text: if no distinction is seen, the discipline should be equal for both.

children.text: pūrvam ākṣārayed yas tu niyataṃ syāt sa doṣabhāk
children.translated_text: But the one who first reviles another is certainly the bearer of fault;

children.text: paścād yaḥ so 'py asatkārī pūrve tu vinayo guruḥ ||
children.translated_text: the one who does so afterward is also improper, but the discipline is heavier for the first.

children.text: dvayor āpannayos tulyam anubadhnāti yaḥ punaḥ
children.translated_text: When two have equally fallen into the offense, whoever then keeps pursuing it,

children.text: sa tayor daṇḍam āpnoti pūrvo vā yadi vetaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: receives the penalty between them, whether he was the first offender or the other.

children.text: śvapākapaṇḍacaṇḍālavyaṅgeṣu vadhavṛttiṣu
children.translated_text: In cases involving <s>Śvapākas</s>, eunuchs, <s>Caṇḍālas</s>, deformed persons, and people who live by killing,

children.text: hastipavrātyadāreṣu gurvācāryāṅganāsu ca ||
children.translated_text: and involving the wives of elephant-keepers and <s>Vrātyas</s>, and women of gurus and teachers,

children.text: maryādātikrame sadyo ghāta evānuśāsanam
children.translated_text: when the boundary is overstepped, immediate killing alone is the prescribed discipline;

children.text: na ca taddaṇḍapāruṣye doṣam āhur manīṣiṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and the wise say there is no fault of physical assault in that punishment.

children.text: yam eva hy ativarterann ete santaṃ janaṃ nṛṣu
children.translated_text: For whichever respectable man among people these persons transgress against,

children.text: sa eva vinayaṃ kuryān na tadvinayabhāṅ nṛpaḥ ||
children.translated_text: that very man should impose discipline; the king is not responsible for that discipline.

children.text: malā hy ete manuṣyeṣu dhanam eṣāṃ malātmakam
children.translated_text: For these are filth among human beings, and their wealth has the nature of filth;

children.text: api tān ghātayed rājā nārthadaṇḍena daṇḍayet ||
children.translated_text: the king may even have them killed; he should not punish them with a monetary fine.

children.text: śataṃ brāhmaṇam ākruśya kṣatriyo daṇḍam arhati
children.translated_text: After abusing a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, a <s>Kṣatriya</s> deserves a fine of one hundred;

children.text: vaiśyo 'dhyardhaṃ śataṃ dve vā śūdras tu vadham arhati ||
children.translated_text: a <s>Vaiśya</s> one hundred and fifty, or two hundred, while a <s>Śūdra</s> deserves death.

children.text: vipraḥ pañcāśataṃ daṇḍyaḥ kṣatriyasyābhiśaṃsane
children.translated_text: A <s>Vipra</s> is to be fined fifty for reviling a <s>Kṣatriya</s>;

children.text: vaiśye syād ardhapañcāśacchūdre dvādaśako damaḥ ||
children.translated_text: for a <s>Vaiśya</s> it is half of fifty, and for a <s>Śūdra</s> the penalty is twelve.

children.text: samavarṇadvijātīnāṃ dvādaśaiva vyatikrame
children.translated_text: For twice-born persons of equal <s>varṇa</s>, the penalty for transgression is exactly twelve;

children.text: vādeṣv avacanīyeṣu tad eva dviguṇaṃ bhavet ||
children.translated_text: in disputes involving words that ought not be spoken, that same amount becomes doubled.

children.text: kāṇam apy athavā khañjam anyaṃ vāpi tathāvidham
children.translated_text: If someone calls another one-eyed, or lame, or anything else of that sort,

children.text: tathyenāpi bruvan dāpyo rājñā kārṣāpaṇāvaram ||
children.translated_text: even truthfully, the king should make him pay at least one <s>kārṣāpaṇa</s>.

children.text: na kilbiṣeṇāpavadecchāstrataḥ kṛtapāvanam
children.translated_text: One should not reproach, on account of a sin, a person who has been purified according to <s>śāstra</s>.

children.text: na rājñā dhṛtadaṇḍaṃ ca daṇḍabhāk tadvyatikramāt ||
children.translated_text: One on whom punishment has already been imposed by the king should not be punished again; one who violates this becomes liable to punishment.

children.text: loke 'smin dvāv avaktavyāv adaṇḍyau ca prakīrtitau
children.translated_text: In this world two are declared not to be denounced, and not to be punishable:

children.text: brāhmaṇaś caiva rājā ca tau hīdaṃ bibhṛto jagat ||
children.translated_text: the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> and the king; for these two uphold this world.

children.text: patitaṃ patitety uktvā cauraṃ caureti vā punaḥ
children.translated_text: Having called a fallen man 'fallen,' or again a thief 'thief,'

children.text: vacanāt tulyadoṣaḥ syān mithyā dvir doṣatāṃ vrajet ||
children.translated_text: by that utterance one incurs an equal fault; if it is false, one falls into twice the fault.

children.text: nāmajātigrahaṃ teṣām abhidroheṇa kurvataḥ
children.translated_text: For a <s>Śūdra</s> who maliciously utters their name and caste,

children.text: nikheyo 'yomayaḥ śaṅkuḥ śūdrasyāṣṭādaśāṅgulaḥ ||
children.translated_text: an iron spike eighteen fingers long is to be driven in.

children.text: dharmāpadeśaṃ darpeṇa dvijānām asya kurvataḥ
children.translated_text: If, through arrogance, he gives instruction in <s>dharma</s> to twice-born men,

children.text: taptam āsecayet tailaṃ vaktre śrotre ca pārthivaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the king should have hot oil poured into his mouth and ears.

children.text: yenāṅgenāvaro varṇo brāhmaṇasyāparādhnuyāt
children.translated_text: Whatever limb an inferior <s>varṇa</s> uses to offend a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>,

children.text: tad aṅgaṃ tasya chettavyam evaṃ śuddhim avāpnuyāt ||
children.translated_text: that limb of his should be cut off; in this way he obtains purification.

children.text: sahāsanam abhiprepsur utkṛṣṭasyāvakṛṣṭajaḥ
children.translated_text: An inferior-born man who seeks to share a seat with one superior to him

children.text: kaṭyāṃ kṛtāṅko nirvāsyaḥ sphigdeśaṃ vāsya kartayet ||
children.translated_text: is to be banished after being branded on the hip, or the king should have his buttock cut.

children.text: avaniṣṭhīvato darpād dvāv oṣṭhau chedayen nṛpaḥ
children.translated_text: If he spits contemptuously, the king should cut off both lips;

children.text: avamūtrayataḥ śiśnam avaśardhayato gudam ||
children.translated_text: if he urinates, his penis; if he passes wind against him, his anus.

children.text: keśeṣu gṛhṇato hastau chedayed avicārayan
children.translated_text: He should at once cut off both hands of one who seizes another by the hair,

children.text: pādayor nāsikāyāṃ ca grīvāyāṃ vṛṣaṇeṣu ca ||
children.translated_text: or by the feet, the nose, the neck, or the testicles.

children.text: upakruśya tu rājānaṃ vartmani sve vyavasthitam
children.translated_text: If someone reviles the king while he is established on his proper path,

children.text: jihvāchedād bhavecchuddhiḥ sarvasvaharaṇena vā ||
children.translated_text: purification comes through cutting off the tongue, or through confiscation of all property.

children.text: rājani prahared yas tu kṛtāgasy api durmatiḥ
children.translated_text: Whoever, evil-minded, strikes the king, even if the king has committed an offense,

children.text: śūle tam agnau vipaced brahmahatyāśatādhikam ||
children.translated_text: should be roasted on a stake in the fire; this is worse than a hundred <s>brahmahatyās</s> (killings of Brāhmaṇas).

children.text: putrāparādhe na pitā na śvavāñ śuni daṇḍabhāk
children.translated_text: For the offense of a son, the father is not liable to punishment; nor is a dog-owner liable for a dog,

children.text: na markaṭe ca tatsvāmī tair eva prahito na cet ||
children.translated_text: nor the owner of a monkey for the monkey, unless they were set on by them.

children.text: Chapter 19
akṣavardhraśalākādyair devanaṃ jihmakāritam
children.translated_text: Gaming made crooked with dice, straps, sticks, and the like,

children.text: paṇakrīḍā vayobhiś ca padaṃ dyūtasamāhvayam ||
children.translated_text: and stake-play with birds: this legal title is called <s>dyūta-samāhvaya</s> (gambling and betting).

children.text: sabhikaḥ kārayed dyūtaṃ deyaṃ dadyāc ca tatkṛtam
children.translated_text: The gambling-hall keeper should conduct the gambling and pay what is due from what is produced by it;

children.text: daśakaṃ tu śataṃ vṛddhis tasya syād dyūtakāritā ||
children.translated_text: his fee for conducting gambling should be a profit of ten in a hundred.

children.text: dvirabhyastāḥ patanty akṣā glahe yasyākṣadevinaḥ
children.translated_text: When the dice of a dice-player have been cast twice for a stake,

children.text: jayaṃ tasyāparasyāhuḥ kitavasya parājayam ||
children.translated_text: they say that victory belongs to the other man and defeat to that gambler.

children.text: kitaveṣv eva tiṣṭheyuḥ kitavāḥ saṃśayaṃ prati
children.translated_text: In a dispute among gamblers, gamblers alone should stand present;

children.text: ta eva tasya draṣṭāraḥ syus ta eva ca sākṣiṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: they themselves are its observers, and they themselves are its witnesses.

children.text: aśuddhaḥ kitavo nānyad āśrayed dyūtamaṇḍalam
children.translated_text: A dishonest gambler should not resort to another gambling circle;

children.text: pratihanyān na sabhikaṃ dāpayet tat svam iṣṭataḥ ||
children.translated_text: he should not obstruct the gambling-hall keeper, who may make him pay his own due as he thinks fit.

children.text: kūṭākṣadevinaḥ pāpān nirbhajed dyūtamaṇḍalāt
children.translated_text: He should expel wicked players with false dice from the gambling circle,

children.text: kaṇṭhe 'kṣamālām āsajya sa hy eṣāṃ vinayaḥ smṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: after hanging a garland of dice around their neck; this is remembered as their discipline.

children.text: Chapter 20
prakīrṇake punar jñeyā vyavahārā nṛpāśrayāḥ
children.translated_text: Again, in <s>prakīrṇaka</s> (miscellaneous cases), legal matters depending on the king are to be known:

children.text: rājñām ājñāpratīghātas tatkarmakaraṇaṃ tathā ||
children.translated_text: resistance to the commands of kings, and likewise the execution of their business;

children.text: purapradānaṃ saṃbhedaḥ prakṛtīnāṃ tathaiva ca
children.translated_text: the granting of a town, the splitting of the constituent bodies of the realm,

children.text: pāṣaṇḍanaigamaśreṇīgaṇadharmaviparyayāḥ ||
children.translated_text: and reversals of the rules of heterodox sects, merchant communities, guilds, and corporate groups;

children.text: pitṛputravivādaś ca prāyaścittavyatikramaḥ
children.translated_text: disputes between father and son, and transgression of penances;

children.text: pratigrahavilopaś ca kopa āśramiṇām api ||
children.translated_text: interference with accepted gifts, and also anger involving members of the <s>āśramas</s>;

children.text: varṇasaṃkaradoṣaś ca tadvṛttiniyamas tathā
children.translated_text: the fault of <s>varṇasaṃkara</s> (mixture of social classes), and the regulation of their livelihoods;

children.text: na dṛṣṭaṃ yac ca pūrveṣu tat sarvaṃ syāt prakīrṇake ||
children.translated_text: and whatever has not been seen among the preceding titles: all of that belongs in <s>prakīrṇaka</s>.

children.text: rājā tv avahitaḥ sarvān āśramān paripālayet
children.translated_text: The king, attentive, should protect all the <s>āśramas</s>

children.text: upāyaiḥ śāstravihitaiś caturbhiḥ prakṛtais tathā ||
children.translated_text: by the four means prescribed in the <s>śāstra</s>, and likewise by the ordinary means.

children.text: yo yo varṇo 'vahīyeta yo vodrekam anuvrajet
children.translated_text: Whichever <s>varṇa</s> declines, or whichever rises beyond its bounds,

children.text: taṃ taṃ dṛṣṭvā svato mārgāt pracyutaṃ sthāpayet pathi ||
children.translated_text: seeing each one fallen from its own path, he should set it back on the path.

children.text: aśāstrokteṣu cānyeṣu pāpayukteṣu karmasu
children.translated_text: In other sinful acts not stated in the <s>śāstra</s>,

children.text: prasamīkṣyātmano rājā daṇḍaṃ daṇḍyeṣu pātayet ||
children.translated_text: the king, after full consideration, should impose punishment on those deserving punishment.

children.text: śrutismṛtiviruddhaṃ ca janānām ahitaṃ ca yat
children.translated_text: Whatever is contrary to <s>śruti</s> and <s>smṛti</s>, and whatever is harmful to people,

children.text: na tat pravartayed rājā pravṛttaṃ ca nivartayet ||
children.translated_text: the king should not set that in motion; if it is already in motion, he should stop it.

children.text: nyāyāpetaṃ yad anyena rājñājñānakṛtaṃ ca yat
children.translated_text: Whatever is devoid of justice, and whatever has been done by another king through ignorance,

children.text: tad apy anyāyavihitaṃ punar nyāye niveśayet ||
children.translated_text: though wrongly ordained, he should set that too back into justice.

children.text: rājñā pravartitān dharmān yo naro nānupālayet
children.translated_text: The man who does not observe the <s>dharmas</s> established by the king

children.text: daṇḍyaḥ sa pāpo vadhyaś ca lopayan rājaśāsanam ||
children.translated_text: is punishable, sinful, and liable to death, for he destroys the king's ordinance.

children.text: āyudhāny āyudhīyānāṃ vāhyādīn vāhyajīvinām
children.translated_text: Weapons belonging to those who live by weapons, and vehicles and the like belonging to those who live by transport,

children.text: veśyāstrīṇām alaṃkāraṃ vādyātodyāni tadvidām ||
children.translated_text: ornaments of courtesan-women, and instruments and musical gear of those skilled in them,

children.text: yac ca yasyopakaraṇaṃ yena jīvanti kārukāḥ
children.translated_text: and whatever equipment belongs to anyone, by which artisans live,

children.text: sarvasvaharaṇe 'py etān na rājā hartum arhati ||
children.translated_text: the king should not take these, even when confiscating all property.

children.text: anādiś cāpy anantaś ca dvipadāṃ pṛthivīpatiḥ
children.translated_text: The lord of earth among men is, as it were, without beginning and without end,

children.text: dīptimattvācchucitvāc ca yadi na syāt pathaś cyutaḥ ||
children.translated_text: because of his brilliance and purity, provided he has not fallen from the path.

children.text: yadi rājā na sarveṣāṃ varṇānāṃ daṇḍadhāraṇam
children.translated_text: If the king did not wield punishment over all the <s>varṇas</s>

children.text: kuryāt patho vyapetānāṃ vinaśyeyur imāḥ prajāḥ ||
children.translated_text: when they have departed from the path, these subjects would perish.

children.text: brāhmaṇyaṃ brāhmaṇo jahyāt kṣatriyaḥ kṣātram utsṛjet
children.translated_text: The <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> would abandon Brāhmaṇa-hood; the <s>Kṣatriya</s> would cast off kṣatriya-power;

children.text: svakarma jahyād vaiśyas tu śūdraḥ sarvān viśeṣayet ||
children.translated_text: the <s>Vaiśya</s> would abandon his own work, and the <s>Śūdra</s> would overstep all distinctions.

children.text: rājānaś cen nābhaviṣyan pṛthivyāṃ daṇḍadhāraṇam
children.translated_text: If kings did not exist on earth as wielders of punishment,

children.text: śūle matsyān ivāpakṣyan durbalān balavattarāḥ ||
children.translated_text: the stronger would roast the weaker like fish on a stake.

children.text: satām anugraho nityam asatāṃ nigrahas tathā
children.translated_text: Constant favor toward the good and restraint of the wicked:

children.text: eṣa dharmaḥ smṛto rājñām arthaś cāmitrapīḍanāt ||
children.translated_text: this is remembered as the <s>dharma</s> of kings, and also their advantage, because it crushes enemies.

children.text: na lipyate yathā vahnir dahañchaśvad imāḥ prajāḥ
children.translated_text: Just as fire is not stained while always burning these creatures,

children.text: na lipyate tathā rājā daṇḍaṃ daṇḍyeṣu pātayan ||
children.translated_text: so the king is not stained while imposing punishment on those deserving punishment.

children.text: ājñā tejaḥ pārthivānāṃ sā ca vāci pratiṣṭhitā
children.translated_text: Command is the splendor of earthly rulers, and it is established in speech;

children.text: te yad brūyur asat sad vā sa dharmo vyavahāriṇām ||
children.translated_text: whatever they say, false or true, is <s>dharma</s> for litigants.

children.text: rājā nāma caraty eṣa bhūmau sākṣāt sahasradṛk
children.translated_text: This one called king moves upon the earth as the thousand-eyed god himself.

children.text: na tasyājñām atikramya saṃtiṣṭheran prajāḥ kvacit ||
children.translated_text: The subjects should never remain anywhere after transgressing his command.

children.text: rakṣādhikārād īśatvād bhūtānugrahadarśanāt
children.translated_text: Because of his authority to protect, his lordship, and the visible favor he shows to beings,

children.text: yad eva rājā kurute tat pramāṇam iti sthitiḥ ||
children.translated_text: whatever the king does is authoritative: such is the established rule.

children.text: nirguṇo 'pi yathā strīṇāṃ pūjya eva patiḥ sadā
children.translated_text: Just as even a husband without virtues is always worthy of honor for women,

children.text: prajānāṃ viguṇo 'py evaṃ pūjya eva narādhipaḥ ||
children.translated_text: so too a ruler, even if deficient, is still worthy of honor for his subjects.

children.text: tapaḥkrītāḥ prajā rājñā prabhur āsāṃ tato nṛpaḥ
children.translated_text: The subjects have been purchased by the king through austerity; therefore the king is their lord.

children.text: tatas tadvacasi stheyaṃ vārtā cāsāṃ tadāśrayā ||
children.translated_text: Therefore they must abide by his word, and their livelihood depends on him.

children.text: pañca rūpāṇi rājāno dhārayanty amitaujasaḥ
children.translated_text: Kings of immeasurable power bear five forms:

children.text: agner indrasya somasya yamasya dhanadasya ca ||
children.translated_text: those of <s>Agni</s>, <s>Indra</s>, <s>Soma</s>, <s>Yama</s>, and <s>Dhanada</s>.

children.text: kāraṇād animittaṃ vā yadā krodhavaśaṃ gataḥ
children.translated_text: When, for a reason or without cause, he has come under the sway of anger,

children.text: prajā dahati bhūpālas tadāgnir abhidhīyate ||
children.translated_text: and the protector of the earth burns his subjects, then he is called <s>Agni</s>.

children.text: yadā tejaḥ samālambya vijigīṣur udāyudhaḥ
children.translated_text: When, taking up his splendor, desirous of conquest and with weapon raised,

children.text: abhiyāti parān rājā tadendraḥ sa udāhṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the king marches against enemies, then he is declared to be <s>Indra</s>.

children.text: vigatakrodhasaṃtāpo hṛṣṭarūpo yadā nṛpaḥ
children.translated_text: When the king's fever of anger has passed and his appearance is cheerful,

children.text: prajānāṃ darśanaṃ yāti soma ity ucyate tadā ||
children.translated_text: and he goes to give audience to his subjects, then he is called <s>Soma</s>.

children.text: dharmāsanagataḥ śrīmān daṇḍaṃ dhatte yadā nṛpaḥ
children.translated_text: When the splendid king, seated on the seat of <s>dharma</s> (law), takes up the rod of punishment,

children.text: samaḥ sarveṣu bhūteṣu tadā vaivasvataḥ yamaḥ ||
children.translated_text: being equal toward all beings, then he is <s>Vaivasvata Yama</s>.

children.text: yadā tv arthiguruprājñabhṛtyādīn avanīpatiḥ
children.translated_text: But when the lord of the earth favors petitioners, elders, wise men, servants, and others

children.text: anugṛhṇāti dānena tadā sa dhanadaḥ smṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: with gifts, then he is remembered as <s>Dhanada</s>.

children.text: tasmāt taṃ nāvajānīyān nākrośen na viśeṣayet
children.translated_text: Therefore one should not disrespect him, abuse him, or censure him,

children.text: ājñāyāṃ cāsya tiṣṭheta mṛtyuḥ syāt tadvyatikramāt ||
children.translated_text: and one should stand within his command; death may come from transgressing it.

children.text: tasya vṛttiḥ prajārakṣā vṛddhaprājñopasevanam
children.translated_text: His function is the protection of his subjects, attendance upon elders and wise men,

children.text: darśanaṃ vyavahārāṇām ātmanaś cābhirakṣaṇam ||
children.translated_text: the hearing of legal disputes, and the protection of himself.

children.text: brāhmaṇān upaseveta nityaṃ rājā samāhitaḥ
children.translated_text: The king, composed in mind, should constantly attend upon Brahmins;

children.text: saṃyuktaṃ brāhmaṇaiḥ kṣatraṃ mūlaṃ lokābhirakṣaṇe ||
children.translated_text: royal power joined with Brahmins is the root of protecting the world.

children.text: brāhmaṇasyāparīhāro rājanyāsanam agrataḥ
children.translated_text: The privileges of a Brahmin are exemption from obstruction, a foremost seat before the prince,

children.text: prathamaṃ darśanaṃ prātaḥ sarvebhyaś cābhivādanam ||
children.translated_text: first audience in the morning, and salutation before all others.

children.text: agraṃ navebhyaḥ sasyebhyo mārgadānaṃ ca gacchataḥ
children.translated_text: He has the first portion from new crops, and the right of way while traveling,

children.text: bhaikṣahetoḥ parāgāre praveśas tv anivāritaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and unhindered entry into another's house for the sake of alms.

children.text: samitpuṣpodakādāneṣv asteyaṃ saparigrahāt
children.translated_text: In taking firewood, flowers, and water, there is no theft, even from property that has an owner;

children.text: anākṣepaḥ parebhyaś ca saṃbhāṣaś ca parastriyā ||
children.translated_text: nor should there be reproach from others, nor for conversation with another man's wife.

children.text: nadīṣv avetanas tāraḥ pūrvam uttaraṇaṃ tathā
children.translated_text: At rivers he has ferrying without fare, and likewise the first crossing;

children.text: tareṣv aśulkadānaṃ ca na ced vāṇijyam asya tat ||
children.translated_text: and at ferries he need not pay toll, unless that is his trade.

children.text: vartamāno 'dhvani śrānto gṛhṇann anivasan svayam
children.translated_text: A Brahmin who is traveling on a road, tired, and taking for himself without settling there,

children.text: brāhmaṇo nāparādhnoti dvāv ikṣū pañca mūlakān ||
children.translated_text: does not commit an offense by taking two sugarcanes and five radishes.

children.text: nābhiśastān na patitān na dviṣo na ca nāstikāt
children.translated_text: He should not take from one who is accused, from a fallen man, from an enemy, or from an atheist,

children.text: na sopadhān nānimittaṃ na dātāraṃ prapīḍya ca ||
children.translated_text: nor from one acting with deceit, nor without cause, nor by oppressing the giver.

children.text: arthānāṃ bhūribhāvāc ca deyatvācca mahātmanām
children.translated_text: Because wealth exists in abundance, and because the noble are worthy recipients,

children.text: śreyān pratigraho rājñāṃ anyeṣāṃ brāhmaṇād ṛte ||
children.translated_text: accepting gifts from kings is better than from others, apart from a Brahmin.

children.text: brāhmaṇaś caiva rājā ca dvāvapyetau dhṛtavratau
children.translated_text: A Brahmin and a king: both of these two keep firm vows,

children.text: naitayor antaraṃ kiṃcit prajādharmābhirakṣaṇāt ||
children.translated_text: and there is no difference at all between them, because they protect the <s>dharma</s> of the subjects.

children.text: dharmajñasya kṛtajñasya rakṣārthaṃ śāsato 'śucīn
children.translated_text: Of a king who knows <s>dharma</s>, remembers benefaction, and rules the impure for the sake of protection,

children.text: medhyam eva dhanaṃ prāhus tīkṣṇasyāpi mahīpateḥ ||
children.translated_text: they say that the wealth is pure, even if the lord of the earth is severe.

children.text: śucīnām aśucīnāṃ ca saṃnipāto yathāmbhasām
children.translated_text: Just as the meeting of pure and impure waters

children.text: samudre samatāṃ yāti tadvad rājño dhanāgamaḥ ||
children.translated_text: comes to sameness in the ocean, so too is the king's acquisition of wealth.

children.text: yathā cāgnau sthitaṃ dīpte śuddhim āyāti kāñcanam
children.translated_text: And just as gold placed in blazing fire comes to purification,

children.text: evam evāgamā sarve śuddhim āyānti rājasu ||
children.translated_text: so all acquisitions become purified among kings.

children.text: ya eva kaścit svadravyaṃ brāhmaṇebhyaḥ prayacchati
children.translated_text: Whoever gives his own property to Brahmins,

children.text: tad rājñāpy anumantavyam eṣa dharmaḥ sanātanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: that is to be approved even by the king; this is the eternal <s>dharma</s>.

children.text: anyaprakārād ucitād bhūmeḥ ṣaḍbhāgasaṃjñitāt
children.translated_text: That tax, in the proper form, is known as the sixth part of the land,

children.text: baliḥ sa tasya vihitaḥ prajāpālanavetanam ||
children.translated_text: and is prescribed as his wage for protecting the subjects.

children.text: śakyaṃ tat punar ādātuṃ yad abrāhmaṇasātkṛtam
children.translated_text: What has been made the property of a non-Brahmin can be taken back,

children.text: brāhmaṇāya tu yad dattaṃ na tasya haraṇaṃ punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: but what has been given to a Brahmin may not be taken away again.

children.text: dānam adhyayanaṃ yajñas tasya karma trilakṣaṇam
children.translated_text: Giving, study, and sacrifice are the three marks of his action;

children.text: yājanādhyāpane vṛttis tṛtīyas tu pratigrahaḥ ||
children.translated_text: his livelihood is officiating at sacrifice and teaching, while acceptance of gifts is the third.

children.text: svakarmaṇi dvijas tiṣṭhed vṛttim āhārayet kṛtām
children.translated_text: A twice-born man should remain in his own duty and bring in an earned livelihood;

children.text: nāsadbhyaḥ pratigṛhṇīyād varṇebhyo niyame 'sati ||
children.translated_text: he should not accept gifts from unworthy people or from the <s>varṇas</s> when there is no rule permitting it.

children.text: aśucir vacanād yasya śucir bhavati puruṣaḥ
children.translated_text: By whose utterance an impure man becomes pure,

children.text: śuciś caivāśuciḥ sadyaḥ kathaṃ rājā na daivatam ||
children.translated_text: and a pure man at once becomes impure: how is the king not a deity?

children.text: vidur ya eva devatvaṃ rājño hy amitatejasaḥ
children.translated_text: Those twice-born men who know the divinity of the king of immeasurable splendor

children.text: tasya te pratigṛhṇanto na lipyante dvijātayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: are not tainted when they accept gifts from him.

children.text: loke 'smin maṅgalāny aṣṭau brāhmaṇo gaur hutāśanaḥ
children.translated_text: In this world there are eight auspicious things: a Brahmin, a cow, fire,

children.text: hiraṇyaṃ sarpir āditya āpo rājā tathāṣṭamaḥ ||
children.translated_text: gold, ghee, the sun, waters, and the king as the eighth.

children.text: etāni satataṃ paśyen namasyed arcayec ca tān
children.translated_text: One should always look upon these, bow to them, and honor them,

children.text: pradakṣiṇaṃ ca kurvīta tathā hy āyur na hīyate ||
children.translated_text: and circumambulate them clockwise; thus one's life is not diminished.

children.text: Chapter 21
dvividhās taskarā jñeyāḥ paradravyāpahāriṇaḥ
children.translated_text: Thieves who steal another's property should be understood as twofold:

children.text: prakāśāś cāprakāśāś ca tān vidyād ātmavān nṛpaḥ ||
children.translated_text: open and concealed; the self-possessed king should know them.

children.text: prakāśavañcakās tatra kūṭamānatulāśritāḥ
children.translated_text: Among them, open deceivers are those who rely on false measures and weights,

children.text: utkoṭakāḥ sāhasikāḥ kitavāḥ paṇyayoṣitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: extortionists, violent robbers, gamblers, and courtesans,

children.text: pratirūpakarāś caiva maṅgaloddeśavṛttayaḥ
children.translated_text: as well as counterfeiters and those who make a living by proclaiming auspicious omens;

children.text: ity evamādayo jñeyāḥ prakāśalokavañcakāḥ ||
children.translated_text: such and others like them should be known as open deceivers of the people.

children.text: aprakāśāś ca vijñeyā bahirabhyantarāśritāḥ
children.translated_text: Concealed thieves should be known as those who operate from outside and within;

children.text: suptān pramattāṃś ca narā muṣṇanty ākramya caiva te ||
children.translated_text: they rob men who are asleep or careless, and they also attack them.

children.text: deśagrāmagṛhaghnāś ca pathighnā granthimocakāḥ
children.translated_text: Raiders of regions, villages, and houses, highwaymen, and cut-purses,

children.text: ity evamādayo jñeyā aprakāśāś ca taskarāḥ ||
children.translated_text: such and others like them should be known as concealed thieves.

children.text: tān viditvā sukuśalaiś cārais tatkarmakāribhiḥ
children.translated_text: After identifying them through very skilled spies engaged in that work,

children.text: anusṛtya gṛhītavyā gūḍhapraṇihitair naraiḥ ||
children.translated_text: they should be followed and seized by men secretly planted there.

children.text: sabhāprapāpūpaśālāveśamadyānnavikrayāḥ
children.translated_text: Assembly halls, water stations, cake shops, lodgings, and sellers of liquor and food,

children.text: catuṣpathāś caityavṛkṣāḥ samājāḥ prekṣaṇāni ca ||
children.translated_text: crossroads, sacred trees, public gatherings, and spectacles,

children.text: śūnyāgārāṇy araṇyāni devatāyatanāni ca
children.translated_text: empty houses, forests, and temples

children.text: cārair vineyāny etāni cauragrahaṇatatparaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: are to be watched by spies intent on catching thieves.

children.text: tathaivānye praṇihitāḥ śraddheyāś citravādinaḥ
children.translated_text: Likewise other planted agents, credible and skilled in varied speech,

children.text: carā hy utsāhayeyus tāṃs taskarān pūrvataskarāḥ ||
children.translated_text: former thieves serving as spies, should indeed incite those robbers.

children.text: annapānasamādānaiḥ samājotsavadarśanaiḥ
children.translated_text: With gifts of food and drink, with visits to gatherings and festivals,

children.text: tathā cauryāpadeśaiś ca kuryus teṣāṃ samāgamam ||
children.translated_text: and also with proposals of theft, they should arrange meetings with them.

children.text: ye tatra nopasarpanti sṛtāḥ praṇihitā api
children.translated_text: Those who do not approach there, even when enticed by planted agents,

children.text: te 'bhisārya gṛhītavyāḥ saputrapaśubāndhavāḥ ||
children.translated_text: should be gone after and arrested, together with their sons, cattle, and relatives.

children.text: yāṃs tatra caurān gṛhṇīyāt tān vitāḍya viḍambya ca
children.translated_text: The thieves whom he captures there should be beaten and publicly disgraced,

children.text: avaghuṣya ca sarvatra vadhyāś citravadhena te ||
children.translated_text: proclaimed everywhere, and then executed by various modes of execution.

children.text: na tv ahoḍhānvitāś caurā rājñā vadhyā hyanāgamāḥ
children.translated_text: But thieves not caught with stolen goods are not to be killed by the king when there is no proof;

children.text: sahoḍhān sopakaraṇān kṣipraṃ caurān praśāsayet ||
children.translated_text: he should quickly punish thieves caught with the stolen goods and their implements.

children.text: svadeśaghātino ye syus tathā panthāvarodhinaḥ
children.translated_text: Those who damage their own country, and likewise those who block the roads,

children.text: teṣāṃ sarvasvam ādāya bhūyo nindāṃ prakalpayet ||
children.translated_text: should have all their property confiscated, and further public disgrace should be imposed.

children.text: ahoḍhān vimṛśec caurān gṛhītān pariśaṅkayā
children.translated_text: Thieves arrested on suspicion, but not with stolen goods, should be examined;

children.text: bhayopadhābhiś citrābhir brūyus tathā yathākṛtam ||
children.translated_text: through many kinds of terrifying stratagems they should tell what was done.

children.text: deśaṃ kālaṃ diśaṃ jātiṃ nāma vā saṃpratiśrayam
children.translated_text: The place, time, direction, caste, name, or place of resort,

children.text: kṛtyaṃ karmakarā vā syuḥ praṣṭavyās te vinigrahe ||
children.translated_text: the intended act, and whether there were accomplices: they should be questioned about these when detained.

children.text: varṇasvarākārabhedāt sasaṃdigdhanivedanāt
children.translated_text: From differences in complexion, voice, or appearance, from a doubtful statement,

children.text: adeśakāladṛṣṭatvād vāsasyāpy aviśodhanāt ||
children.translated_text: from having been seen in the wrong place or time, or from failure to clear up even one's clothing,

children.text: asadvyayāt pūrvacauryād asatsaṃsargakāraṇāt
children.translated_text: from improper expenditure, previous theft, or association with bad people,

children.text: leśair apy avagantavyā na hoḍhenaiva kevalam ||
children.translated_text: they may be recognized even by slight signs, not only by stolen goods.

children.text: dasyuvṛtte yadi nare śaṅkā syāt taskare 'pi vā
children.translated_text: If suspicion falls on a man living by banditry, or on a thief,

children.text: yadi spṛśyeta leśena kāryaḥ syācchapathaḥ tataḥ ||
children.translated_text: and he is touched by even slight evidence, then an oath should be required.

children.text: caurāṇāṃ bhaktadā ye syus tathāgnyudakadāyakāḥ
children.translated_text: Those who give food to thieves, and likewise those who give fire or water,

children.text: āvāsadā deśikadās tathaivottaradāyakāḥ ||
children.translated_text: those who give lodging, act as guides, or supply replies,

children.text: kretāraś caiva bhāṇḍānāṃ pratigrāhiṇa eva ca
children.translated_text: and buyers of the goods and receivers of them,

children.text: samadaṇḍāḥ smṛtā hy ete ye ca pracchādayanti tān ||
children.translated_text: as well as those who conceal the thieves, are remembered as deserving the same penalty.

children.text: rāṣṭreṣu rāṣṭrādhikṛtāḥ sāmantāś caiva coditāḥ
children.translated_text: District officials in the provinces, and also neighboring chiefs, once they have been notified,

children.text: abhyāghāteṣu madhyasthā yathā caurās tathaiva te ||
children.translated_text: if they remain neutral during attacks, are just like thieves.

children.text: gocare yasya muṣyeta tena caurāḥ prayatnataḥ
children.translated_text: In whose range anything is stolen, by him the thieves must be diligently sought;

children.text: mṛgyā dāpyo 'nyathā moṣaṃ padaṃ yadi na nirgatam ||
children.translated_text: otherwise he must be made to pay for the theft, if the trail has not gone out.

children.text: nirgate tu pade tasmin naṣṭe 'nyatra nipātite
children.translated_text: But if the trail has gone out, is lost, or falls into another territory,

children.text: sāmantān mārgapālāṃś ca dikpālāṃś caiva dāpayet ||
children.translated_text: the neighboring chiefs, road-guards, and boundary-guards should be made to pay.

children.text: gṛhe vai muṣite rājā cauragrāhāṃs tu dāpayet
children.translated_text: When a house has been robbed, the king should make the thief-catchers pay,

children.text: ārakṣakān rāṣṭrikāṃś ca yadi cauro na labhyate ||
children.translated_text: and the guards and district officers too, if the thief is not found.

children.text: yadi vā dāpyamānānāṃ tasmin moṣe tu saṃśayaḥ
children.translated_text: But if there is doubt about that theft while they are being made to pay,

children.text: muṣitaḥ śapathaṃ śāpyo moṣe vaiśodhyakāraṇāt ||
children.translated_text: the robbed man should be made to swear an oath, to establish the proof of the theft.

children.text: acaure dāpite moṣaṃ cauryavaiśodhyakāraṇāt
children.translated_text: When someone who is not the thief has been made to pay for the theft in order to establish it,

children.text: caure labdhe labheyus te dviguṇaṃ pratipāditāḥ ||
children.translated_text: once the thief is found, those who were made to pay should receive double in return.

children.text: caurahṛtaṃ prayatnena sarūpaṃ pratipādayet
children.translated_text: He should carefully restore the property stolen by thieves in its original form;

children.text: tadabhāve tu mūlyaṃ syād daṇḍaṃ dāpyaś ca tatsamam ||
children.translated_text: if that is not possible, its value is due, and he must be made to pay an equal fine.

children.text: kāṣṭhakāṇḍatṛṇādīnāṃ mṛnmayānāṃ tathaiva ca
children.translated_text: For wood, stalks, grass, and the like, and likewise for earthen objects,

children.text: veṇuvaiṇavabhāṇḍānāṃ vetrasnāyvasthicarmaṇām ||
children.translated_text: for bamboo and cane vessels, and for rattan, sinew, bone, and leather,

children.text: śākaharitamūlānāṃ haraṇe phalapuṣpayoḥ
children.translated_text: for vegetables, greens, roots, and for the taking of fruits and flowers,

children.text: gorasekṣuvikārāṇāṃ tathā lavaṇatailayoḥ ||
children.translated_text: for dairy products, sugarcane products, and likewise salt and oil,

children.text: pakvānnānāṃ kṛtānnānāṃ madyānām āmiṣasya ca
children.translated_text: for cooked foods, prepared foods, liquors, and meat,

children.text: sarveṣām alpamūlyānāṃ mūlyāt pañcaguṇo damaḥ ||
children.translated_text: for all things of small value, the fine is five times the value.

children.text: tulādharimameyānāṃ gaṇimānāṃ ca sarvaśaḥ
children.translated_text: For all things weighed on scales, measured by volume, or counted,

children.text: ebhyas tūtkṛṣṭamūlyānāṃ mūlyād daśaguṇo damaḥ ||
children.translated_text: when their value is higher than these, the fine is ten times the value.

children.text: dhānyaṃ daśabhyaḥ kumbhebhyo harato 'bhyadhikaṃ vadhaḥ
children.translated_text: For one stealing grain in excess of ten <s>kumbhas</s> (jars), death is prescribed;

children.text: nyūnaṃ tv ekādaśaguṇaṃ daṇḍaṃ dāpyo 'bravīn manuḥ ||
children.translated_text: for a lesser amount, he must be made to pay an elevenfold fine, <s>Manu</s> said.

children.text: suvarṇarajatādīnām uttamānāṃ ca vāsasām
children.translated_text: For gold, silver, and other such things, and for excellent garments,

children.text: ratnānāṃ caiva mukhyānāṃ śatād abhyadhikaṃ vadhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and for the chief jewels, theft above a hundred in value brings death.

children.text: puruṣaṃ harataḥ pātyo daṇḍa uttamasāhasaḥ
children.translated_text: For abducting a man, the penalty is the highest <s>sāhasa</s> (violent-offense) fine;

children.text: sarvasvaṃ strīṃ tu harataḥ kanyāṃ tu harato vadhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: for abducting a woman, all one's property; for abducting a maiden, death.

children.text: mahāpaśūn stenayato daṇḍa uttamasāhasaḥ
children.translated_text: For stealing large animals, the penalty is the highest <s>sāhasa</s> fine;

children.text: madhyamo madhyamapaśuṃ pūrvaḥ kṣudrapaśuṃ haran ||
children.translated_text: the middle fine applies to one taking a middle-sized animal, and the first to one taking a small animal.

children.text: caturviṃśāvaraḥ pūrvaḥ paraḥ ṣaṇṇavatir bhavet
children.translated_text: The first fine has twenty-four as its lower limit and ninety-six as its upper limit;

children.text: śatāni pañca tu paro madhyamo dviśatāvaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: the middle fine has five hundred as its upper limit and two hundred as its lower limit.

children.text: sahasraṃ tūttamo jñeyaḥ paraḥ pañcaśatāvaraḥ
children.translated_text: The highest fine should be known as one thousand, with five hundred as its lower limit;

children.text: trividhaḥ sāhaseṣv eva daṇḍaḥ proktaḥ svayaṃbhuvā ||
children.translated_text: the threefold fine in cases of <s>sāhasa</s> has been declared by <s>Svayaṃbhū</s> himself.

children.text: prathame granthibhedānām aṅgulyaṅguṣṭhayor vadhaḥ
children.translated_text: For knot-cutters on the first offense, the fingers and thumb are to be cut off;

children.text: dvitīye caiva taccheṣaṃ daṇḍaḥ pūrvaś ca sāhasaḥ ||
children.translated_text: on the second offense, the rest of the hand is to be cut off, and the first <s>sāhasa</s> fine imposed.

children.text: goṣu brāhmaṇasaṃsthāsu sthūrāyāś chedanaṃ bhavet
children.translated_text: In the case of cows belonging to <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, there should be cutting of the tendon;

children.text: dāsīṃ tu harato nityam ardhapādavikartanam ||
children.translated_text: and for one who steals a female slave, always the cutting off of half a foot.

children.text: yena yena viśeṣeṇa stenāṅgena viceṣṭate
children.translated_text: With whatever particular limb the thief acts,

children.text: tat tad evāsya chettavyaṃ tan manor anuśāsanam ||
children.translated_text: that very limb of his should be cut off; that is <s>Manu</s>'s instruction.

children.text: garīyasi garīyāṃsam agarīyasi vā punaḥ
children.translated_text: A heavier punishment should be imposed for a heavier theft, and again a lighter one for a lighter theft;

children.text: stene nipātayed daṇḍaṃ na yathā prathame tathā ||
children.translated_text: one should not impose the penalty on a thief in the same way as for a first offense.

children.text: daśa sthānāni daṇḍasya manuḥ svāyaṃbhuvo 'bravīt
children.translated_text: <s>Manu Svāyaṃbhuva</s> declared ten places for punishment.

children.text: triṣu varṇeṣu yāni syur brāhmaṇo rakṣitaḥ sadā ||
children.translated_text: Whatever punishments there may be for the three <s>varṇas</s>, the Brahmin is always protected.

children.text: upastham udaraṃ jihvā hastau pādau ca pañcamam
children.translated_text: The genitals, the belly, the tongue, the two hands, and the two feet as the fifth,

children.text: cakṣur nāsā ca karṇau ca dhanaṃ dehas tathaiva ca ||
children.translated_text: the eyes, the nose, the ears, property, and the body likewise:

children.text: aparādhaṃ parijñāya deśakālau ca tattvataḥ
children.translated_text: having ascertained the offense, and the place and time as they truly are,

children.text: sārānubandhāv ālokya daṇḍān etān prakalpayet ||
children.translated_text: and having considered its substance and consequences, he should prescribe these punishments.

children.text: na mitrakāraṇād rājñā vipulād vā dhanāgamāt
children.translated_text: A violent offender should not be released by the king on account of a friend,

children.text: utsraṣṭavyaḥ sāhasikas tyaktātmā manur abravīt ||
children.translated_text: or because of a great acquisition of wealth; such a man is reckless of himself, said <s>Manu</s>.

children.text: yāvān avadhyasya vadhe tāvān vadhyasya mokṣaṇe
children.translated_text: As much wrong belongs to killing one who must not be killed, so much belongs to releasing one who deserves death;

children.text: bhavaty adharmo nṛpater dharmas tu viniyacchataḥ ||
children.translated_text: but <s>dharma</s> belongs to the king when he restrains him properly.

children.text: na jātu brāhmaṇaṃ hanyāt sarvapāpeṣv api sthitam
children.translated_text: He should never kill a Brahmin, even one involved in every sin;

children.text: nirvāsaṃ kārayet kāmam iti dharmo vyavasthitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: he may have him exiled instead. This is the settled <s>dharma</s>.

children.text: sarvasvaṃ vā hared rājā caturthaṃ vāvaśeṣayet
children.translated_text: Or the king may confiscate all his property, or leave one fourth,

children.text: bhṛtyebhyo 'nusmaran dharmaṃ prājāpatyam iti sthitiḥ ||
children.translated_text: mindful of <s>dharma</s> toward his dependents; this is the rule called <s>prājāpatya</s>.

children.text: brāhmaṇasyāparādhe tu caturṣv aṅko vidhīyate
children.translated_text: For an offense by a Brahmin, branding is prescribed in four cases:

children.text: gurutalpe surāpāne steye brāhmaṇahiṃsane ||
children.translated_text: violating the teacher's bed, drinking liquor, theft, and harming a Brahmin.

children.text: gurutalpe bhagaḥ kāryaḥ surāpāne dhvajaḥ smṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: For violating the teacher's bed, a mark of a vulva is to be made; for drinking liquor, a banner is remembered;

children.text: steye tu śvapadaṃ kṛtvā śikhipittena kūṭayet ||
children.translated_text: for theft, after making the mark of a dog's foot, he should brand it with peacock bile.

children.text: viśirāḥ puruṣaḥ kāryo lalāṭe bhrūṇaghātinaḥ
children.translated_text: For the killer of an embryo, a headless man is to be made on the forehead,

children.text: asaṃbhāṣyaś ca kartavyas tan manor anuśāsanam ||
children.translated_text: and he is to be made one with whom no one should converse. That is <s>Manu</s>'s injunction.

children.text: rājā stenena gantavyo muktakeśena dhāvatā
children.translated_text: A thief should go to the king with loose hair, running,

children.text: ācakṣāṇena tatsteyam evaṃ kartāsmi śādhi mām ||
children.translated_text: declaring that theft: 'I have done this; punish me.'

children.text: anenā bhavati stenaḥ svakarmapratipādanāt
children.translated_text: By this, through the declaration of his own act, the thief becomes free of guilt;

children.text: rājānaṃ tat spṛśed ena utsṛjantaṃ sakilbiṣam ||
children.translated_text: that guilt would touch the king if he released him while he was still guilty.

children.text: rājabhir dhṛtadaṇḍās tu kṛtvā pāpāni mānavāḥ
children.translated_text: But men who have committed sins and have had punishment imposed by kings

children.text: nirmalāḥ svargam āyānti santaḥ sukṛtino yathā ||
children.translated_text: go stainless to heaven, like good men who have done meritorious acts.

children.text: śāsanād vā vimokṣād vā steno mucyate kilbiṣāt
children.translated_text: A thief is freed from guilt either by punishment or by release after judgment;

children.text: aśāsanāt tu tad rājā stenasyāpnoti kilbiṣam ||
children.translated_text: but if he is not punished, the king incurs that guilt of the thief.

children.text: gurur ātmavatāṃ śāstā śāstā rājā durātmanām
children.translated_text: The teacher is the chastiser of self-controlled men; the king is the chastiser of the wicked;

children.text: atha pracchannapāpānāṃ śāstā vaivasvato yamaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and for those whose sins are hidden, <s>Vaivasvata Yama</s> is the chastiser.

children.text: aṣṭāpādyaṃ tu śūdrasya steye bhavati kilbiṣam
children.translated_text: In theft, the guilt is eightfold for a Śūdra;

children.text: dvir aṣṭāpādyaṃ vaiśyasya dvātriṃśat kṣatriyasya tu ||
children.translated_text: it is twice eightfold for a Vaiśya, and thirty-twofold for a Kṣatriya.

children.text: brāhmaṇasya catuḥṣaṣṭīty evaṃ svāyaṃbhuvo 'bravīt
children.translated_text: For a Brahmin it is sixty-fourfold: so <s>Svāyambhuva</s> said;

children.text: tatrāpi ca viśeṣeṇa vidvatsv abhyadhikaṃ bhavet ||
children.translated_text: and even there, in particular, it should be greater for learned men.

children.text: śārīraś cārthadaṇḍaś ca daṇḍas tu dvividhaḥ smṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: Bodily punishment and monetary punishment: punishment is remembered as twofold;

children.text: śārīrā daśadhā proktā arthadaṇḍās tv anekadhā ||
children.translated_text: bodily punishments are declared to be tenfold, while monetary punishments are manyfold.

children.text: kākaṇyādis tv arthadaṇḍaḥ sarvasvāntas tathaiva ca
children.translated_text: Monetary punishment begins with a <s>kākaṇī</s> and extends as far as confiscation of all property;

children.text: śārīras tv avarodhādir jīvitāntas tathaiva ca ||
children.translated_text: bodily punishment begins with confinement and extends as far as taking life.

children.text: kākaṇyādis tu yo daṇḍaḥ sa tu māṣāparaḥ smṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: The fine that begins with a <s>kākaṇī</s> is remembered as having a <s>māṣa</s> as its upper limit;

children.text: māṣāvarādyo yaḥ proktaḥ kārṣāpaṇaparas tu saḥ ||
children.translated_text: the one said to begin from a <s>māṣa</s> has a <s>kārṣāpaṇa</s> as its upper limit.

children.text: kārṣāpaṇāparādyas tu catuḥkārṣāpaṇaḥ paraḥ
children.translated_text: The grade beginning with a <s>kārṣāpaṇa</s> has four <s>kārṣāpaṇas</s> as its upper limit;

children.text: dvyavaro 'ṣṭāparaś cānyas tryavaro dvādaśottaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: another has two as its lower limit and eight as its upper, and another has three as lower and twelve as upper.

children.text: kārṣāpaṇādyā ye proktāḥ sarve te syuś caturguṇāḥ
children.translated_text: All those that are said to begin with <s>kārṣāpaṇas</s> are to be fourfold;

children.text: evam anye tu vijñeyāḥ prāk ca te pūrvasāhasāt ||
children.translated_text: others should be understood in this way as well, up to the first <s>sāhasa</s> fine.

children.text: kārṣāpaṇo dakṣiṇasyāṃ diśi raupyaḥ pravartate
children.translated_text: In the southern region, the <s>kārṣāpaṇa</s> circulates as a silver coin;

children.text: paṇair nibaddhaḥ pūrvasyāṃ ṣoḍaśaiva paṇāḥ sa tu ||
children.translated_text: in the eastern region it is fixed by <s>paṇas</s>, and it is exactly sixteen <s>paṇas</s>.

children.text: māṣo viṃśatibhāgas tu jñeyaḥ kārṣāpaṇasya tu
children.translated_text: A <s>māṣa</s> should be known as a twentieth part of a <s>kārṣāpaṇa</s>;

children.text: kākaṇī tu caturbhāgo māṣasya ca paṇasya ca ||
children.translated_text: and a <s>kākaṇī</s> is a fourth part of both a <s>māṣa</s> and a <s>paṇa</s>.

children.text: pāñcanadyāḥ pradeśe tu saṃjñā yā vyāvahārikī
children.translated_text: In the region of <s>Pāñcanada</s>, the practical commercial designation that is used

children.text: kārṣāpaṇapramāṇaṃ tu nibaddham iha vai tayā ||
children.translated_text: is the one by which the measure of the <s>kārṣāpaṇa</s> is fixed here.

children.text: kārṣāpaṇo 'ṇḍikā jñeyāś catasras tās tu dhānakaḥ
children.translated_text: A <s>kārṣāpaṇa</s> should be known as an <s>aṇḍikā</s>; four of these are a <s>dhānaka</s>;

children.text: taddvādaśa suvarṇasya dīnāraś citrakaḥ smṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: twelve of those make a <s>suvarṇa</s>; the <s>dīnāra</s> is remembered as a <s>citraka</s>.

children.text: vārttāṃ trayīṃ cāpy atha daṇḍanītim rājānuvartet saṃtatāpramattaḥ
children.translated_text: The king, constantly alert, should adhere to <s>vārttā</s> (economic activity), the <s>trayī</s> (the three Vedas), and <s>daṇḍanīti</s> (the policy of punishment);

children.text: hanyād upāyair nipuṇair gṛhītān pure ca rāṣṭre nigṛhṇīyāt pāpān ||
children.translated_text: he should strike down, by skillful means, criminals who have been caught, and restrain wrongdoers in city and kingdom.

children.text: Chapter 22
yadā sākṣī na vidyate vivāde vadatāṃ nṛṇām
children.translated_text: When there is no witness in a dispute among men who are making claims,

children.text: tadā divyaiḥ parīkṣeta śapathaiś ca pṛthagvidhaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: then he should examine them by ordeals and by oaths of various kinds.

children.text: satyaṃ vāhanaśastrāṇi gobījarajatāni ca
children.translated_text: Truth, vehicles, weapons, cows, seed, and silver,

children.text: devatāpitṛpādāś ca dattāni sukṛtāni ca ||
children.translated_text: the feet of deities and ancestors, gifts, and meritorious acts are oath-objects.

children.text: mahāparādhe divyāni dāpayet tu mahīpatiḥ
children.translated_text: In a major offense, the lord of the earth should administer ordeals;

children.text: alpeṣu ca naraḥ śreṣṭhaḥ śapathaiḥ śāpayen naram ||
children.translated_text: but in minor matters the best of men should make a man swear by oaths.

children.text: ete hi śapathāḥ proktāḥ sukarāḥ svalpasaṃśaye
children.translated_text: These oaths are said to be easy when suspicion is slight;

children.text: sāhaseṣv abhiśāpe ca vidhir divyaḥ prakīrtitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: in violent offenses and formal accusations, the rule of the <s>divya</s> (ordeal) is prescribed.

children.text: saṃdigdhe 'rthe 'bhiyuktānāṃ pracchanneṣu viśeṣataḥ
children.translated_text: In a doubtful matter involving accused persons, especially in hidden cases,

children.text: divyaḥ pañcavidho jñeya ity āha bhagavān manuḥ ||
children.translated_text: the ordeal should be known as fivefold, says the blessed <s>Manu</s>.

children.text: dhaṭo 'gnir udakaṃ caiva viṣaṃ kośaś ca pañcamaḥ
children.translated_text: The balance, fire, water, poison, and the <s>kośa</s> as the fifth:

children.text: uktāny etāni divyāni dūṣitānāṃ viśodhane ||
children.translated_text: these ordeals are stated for the purification of those who are tainted by accusation.

children.text: saṃdigdheṣv abhiyuktānāṃ viśuddhyarthaṃ mahātmanā
children.translated_text: For the sake of purification of accused persons in doubtful cases,

children.text: nāradena punaḥ proktāḥ satyānṛtavibhāvanāḥ
children.translated_text: the great-souled <s>Nārada</s> again taught the determinations of truth and falsehood.

children.text: vādino 'numatenainaṃ kārayen nānyathā budhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: A wise man should have this performed with the litigant's consent, and not otherwise.

children.text: caturhastau tulāpādāv ucchrayeṇa prakīrtitau
children.translated_text: The two supports of the balance are prescribed as four hastas in height;

children.text: ṣaḍḍhastaṃ tu tayor dṛṣṭaṃ pramāṇaṃ parimāṇataḥ ||
children.translated_text: their measured span is seen as six hastas.

children.text: pādayor antaraṃ hastaṃ bhaved adhyardham eva ca
children.translated_text: The distance between the two feet should be exactly one and a half hastas;

children.text: śikyadvayaṃ samāsajya dhaṭe karkaṭake dṛḍhe ||
children.translated_text: one should attach two slings to the firm hook of the balance.

children.text: tulayitvā naraṃ pūrvaṃ cihnaṃ kuryād dhaṭasya tu
children.translated_text: Having first weighed the man, one should make a mark on the balance;

children.text: kakṣāsthānena taṃ tulyam avatārya tato dhaṭāt ||
children.translated_text: then, when it is equal at the armpit position, one should lower him from the balance.

children.text: samayaiḥ parigṛhyainaṃ punar āropayen naraḥ
children.translated_text: Having taken him under the prescribed conditions, one should place the man on it again.

children.text: tasmin evaṃ kṛte sā cet kakṣe sthāpya suniścalā ||
children.translated_text: When this has been done, if the balance, once set in position, is completely steady,

children.text: tulito yadi vardheta śuddhaḥ syān nātre saṃśayaḥ
children.translated_text: and if, when weighed, it rises, he is pure; there is no doubt about this.

children.text: samo vā hīyamāno vā na viśuddho bhaven naraḥ ||
children.translated_text: But if the man is equal in weight or sinks lower, he is not purified.

children.text: dharmaparyāyavacanair dhaṭa ity abhidhīyase
children.translated_text: O balance, you are named by words that are synonyms of <s>dharma</s> (justice).

children.text: tvaṃ vetsi sarvabhūtānāṃ pāpāni sukṛtāni ca
children.translated_text: You know the sins and good deeds of all beings.

children.text: tvam eva dhaṭa jānīṣe na vidur yāni mānuṣāḥ ||
children.translated_text: You alone, O balance, know the things that human beings do not know.

children.text: vyavahārābhiśasto 'yaṃ mānuṣas tulyate tathā
children.translated_text: This man, accused in a lawsuit, is being weighed in this way.

children.text: tad eva saṃśayāpannaṃ dharmatas trātum arhasi ||
children.translated_text: Therefore you ought to protect him, who has fallen into uncertainty, according to <s>dharma</s>.

children.text: ata ūrdhvaṃ pravakṣyāmi lohasya vidhim uttamam
children.translated_text: After this I shall declare the excellent rule for the iron ordeal.

children.text: dvātriṃśadaṅgulāni tu maṇḍalān maṇḍalāntaram ||
children.translated_text: There should be thirty-two fingerbreadths from one circle to the next.

children.text: aṣṭābhir maṇḍalair evam aṅgulānāṃ śatadvayam
children.translated_text: Thus, with eight circles, the measure in fingerbreadths

children.text: caturviṃśat samākhyātaṃ saṃkhyātattvārthadarśibhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: is declared by those who discern the truth of numbers to be two hundred and twenty-four.

children.text: kalpitair maṇḍalair evam uṣitasya śucer api
children.translated_text: When the circles have been arranged in this way, for one who has observed the rite and is pure,

children.text: saptāśvatthasya pattrāṇi sūtreṇāveṣṭya hastayoḥ ||
children.translated_text: one should wrap seven leaves of the <s>aśvattha</s> tree around his hands with thread.

children.text: vidadhyāt taptalohasya pañcāśatpalam saṃmitam
children.translated_text: One should prepare a ball of heated iron measuring fifty <s>palas</s> (weights).

children.text: hastābhyāṃ piṇḍam ādāya śanaiḥ saptapadaṃ vrajet ||
children.translated_text: Taking the ball in both hands, he should slowly walk seven steps.

children.text: na maṇḍalam atikrāmen nāpy arvāk pādayet padam
children.translated_text: He must not overstep a circle, nor place his foot short of it.

children.text: na ca pātayetāprāptaḥ yāvadbhūmiḥ prakalpitā ||
children.translated_text: Nor should he drop it before he reaches the ground that has been marked out.

children.text: tīrtvānena vidhānena maṇḍalāni samāhitaḥ
children.translated_text: Having crossed the circles by this procedure, composed and attentive,

children.text: adagdhaḥ sarvato yas tu sa viśuddho bhaven naraḥ ||
children.translated_text: the man who is unburned in every respect is purified.

children.text: bhayād vā pātayate yas tv adagdho yo vibhāvyate
children.translated_text: But if he drops it from fear, though he is seen to be unburned,

children.text: punas taṃ hārayel lohaṃ sthitir eṣā purātanī
children.translated_text: one should have him carry the iron again; this is the ancient rule.

children.text: anena vidhinā kāryo hutāśasamayaḥ smṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: By this procedure the fire ordeal is remembered as one to be performed.

children.text: tvam agne sarvabhūtānām antaścarasi sākṣivat
children.translated_text: O <s>Agni</s>, you move within all beings like a witness.

children.text: sukṛtaṃ duṣkṛtaṃ lokena ajñātaṃ vidyate tvayā ||
children.translated_text: Good and bad deeds, unknown to the world, are known by you.

children.text: pracchannāni manuṣyāṇāṃ pāpāni sukṛtāni ca
children.translated_text: The hidden sins and good deeds of human beings,

children.text: yathāvad eva jānīṣe na vidur yāni mānuṣāḥ ||
children.translated_text: which mortals do not know, you know exactly as they are.

children.text: vyavahārābhiśasto 'yaṃ puruṣaḥ śuddhim icchati
children.translated_text: This man, accused in litigation, desires purification.

children.text: tad enaṃ saṃśayāpannaṃ dharmatas trātum arhasi ||
children.translated_text: Therefore you ought to protect him, who has fallen into uncertainty, according to <s>dharma</s>.

children.text: ataḥ paraṃ pravakṣyāmi toyasya vidhim uttamam
children.translated_text: Next I shall declare the excellent rule for the water ordeal.

children.text: nātikrūreṇa dhanuṣā prerayet sāyakatrayam ||
children.translated_text: One should shoot three arrows with a bow that is not too harsh in strength.

children.text: madhyamas tu śaro grāhyaḥ puruṣeṇa yavīyasā
children.translated_text: The middle arrow should be fetched by a younger man.

children.text: pratyānītasya tasyātha sa viśuddho bhaven naraḥ ||
children.translated_text: When that arrow has been brought back, the man is then purified.

children.text: anyathā na viśuddhaḥ syād ekāṅgam api darśayet
children.translated_text: Otherwise he is not purified, if he shows even a single limb,

children.text: sthānād anyatra vā gacched yasmin pūrvaṃ niveśitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: or if he moves from the place where he was first set.

children.text: striyas tu na balāt kāryā na pumān api durbalaḥ
children.translated_text: Women should not be compelled by force, nor should a weak man.

children.text: bhīrutvād yoṣito mṛtyuḥ kṛśasyāpi balāt kuryāt
children.translated_text: Through timidity a woman may die, and force may kill even a frail man;

children.text: sahasā prāpnuyāt sarvāṃs tasmād etān na majjayet ||
children.translated_text: death may suddenly overtake all such persons; therefore one should not immerse them.

children.text: toyamadhye manuṣyasya gṛhītvorū susaṃyataḥ ||
children.translated_text: In the midst of the water, the man should be well restrained after his thighs have been grasped.

children.text: satyānṛtavibhāgasya toyāgnī spaṣṭakṛttamau
children.translated_text: Water and fire are the clearest makers of the division between truth and falsehood.

children.text: yataś cāgnir abhūd asmāt tatas toyaṃ viśiṣyate ||
children.translated_text: And because fire arose from water, water is therefore distinguished as superior.

children.text: kriyate dharmatattvajñair dūṣitānāṃ viśodhanam
children.translated_text: By those who know the truth of <s>dharma</s>, purification is performed for those who have been tainted.

children.text: tasmāt satyena bhagavañ jaleśa trātum arhasi ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, by truth, O blessed lord of waters, you ought to protect him.

children.text: ataḥ paraṃ pravakṣyāmi viṣasya vidhim uttamam
children.translated_text: Next I shall declare the excellent rule for the poison ordeal.

children.text: tulayitvā viṣaṃ pūrvaṃ deyam etaddhimāgame ||
children.translated_text: After the poison has first been weighed, it should be given at the coming of winter.

children.text: na pūrvāhṇe na madhyāhne na saṃdhyāyāṃ tu dharmavit
children.translated_text: A knower of <s>dharma</s> should not give it in the forenoon, at midday, or at twilight,

children.text: śaradgrīṣmavasanteṣu varṣāsu ca na dāpayet ||
children.translated_text: nor should he have it given in autumn, summer, spring, or the rainy season.

children.text: bhagnaṃ ca dāritaṃ caiva dhūpitaṃ miśritaṃ tathā
children.translated_text: Poison that is broken, split, fumigated, or mixed,

children.text: kālakūṭam alambuṃ ca viṣaṃ yatnena varjayet ||
children.translated_text: as well as <s>Kālakūṭa</s> and <s>Alambu</s> poison, should be carefully avoided.

children.text: śārṅgahaimavataṃ śastaṃ gandhavarṇarasānvitam
children.translated_text: The <s>Śārṅga</s> or <s>Haimavata</s> variety is approved, if endowed with smell, color, and taste.

children.text: mahādoṣavate deyaṃ rājñā tattvabubhutsayā ||
children.translated_text: It should be given by the king to one charged with a grave fault, when he wishes to know the truth.

children.text: na bālāturavṛddheṣu naiva svalpāparādhiṣu
children.translated_text: It should not be given to children, the sick, or the aged, nor to those guilty of a slight offense.

children.text: viṣasya tu yavān sapta dadyācchodhye ghṛtaplutān ||
children.translated_text: For the person to be purified, he should give seven barley-grains of poison, soaked in ghee.

children.text: viṣasya palaṣaḍbhāgād bhāgo viṃśatimas tu yaḥ
children.translated_text: Of poison, the portion that is the twentieth part of a sixth of a <s>pala</s>,

children.text: tam aṣṭabhāgahīnaṃ tu śodhye dadyād ghṛtaplutam ||
children.translated_text: diminished by one eighth, should be given to the person to be purified, soaked in ghee.

children.text: yathoktena vidhānena viprān spṛṣṭvānumoditaḥ
children.translated_text: According to the prescribed procedure, after touching the Brahmins and being approved,

children.text: sopavāsaś ca khādeta devabrāhmaṇasaṃnidhau ||
children.translated_text: he should eat it while fasting, in the presence of the gods and Brahmins.

children.text: viṣaṃ vegaklamāpetaṃ sukhena yadi jīryate
children.translated_text: If the poison is digested easily, without violent reaction or exhaustion,

children.text: viśuddham iti taṃ jñātvā rājā satkṛtya mokṣayet ||
children.translated_text: the king, knowing him to be purified, should honor him and release him.

children.text: tvaṃ viṣa brahmaṇaḥ putraḥ satyadharmaratau sthitaḥ
children.translated_text: O poison, you are the son of <s>Brahmā</s>, established in devotion to truth and <s>dharma</s>.

children.text: śodhayainaṃ naraṃ pāpāt satyenāsyāmṛtībhava ||
children.translated_text: Cleanse this man from sin; through truth become nectar for him.

children.text: ataḥ paraṃ pravakṣyāmi kośasya vidhim uttamam ||
children.translated_text: Next I shall declare the excellent rule for the <s>kośa</s> (sacred-water ordeal).

children.text: pūrvāhṇe sopavāsasya snātasyārdrapaṭasya ca
children.translated_text: In the forenoon, for one who has fasted, bathed, and is wearing wet cloth,

children.text: saśūkasyāvyasaninaḥ kośapānaṃ vidhīyate ||
children.translated_text: and who bears the prescribed <s>śūka</s> and is free from calamity, drinking the <s>kośa</s> is enjoined.

children.text: yadbhaktaḥ so 'bhiyuktaḥ syāt taddaivatyaṃ tu pāyayet
children.translated_text: Whatever deity the accused is devoted to, one should make him drink water belonging to that deity.

children.text: saptāhād yasya dṛśyate dvisaptāhena vā punaḥ
children.translated_text: If, after seven days, or again within two weeks,

children.text: pratyātmikaṃ tu yatkiṃcit saiva tasya vibhāvanā ||
children.translated_text: any personal affliction is seen in him, that itself is the evidence in his case.

children.text: dvisaptāhāt paraṃ yasya mahad vā vaikṛtaṃ bhavet
children.translated_text: But if after two weeks some great deformity or disorder occurs to him,

children.text: nābhiyojyaḥ sa viduṣāṃ kṛtakālavyatikramāt ||
children.translated_text: he should not be prosecuted by the learned, since the appointed time has passed.

children.text: mahāparādhe nirdharme kṛtaghne klībakutsite
children.translated_text: In a case of great offense, or for an unrighteous man, an ingrate, an impotent man, or a despised person,

children.text: nāstikavrātyadāseṣu kośapānaṃ vivarjayet ||
children.translated_text: and for atheists, <s>vrātyas</s> (outcastes), and slaves, one should avoid the <s>kośa</s>-drinking ordeal.

children.text: yathoktena prakāreṇa pañca divyāni dharmavit
children.translated_text: In the manner stated, the king who knows <s>dharma</s> should administer the five ordeals

children.text: dadyād rājābhiyuktānāṃ pretya ceha ca nandati ||
children.translated_text: to accused persons; he rejoices both after death and here in this world.

children.text: na viṣaṃ brāhmaṇe dadyān na lohaṃ kṣatriyo haret
children.translated_text: One should not give poison to a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, and a <s>Kṣatriya</s> should not carry the iron.

children.text: na nimajjyāpsu vaiśyaś ca śūdraḥ kośaṃ na pāyayet ||
children.translated_text: A <s>Vaiśya</s> should not be immersed in water, and a <s>Śūdra</s> should not be made to drink the <s>kośa</s> (sacred draught ordeal).

children.text: varṣāsu na viṣaṃ dadyāt hemante nāpsu majjayet
children.translated_text: In the rainy season one should not administer poison; in winter one should not immerse someone in water.

children.text: na lohaṃ hārayed grīṣme na kośaṃ pāyayen niśi ||
children.translated_text: In summer one should not make someone carry the hot iron, and one should not make someone drink the <s>kośa</s> at night.
